- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qrb06p1", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Stage 3 (2030\u20132032): Currency and Sovereign Stress", "created": 1780965790955, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1825/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qrbq562", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Cash and bonds lose purchasing power slowly but surely.", "created": 1780965790954, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1826/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qrb9p3a", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Hard assets (stocks, commodities, real estate, Bitcoin, gold) outperform.", "created": 1780965790953, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1827/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qrbul67", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "\"Financial repression\" deepens: Real interest rates stay below inflation on purpose.", "created": 1780965790951, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1828/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qrbc54r", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Inflation will be cyclical but trending higher \u2014 sticky above 3\u20134%, with spikes to 6\u20138%.", "created": 1780965790950, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1829/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qrbhlkp", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Yield curve control (YCC) likely reintroduced openly \u2014 cap long-term rates.", "created": 1780965790949, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1830/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qrbw2i4", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Central banks are increasingly forced to finance deficits quietly.", "created": 1780965790948, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1831/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qrbx4wm", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Government deficits explode (military, social programs, stimulus).", "created": 1780965790947, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1832/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qrbebl7", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Stage 2 (2026\u20132029): Rising Fiscal Dominance and Inflation Surges", "created": 1780965790946, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1833/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qrbm8sa", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Sell strength when liquidity peaks.", "created": 1780965790945, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1834/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qrak870", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Stage 1 (Now\u20132026): Volatile Liquidity Waves", "created": 1780965790937, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1835/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qra3jwk", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "\ud83d\udcc5 Timeline: What Likely Happens 2025\u20132035 Under the \"Post-2019\" Financial Regime", "created": 1780965790936, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1836/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qraye45", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Bottom line:September 2019 quietly marked the death of \"normal\" financial markets \u2014We entered the era of perpetual Fed intervention, stealth debt monetization, hidden inflation, and liquidity-driven asset cycles.", "created": 1780965790933, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1837/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qra89m9", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Tightening without systemic risk", "created": 1780965790929, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1838/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qraygyg", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Belief in independent monetary policy", "created": 1780965790927, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1839/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qrasxlv", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Fed believed in shrinking balance sheet", "created": 1780965790925, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1840/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qra3ey4", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Crypto, meme stocks, speculative assets \u2014 all benefited enormously from this new forever liquidity environment post-2019.", "created": 1780965790922, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1841/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qras7d3", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Since September 2019, we are living in a world where:", "created": 1780965790917, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1842/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qraxf28", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "\ud83e\udde0 4. Why It Matters for Markets and Assets Today", "created": 1780965790916, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1843/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qrabce7", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Fiscal dominance (government spending financed by central banks) was inevitable.", "created": 1780965790915, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1844/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qra9myz", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "The global dollar system had already lost the ability to handle normal liquidity tightening.", "created": 1780965790914, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1845/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qraf05b", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "COVID didn\u2019t cause the monetary shift \u2014 it merely accelerated a process that started with the repo crisis.", "created": 1780965790913, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1846/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qracrzw", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Many macro experts (like Luke Gromen, Jeff Snider, Lyn Alden) argue:", "created": 1780965790912, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1847/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qran30q", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "When COVID hit in early 2020, the Fed massively expanded its balance sheet again \u2014 but the foundation had already been laid in late 2019.", "created": 1780965790911, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1848/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qra9bjy", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "\ud83c\udf0e 3. COVID Just Accelerated What September 2019 Started", "created": 1780965790910, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1849/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qrap7n0", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "\ud83d\udc49 Meaning: The new regime is QE without end, low rates, and hidden inflation taxation on savers.", "created": 1780965790909, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1850/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qra44pk", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "This is called \"financial repression\" \u2014 keeping interest rates artificially low relative to inflation to slowly inflate away debt.", "created": 1780965790908, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1851/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qradsj8", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Finance massive government deficits silently", "created": 1780965790907, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1852/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qraghso", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Prevent bond market seizures", "created": 1780965790906, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1853/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qras987", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Keep repo and dollar funding markets stable", "created": 1780965790905, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1854/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qrazf0z", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "After September 2019, central banks tacitly accepted that permanent liquidity support was now a feature, not a bug.", "created": 1780965790903, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1855/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qrajt3z", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "\ud83d\udc49 Meaning: Central banks realized that shrinking balance sheets breaks the plumbing. They can\u2019t shrink anymore without crises.", "created": 1780965790901, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1856/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qradjtx", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Fact: In October 2019, the Fed announced it would buy $60 billion/month of Treasury bills \u2014 injecting permanent liquidity into the system.", "created": 1780965790900, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1857/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qraxkbg", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "But the repo market seizure forced the Fed to immediately halt QT and start expanding the balance sheet again (even though they refused to call it QE).", "created": 1780965790899, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1858/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qrafaky", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "The goal was to exit from crisis-era support (QE1, QE2, QE3) and return to pre-2008 financial norms.", "created": 1780965790898, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1859/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qrac7rv", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Before September 2019, the Fed was trying to \"normalize\" \u2014 slowly raise interest rates and shrink its $4.5 trillion balance sheet (\"quantitative tightening\" or QT).", "created": 1780965790897, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1860/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qramcbr", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "\ud83d\udcc9 1. The End of \"Balance Sheet Shrinkage\" Dreams", "created": 1780965790896, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1861/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qraedvj", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "It also forced the Fed to abandon quantitative tightening, restart balance sheet expansion, and set the stage for the even bigger interventions of 2020.", "created": 1780965790893, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1862/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qram9cs", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "It exposed that even small shocks could create a full-blown liquidity crisis without immediate Fed intervention.", "created": 1780965790892, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1863/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qra32kl", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "The repo spike was a stress fracture \u2014 a preview of how fragile the global dollar funding system had become.", "created": 1780965790891, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1864/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qrakrse", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Fed shrank liquidity too much, misreading post-crisis reserve needs", "created": 1780965790890, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1865/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qra2idh", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "repo-funded bets blew up, needing emergency liquidity", "created": 1780965790888, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1866/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qrayjys", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Hedge fund leveraged trades", "created": 1780965790887, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1867/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qrabwch", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "desperate for U.S. dollars, straining dollar funding markets", "created": 1780965790886, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1868/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qral0x5", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Deutsche Bank & European banks", "created": 1780965790885, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1869/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qrajr9u", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "due to liquidity regulations, draining repo liquidity", "created": 1780965790884, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1870/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qra6x3v", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "\ud83d\udca5 Summary of the Deeper Causes:", "created": 1780965790882, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1871/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qra93ve", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "\ud83d\udc49 Result: Cross-border demand for dollars exploded, but U.S. banks didn\u2019t meet that demand.", "created": 1780965790871, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1872/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qrac6tz", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "When liquidity tightened, they were squeezed hard, scrambling for cash at almost any price.", "created": 1780965790870, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1873/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qraejrm", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "It\u2019s suspected that Deutsche Bank and other European banks (Credit Suisse, etc.) were desperate for dollars.", "created": 1780965790868, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1874/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr9am0o", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Around the same time, Deutsche Bank (which was in severe trouble) was rapidly unwinding its investment bank operations.", "created": 1780965790866, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1875/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr9hrg2", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "\ud83d\udc49 Result: A lot of \"potential\" liquidity existed but was locked \u2014 causing repo rates to spike.", "created": 1780965790864, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1876/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr9lak0", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "In fact, JPMorgan alone had about $130 billion in reserves \u2014 but withheld about $60\u201370 billion from the market.", "created": 1780965790863, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1877/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr9hq6v", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Why? Because of strict liquidity regulations (like the Liquidity Coverage Ratio, LCR) \u2014 JPMorgan calculated it was safer to keep reserves rather than lend and risk falling below regulatory thresholds.", "created": 1780965790862, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1878/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr9k06v", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "But instead of lending those reserves into the repo market, JPMorgan chose to hoard them.", "created": 1780965790861, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1879/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr9xdhl", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "JPMorgan Chase, the largest U.S. bank, was sitting on a huge amount of reserves at the Fed.", "created": 1780965790860, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1880/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr935q1", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Excellent \u2014 here\u2019s the deeper layer of what likely really happened in the September 2019 financial plumbing crisis:", "created": 1780965790858, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1881/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr94hwk", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Summary:In September 2019, the repo market broke because banks didn't have enough cash reserves, regulations discouraged lending, and the Fed had shrunk liquidity too far. The Fed had to inject emergency liquidity, exposing hidden fragilities that would worsen during the 2020 COVID-19 crash.", "created": 1780965790856, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1882/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr9an6v", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Some analysts view this event as the first clear sign that the post-2008 financial system was broken and over-reliant on Fed intervention.", "created": 1780965790855, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1883/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr9xval", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "It showed that the system was fragile even before COVID-19 \u2014 there were hidden cracks in the financial plumbing.", "created": 1780965790854, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1884/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr9c3t2", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "This event revealed that global dollar liquidity was much tighter than people thought.", "created": 1780965790853, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1885/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr9f6hw", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "The Fed even had to restart a form of QE (\"Not QE\") in October 2019, buying $60 billion/month in Treasury bills.", "created": 1780965790851, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1886/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr9nhf9", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "This bailout of the repo market continued through early 2020, and then got even larger during the COVID-19 crash.", "created": 1780965790850, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1887/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr96262", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "The New York Fed intervened by offering repo operations, effectively injecting tens of billions of dollars daily into the banking system.", "created": 1780965790849, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1888/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr9oy11", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Regulatory requirements (like Basel III liquidity rules) made banks reluctant to lend spare cash even when they had it.", "created": 1780965790847, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1889/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr9tbj9", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Big banks held lots of Treasuries but not enough cash reserves \u2014 they were \"collateral rich but cash poor.\"", "created": 1780965790846, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1890/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr93ifc", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Bank reserves at the Fed had dropped significantly because the Fed had been shrinking its balance sheet (\"quantitative tightening\") since 2018.", "created": 1780965790845, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1891/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr9xz7c", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Corporate tax payments and settlement of a large batch of U.S. Treasury securities both happened at the same time, draining cash from the banking system.", "created": 1780965790844, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1892/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr95hzj", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "This was abnormal \u2014 repo is supposed to be ultra-safe and low-yield. It meant banks and institutions stopped trusting each other short-term, or they didn't have enough cash.", "created": 1780965790842, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1893/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr9edie", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "On September 16\u201317, 2019, overnight repo rates, which are normally close to the Fed Funds rate (then around 2%), suddenly spiked to as high as 10%.", "created": 1780965790841, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1894/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr99wug", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Here\u2019s a detailed breakdown of what happened:", "created": 1780965790839, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1895/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr9ocx1", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "In September 2019, there was a major liquidity crisis in the U.S. repo market \u2014 a key part of the financial plumbing system \u2014 and it sent shockwaves through Wall Street and the Federal Reserve.", "created": 1780965790838, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1896/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr964an", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "what happened in september 2019 in the financial plumbing system?", "created": 1780965790837, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1897/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr974ia", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Regulatory Constraints: Post-2008 financial regulations limited banks' flexibility to respond quickly to liquidity shortages.", "created": 1780965790836, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1898/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr9byz8", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Declining Bank Reserves: A gradual reduction in bank reserves due to the Federal Reserve's balance sheet normalization left less liquidity in the system.\u200b", "created": 1780965790835, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1899/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr9w3py", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Treasury Settlements: The settlement of newly issued Treasury securities on the same day required substantial cash outflows from investors.\u200b", "created": 1780965790834, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1900/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr966o0", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Corporate Tax Payments: Quarterly corporate tax payments due on September 16 led to significant cash withdrawals from the banking system", "created": 1780965790833, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1901/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr9hye3", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Several factors contributed to this sudden stress:", "created": 1780965790832, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1902/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr9890b", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "On September 17, 2019, interest rates on overnight repo agreements surged dramatically, with the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) jumping from 2.43% to 5.25%, and some transactions reaching as high as 10%. This spike disrupted the normal functioning of short-term funding markets, prompting the Federal Reserve to intervene by injecting $75 billion in liquidity to stabilize the system. \u200b", "created": 1780965790830, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 1903/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr74k3g", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "\ud83d\udcca 2. Interest Rate Swap Spread Convergence", "created": 1780965790664, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2031/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr7sejd", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "\"Hedge\" completely failed due to correlation inversion and panic-driven capital flight.", "created": 1780965790663, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2032/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr7h4wb", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "No liquidity in EM debt markets; no exit.", "created": 1780965790662, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2033/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr748ic", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Markets became irrational \u2014 it wasn\u2019t about relative value anymore, just getting out alive.", "created": 1780965790661, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2034/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr75o1r", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Losses on both legs again.", "created": 1780965790660, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2035/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr7i3qm", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Their \u201chedge\u201d in Treasuries actually lost value because people rushed to buy U.S. debt \u2192 yields dropped \u2192 they lost on the short.", "created": 1780965790659, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2036/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr73g6p", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "LTCM\u2019s longs were crushed.", "created": 1780965790658, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2037/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr7680f", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "EM bonds plummeted. Spreads blew out from ~600 bps to 1500+ bps.", "created": 1780965790657, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2038/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr7rhbj", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "In August 1998, Russia defaulted on its debt and devalued the ruble.", "created": 1780965790656, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2039/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr7z23w", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "To hedge, they shorted developed market debt (like Treasuries or German Bunds).", "created": 1780965790654, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2040/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr7dmjz", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "They went long EM government bonds, betting that yields would fall and spreads vs U.S. Treasuries would tighten over time.", "created": 1780965790653, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2041/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr731c4", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "LTCM believed that sovereign debt in emerging markets (like Russia or Brazil) was mispriced due to panic or political noise.", "created": 1780965790652, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2042/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr7fjwz", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "\ud83d\udcc9 1. Emerging Market Arbitrage (Russia, Brazil)", "created": 1780965790651, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2043/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr7wd6h", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Interest Rate Swap Spread Convergence.", "created": 1780965790650, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2044/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr735ly", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Emerging Market Arbitrage, and", "created": 1780965790649, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2045/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6pwk2", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "let\u2019s dive into two more LTCM trades that blew up in 1998:", "created": 1780965790647, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2046/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6n15l", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "A beautifully engineered hedge \u2014 under normal conditions \u2014 became a trap in a panic. The \u201cmarket-neutral\u201d trade magnified losses when liquidity dried up and correlation patterns flipped.", "created": 1780965790646, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2047/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6jj1s", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Fed stepped in with a $3.6 billion bailout via a consortium of banks.", "created": 1780965790645, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2048/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6zu8d", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Their leveraged position size meant tiny spread changes wiped out capital.", "created": 1780965790644, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2049/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6z86w", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "LTCM couldn\u2019t exit without taking catastrophic losses.", "created": 1780965790643, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2050/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr68n7u", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "In the crisis, market participants abandoned pricing models and rushed to sell.", "created": 1780965790642, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2051/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6jgr6", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "But the hedge relied on normal market functioning \u2014 specifically, liquidity and rational spread behavior.", "created": 1780965790641, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2052/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6z55r", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "This wasn\u2019t a directional trade \u2014 it was a relative value play.", "created": 1780965790640, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2053/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6xmfo", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "(Imagine a chart showing a normally tight spread of 5\u201310 bps suddenly exploding to 60\u2013100 bps in days.)", "created": 1780965790638, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2054/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr69klh", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "They lost on both legs of the trade.", "created": 1780965790636, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2055/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6qz7e", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "But in the crisis, the on-the-run got even more expensive, and the off-the-run tanked.", "created": 1780965790635, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2056/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6ioea", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "LTCM\u2019s \u201chedge\u201d (short on-the-run, long off-the-run) was supposed to be neutral.", "created": 1780965790634, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2057/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6rntq", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "This caused the spread to widen massively, instead of narrowing.", "created": 1780965790632, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2058/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr66zs2", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "They dumped off-the-run bonds.", "created": 1780965790631, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2059/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr65zhz", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Investors rushed into the most liquid bonds \u2014 on-the-run Treasuries.", "created": 1780965790630, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2060/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6ql4t", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Use massive leverage to magnify returns on small spreads (e.g. 2\u20135 bps)", "created": 1780965790627, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2061/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6t9w0", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Wait for the spread to converge \u2014 pocket the difference", "created": 1780965790626, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2062/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6ygc5", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Long the cheaper off-the-run bond", "created": 1780965790625, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2063/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6uaze", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Short the overpriced on-the-run bond", "created": 1780965790624, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2064/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr627b4", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Normally, these have similar yields, but on-the-run bonds trade slightly more expensive due to liquidity premium.", "created": 1780965790622, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2065/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr61sjx", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "\u201cOff-the-run\u201d Treasuries = older issues (less liquid)", "created": 1780965790621, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2066/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6h45x", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "\u201cOn-the-run\u201d Treasuries = most recently issued (highly liquid)", "created": 1780965790620, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2067/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6c1cd", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "\ud83e\uddfe TRADE EXAMPLE: On-the-Run vs. Off-the-Run U.S. Treasuries", "created": 1780965790619, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2068/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6qfrg", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Let\u2019s break down a real LTCM convergence trade that backfired \u2014 and show how the hedge turned into a disaster.", "created": 1780965790618, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2069/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6x642", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "In a systemic crisis, hedging models fail, liquidity vanishes, and correlations go haywire \u2014 turning textbook hedges into ticking time bombs.", "created": 1780965790617, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2070/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6em5m", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "LTCM thought they were \u201cmarket neutral.\u201d In reality, they were massively long liquidity and short volatility \u2014 and didn\u2019t realize it until too late.", "created": 1780965790615, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2071/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr63ivl", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "In a crisis, correlations reversed, markets froze, and hedges became liabilities.", "created": 1780965790614, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2072/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr60jmn", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "They were theoretical hedges in normal conditions.", "created": 1780965790613, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2073/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6zfb3", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "The Fed had to orchestrate a bailout to prevent systemic collapse.", "created": 1780965790611, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2074/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6vpea", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "LTCM\u2019s failure threatened major banks and brokers (they were counterparties to trillions in derivatives).", "created": 1780965790610, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2075/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6wrxg", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "LTCM couldn\u2019t meet margin calls, and counterparties started demanding more collateral.", "created": 1780965790608, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2076/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr66bc3", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "A 3% spread blowout could mean a 75% loss if you\u2019re 25x leveraged.", "created": 1780965790607, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2077/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6f8md", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Everyone was de-risking. There was no one left to sell to or buy from \u2014 so hedges were trapped.", "created": 1780965790605, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2078/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6ax73", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "But in the crisis, liquidity vanished.", "created": 1780965790604, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2079/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr68o2i", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Normally, LTCM could rebalance or add to positions.", "created": 1780965790603, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2080/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6uaoc", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Hedges failed because they moved the same direction.", "created": 1780965790601, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2081/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6psuh", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Hedges \u2014 like short positions in Treasuries \u2014 lost money at the same time their long positions in corporate or emerging market debt lost money.", "created": 1780965790600, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2082/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6r8dx", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "But spreads blew out instead.", "created": 1780965790599, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2083/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr64cxz", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "LTCM was betting that spreads would narrow (e.g. between corporate bonds and Treasuries).", "created": 1780965790598, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2084/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6q7sq", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Investors panicked and fled to safe assets (U.S. Treasuries), dumping riskier ones (even if high-quality).", "created": 1780965790596, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2085/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6vd09", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Russia defaulted on its debt, shocking global markets.", "created": 1780965790595, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2086/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6337i", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "They hedged with offsetting positions, often using leverage up to 25x to 50x.", "created": 1780965790592, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2087/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr60hog", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Their strategy: convergence trades \u2014 betting that price spreads (like on bonds or swaps) would normalize.", "created": 1780965790591, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2088/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6g0jh", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "LTCM was run by Nobel Prize winners and elite quants.", "created": 1780965790590, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2089/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6fsdm", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "EXAMPLE 2: Long-Term Capital Management (LTCM) is a classic example where hedges not only disappeared, but amplified risk.", "created": 1780965790588, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2090/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6vt01", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "When Lehman collapsed, it wasn\u2019t just that a big bank failed \u2014 it destroyed trust in counterparties, froze funding markets, and rendered many hedges either untradable, unpayable, or ineffective. Everyone rushed to unwind risk, and the whole system broke down together.", "created": 1780965790587, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2091/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6p6kl", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Hedges that required rolling over short-term funding couldn\u2019t be maintained.", "created": 1780965790586, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2092/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6f24f", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "When Lehman failed, repo lenders froze, causing massive liquidity stress.", "created": 1780965790585, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2093/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr62923", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Many leveraged players (hedge funds, banks) used the repo market for short-term funding.", "created": 1780965790584, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2094/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6oi3p", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Equities, commodities, and even investment-grade bonds dropped as the market panicked and deleveraged across the board.", "created": 1780965790582, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2095/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6n270", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Normally uncorrelated assets began falling together.", "created": 1780965790581, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2096/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr67bzy", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "This caused hedges to drop in value, even though they were \u201csafe,\u201d because of forced liquidation.", "created": 1780965790579, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2097/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6q9bs", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Investors holding Treasury futures or gold as hedges had to sell them for cash to meet margin calls.", "created": 1780965790578, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2098/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6fo0e", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Firms couldn\u2019t unwind or access hedges because the clearing process froze.", "created": 1780965790576, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2099/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6szh7", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "When Lehman collapsed, the whereabouts of collateral became unclear, locking up billions in supposedly hedged positions.", "created": 1780965790575, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2100/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr6076b", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Many trades with Lehman involved collateral and rehypothecation (Lehman reused posted collateral).", "created": 1780965790574, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2101/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5o3rd", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Even if you were \u201cright\u201d and held CDS protection, if your counterparty was Lehman, you were out of luck.", "created": 1780965790571, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2102/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5nwcx", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "But Lehman was a seller of CDS. So when it collapsed, those hedges became worthless or highly uncertain.", "created": 1780965790570, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2103/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5txaj", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Hedge funds and banks used CDS to protect against defaults.", "created": 1780965790569, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2104/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5khrc", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Lehman was a major counterparty in global derivatives \u2014 swaps, CDS, repo, you name it. When they filed for bankruptcy on September 15, 2008, it shattered confidence in the financial system.", "created": 1780965790566, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2105/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5wfa6", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "EXAMPLE 1: Let\u2019s break down how hedges disappeared during the Lehman Brothers collapse (2008) \u2014 a textbook example of counterparty and systemic risk destroying risk protection.", "created": 1780965790565, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2106/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr58fqe", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "In a credit crisis, the financial system is so stressed that your safety net either breaks, gets pulled out, or becomes useless\u2014this is why hedges \"disappear.\"", "created": 1780965790564, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2107/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5ts7u", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Example: VaR-based hedging strategies underestimate tail risk.", "created": 1780965790563, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2108/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5xi0s", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "In a credit crisis, those models break down, leading to improper risk exposure.", "created": 1780965790562, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2109/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr532ab", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Many hedging strategies rely on models assuming normal market behavior.", "created": 1780965790561, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2110/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5trok", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Even if your hedge gains value, you may face margin calls on your core position and be forced to liquidate your hedge early, locking in losses.", "created": 1780965790559, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2111/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5a2ov", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Bid-ask spreads blow out, so you eat losses even when \u201ctechnically\u201d hedged.", "created": 1780965790557, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2112/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr524xe", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "You can\u2019t sell or adjust your hedge at a fair price.", "created": 1780965790556, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2113/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5fdxl", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Instruments used to hedge (like CDS, options, futures) may become illiquid.", "created": 1780965790555, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2114/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5k63i", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Example: In 2008, even safe-haven assets like gold and Treasuries sold off briefly due to forced liquidations.", "created": 1780965790553, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2115/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5l3ij", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "A hedge that was designed to move opposite your main position now crashes too.", "created": 1780965790552, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2116/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5hm2p", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Assets that are normally uncorrelated start moving together.", "created": 1780965790551, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2117/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5tg86", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "In a crisis, counterparties go bankrupt or become illiquid, so your hedge might be worthless even if it's \u201cin the money.\u201d", "created": 1780965790549, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2118/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr508no", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Hedges like credit default swaps (CDS) or interest rate swaps rely on the other party being able to pay.", "created": 1780965790548, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2119/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5wmmn", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "even positions that are supposed to protect you from losses (hedges) can fail or become ineffective during a severe financial crisis.", "created": 1780965790546, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2120/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr54rh0", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "IN A CREDIT CRISIS HEDGES SUDDENLY DISAPPEAR:", "created": 1780965790545, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2121/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5z3ov", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "This is why in a crisis, everyone demands actual ownership, not just \u201crights to rehypothecated collateral.\u201d", "created": 1780965790544, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2122/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5k3t4", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "One default locks up the whole chain, causing a liquidity freeze (as seen in Lehman collapse).", "created": 1780965790543, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2123/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5b89u", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "More links = greater fragility.", "created": 1780965790542, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2124/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr52ff6", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "High collateral velocity = greater system-wide leverage.", "created": 1780965790541, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2125/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5cjor", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Collateral transformation allows firms to swap illiquid assets for Treasuries to repledge again.", "created": 1780965790540, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2126/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr533f8", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "No regulation cap in many jurisdictions (esp. UK pre-2008).", "created": 1780965790539, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2127/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5n0wq", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "\ud83d\udd0d *Some studies (e.g. by IMF and BIS) found collateral velocity in excess of 3.0 \u2014 meaning each dollar of collateral supported 3+ dollars of leverage, especially in hedge fund\u2013prime broker chains.", "created": 1780965790537, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2128/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5utlo", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "In the shadow banking system, rehypothecation of Treasuries can be used 4 to 10+ times per trade chain \u2014 and in some cases, even more.", "created": 1780965790530, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2129/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr56pdr", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "IN SHADOW BANKING HOW MANY TIMES rehypothecation OF TREASURIES IS USED ON TRADE?", "created": 1780965790529, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2130/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5w0g8", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "In a crisis, rehypothecation turns the safest asset (Treasuries) into a source of systemic risk.Collateral chains break, liquidity dries up, and trust collapses \u2014 intensifying the crash.", "created": 1780965790528, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2131/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5d9y5", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "In a downturn, that leverage amplifies losses, leading to forced liquidations and fire sales of good collateral \u2014 crashing prices further.", "created": 1780965790527, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2132/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5icp4", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Rehypothecation allows firms to create hidden leverage.", "created": 1780965790526, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2133/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr58yc1", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Result: Lending freezes, haircuts go up, repo rates spike \u2014 just when cash is most needed.", "created": 1780965790524, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2134/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5uevs", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "In a panic, lenders ask: \u201cIs that Treasury really yours to pledge?\u201d", "created": 1780965790523, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2135/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5c4bc", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "In calm times, everyone assumes the system works.", "created": 1780965790522, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2136/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr58ty5", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "\ud83d\ude31 Loss of Trust in Collateral Chains", "created": 1780965790521, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2137/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5vf84", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Everyone down the chain who counted on that collateral also fails or faces a margin call.", "created": 1780965790520, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2138/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5ygj6", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "If one player can't return rehypothecated collateral, it causes a domino effect.", "created": 1780965790519, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2139/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr50trv", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "The system loses access to critical liquidity.", "created": 1780965790517, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2140/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr57evl", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "That collateral becomes frozen in bankruptcy court or litigation.", "created": 1780965790516, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2141/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5cr63", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "When one party fails (e.g., Lehman), nobody knows who really owns the Treasuries.", "created": 1780965790515, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2142/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5hvsm", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "\ud83d\udd0d Think of it like 1 Treasury bond being used as \u201cbacking\u201d for 3\u20134 different loans across the system.", "created": 1780965790512, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2143/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5tif9", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "This cycle can repeat multiple times, especially in the shadow banking system.", "created": 1780965790511, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2144/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr56kos", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "When you post Treasuries as collateral (say, in a repo or margin loan), the lender can reuse those same Treasuries as collateral for its own trades.", "created": 1780965790510, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2145/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr58dy1", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Rehypothecation of Treasuries makes a financial crisis worse because it multiplies hidden leverage, traps collateral, and causes a chain reaction of liquidity freezes when trust breaks down.", "created": 1780965790507, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2146/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5n8zk", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "WHY DOES rehypothecation OF TREASURIES MAKE FINANCIAL CRISIS EVEN WORST?", "created": 1780965790506, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2147/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5qwe4", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "BCS ALL THE INTERNATIONAL TRADE IS SETTLED ON THE US DOLLAR THAT FORCES GLOBAL CENTRAL BANKS TO KEEP US DOLLARS AS RESERVE CURRENCY FOR PAYMENTS OF FUTURE IMPORTS. AND THAT RESULTS IN HUGE AMOUNT OF DOLLARS HODLED IN THE MARKET. THERE IS A GLOBAL ABSOLUTE NEED TO HOLD US DOLLARS TO CONDUCT GLOBAL TRADE.", "created": 1780965790505, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2148/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr515y7", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "That's mostly through the wealth effect people who own assets have higher asset valuations in their portfolio, they are likely to spend more and also if a company valuations expand , they are more likely invest more. When you balance sheet increases bcs as the stocks go up in your portfolio and you feel wealthier, you are more generous in your spending behavior than when it goes the other way.", "created": 1780965790504, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2149/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr56h22", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Financial assets today are at historic high relative to the size of the economy.", "created": 1780965790503, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2150/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5raxt", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "It's sort of George soros reflexively theory: the stock market or financial markets influence the real economy to a much higher degree than the real economy influences financial markets.", "created": 1780965790502, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2151/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5bebb", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "IT'S MUCH MORE IMPORTANT FOR THE ECONOMY WHAT THE STOCK MARKET DOES THAN FOR THE STOCK MARKET WHAT THE ECONOMY DOES.", "created": 1780965790501, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2152/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5d3nv", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "THE STOCK MARKET HAS IMMEDIATE EFFECT ON THE ECONOMY BCS MOST SPENDING IS DONE BY WEALTHY INDIVIDUALS WHOME WEALTH IS MOSTLY INVESTED IN THE STOCK MARKET.", "created": 1780965790500, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2153/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr5djpq", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "The FED HAS 2 OFFICIAL MANDATES: FULL EMPLOYMENT , LOW INFLATION. AND THE THIRS UNOFFICIAL MANDATE IS TO KEEP THE SYSTEM PROPERLY WORKING, USUALLY WHEN THE MARKET DUMPS BEYOND 20% THATS WHEN THE FED GETS NERVOUS AND INTERVENES TO BAIL OUT THE MARKETS AS LONG AS INFLATION AND INFLATION EXPECTATIONS ARE LOW. IF INFLATION AND INFLATION EXPECTATIONS ARE HIGH THEN THE FED WOULDN'T INTERVENE UNTIL THE MARKET DUMPS BEYOND 30% BCS THEN THEY HAVE TO SAVE THE SYSTEM AT ALL COST AND THEY JUST DONT CARE NEITHER ABOUT INFLATION NOR INFLATION EXPECTATIONS.", "created": 1780965790499, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2154/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr49gin", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "IN THE US COMMUNITY AND SMALL BANKS PROVIDE 70% OF AGRICULTURAL LENDING, 40% OF SMALL BUSINESS LENDING, 40% OF REAL ESTATE LENDING.", "created": 1780965790496, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2155/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr4qs3h", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "WHAT DOES THE US HAS THAT\u2019S DIFFERENT THAN THE OTHER G7 COUNTRIES? IT\u2019S THE NUMBER OF LARGE BANKS AND FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS AND THE DEPTH AND BREADTH OF CAPITAL AND CREDIT MARKETS.", "created": 1780965790495, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2156/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr44p6f", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "ONE GUY\u2019S INCOME IS ANOTHER GUY\u2019S SPENDING AND VICE VERSA.", "created": 1780965790494, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2157/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr4p9bb", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "ZERO COUPON IS A LEVERED TREASURY BOND.", "created": 1780965790493, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2158/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr4l88z", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "HOW DOES LIQUIDATING BEAR MARKET? WHAT USUALLY HAPPENS IN THESE SEVERE MARKET DECLINES LIKE 2008, 2019. WHEN MONEY MANAGERS HAVE SOLD EVERYTHING, THEY WANNA SELL EXCEPT THE GOLD. THEN THEY FINALLY SAY: \u201cWE STILL NEED MORE CASH\u201d AND THEN THEY SELL THE GOLD AS WELL. BUT THOSE DECLINES ARE SHORT TERM MAYBE THEY LAST 1 OR 2 MONTHS AND THAT GIVES YOU A GREAT BUYING OPPORTUNITY.", "created": 1780965790492, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2159/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1qr4boxw", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "IN A LIQUIDATING BEAR MARKET PEOPLE SELL WHATEVER THEY CAN SELL JUST TO GET CASH. AND HOW DO WE KNOW WE ARE IN A LIQUIDATING BEAR MARKET? HIGH VOLUME BIG SELLING GOING ON IN THE MARKET. JUST HUGE SELLING OF ANY STOCK NOT SPECIFIC SECTOR NOT NEWS RELATED AND THERE ISNT EVEN ANYTHING BAD ABOUT THE COMPANY. A VERY VERY URGENT CASE OF RAISING MONEY.", "created": 1780965790491, "pinned": false, "source": "global  liquidity notes.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2160/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1e4r4xp4", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Commercial paper is issued by large institutions to raise money to cover short-term financial needs. It pays fixed interest rates and has maturities ranging from as few as one to as many as 270 days. Unlike longer-term debt instruments, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) doesn't require commercial paper securities to be registered", "created": 1780965776249, "pinned": false, "source": "Financial Notes to print.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2278/12122  ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1e4r7uy5", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Commercial paper is a short-term, unsecured debt obligation typically issued by large banks and Corporations. As an individual investor, you may have seen it listed as one of the holdings of a mutual fund you own. The nature of commercial paper makes it most suitable for institutional investors and perhaps wealthy individuals to buy it directly. Smaller investors are most likely to have exposure to it through products such as money market funds", "created": 1780965776248, "pinned": false, "source": "Financial Notes to print.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2279/12122  ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1e4r970i", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Commercial paper is a type of debt security that Corporations use as an alternative to loans to raise capital", "created": 1780965776247, "pinned": false, "source": "Financial Notes to print.docx"}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1e4r1g06", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "A reverse repo is, logically enough, the reverse of that, where the bank makes a short-term, guaranteed loan to the central bank. Reverse repos are a sign of excess liquidity in the system, meaning that banks have money left over after covering their liabilities and investing and lending what they are comfortable with.", "created": 1780965776197, "pinned": false, "source": "Financial Notes to print.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2311/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1e4r0p26", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "When the repo rate increases, the cost of borrowing for banks also increases, which is passed to their account holders by increasing the interest rate on loans and deposit rates. - `18:08:22` --- note 2312/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1e4rclb6", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "An increase in the reverse repo rate will decrease the money supply and vice-versa, other things remaining constant. - `18:08:22` --- note 2410/12122  ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1e4r2uid", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "There are some big benefit\u2019s to having a low valued currency. For starters, if your currency is less valuable then importing stuff becomes more expensive. And this sounds bad but it\u2019s actually good for producing nations bcs it gives domestic made good an advantage as it makes domestic made goods cheaper to local citizens than foreign goods. For ex: if someone is tossing up between a Cadillac and a Mercedes, they might be pretty cost comparable. if the US dollar loses half or its value though, then that Mercedes is going to be twice as expensive to purchase bcs it\u2019s going to take double the amount of American dollars to pay the German auto manufacturer in euros. which would make the American car buyer just stick with the Cadillac even if that means getting a lower quality car but hey it\u2019s half the price, and hey look American auto manufacturer lives to see another day. This currency manipulation or drop in the ex, would achieve the same goal as tariffs but it does not break any rules of any trade agreements that will normally stipulate that tariffs are banned. So devaluing the currency is big win for local industry.", "created": 1780965776048, "pinned": false, "source": "Financial Notes to print.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2411/12122  ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1e4rsnn0", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "we would have a negative growth a 10% decline. Why does Economic growth matter? Economic growth is important bcs more production usually means more jobs, higher incomes and less poverty so a better living standards. How is economic growth measured? Growth is measured by changes in GDP.", "created": 1780965776039, "pinned": false, "source": "Financial Notes to print.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2412/12122  ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1e4rqorh", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "For ex: let\u2019s imagine an economy that only produces cars, in the first year they produced 1000 cars, while in the second year they produced 1050. The real GDP growth in the second year would then be 5% ( the 50 extra cars). Growth can also be negative for ex: if an economy that only produce cars produce 1000 cars in the first year and 900 cars in the second year then", "created": 1780965776038, "pinned": false, "source": "Financial Notes to print.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2413/12122  ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1e4r0uiz", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Economic growth is the total increase in the value of all goods and services a country produce (like: bread, cars, machinery, hotel stays, restaurant meals) each year compared to last.", "created": 1780965776037, "pinned": false, "source": "Financial Notes to print.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2414/12122  ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1e4r0v44", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Indebted Gov and Corp have only 2 choices either growing their way out of debt ( by increasing production) or inflating it away ( higher inflation).", "created": 1780965776004, "pinned": false, "source": "Financial Notes to print.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2415/12122  ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1e4rzz1n", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Wars, Deglobalization and onshoring of supply chains are inflationary. Being unable to leverage cheap commodities and labor in places like Russia means there is a high likelihood of higher inflation in the west going forward.", "created": 1780965775999, "pinned": false, "source": "Financial Notes to print.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2416/12122  ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1e4rrkgu", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Central Banks can ONLY keep short term interest rates low. The interest rate changes that central bank make only apply to overnight interest rates which have a kock on effect on other short term interest rates however longer-term interest rates are mostly determined by the market by the buying and selling of longer term treasuries. The amount of buying and selling depends on a combination of factors but primarily expectations about future inflation levels and Central Bank interest rates in each country.", "created": 1780965775997, "pinned": false, "source": "Financial Notes to print.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2417/12122  ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1e4r616d", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Corporate raise funds in 3 to 5 year area. 1y-3y shows u if their cost of financing going up and 5y-10y show u investors\u2019 appetite for their debt", "created": 1780965775988, "pinned": false, "source": "Financial Notes to print.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2418/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1e4rkmf7", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "Bonds can be divided into 2 parts: the front part which is about interest rates expectations 1y-3y or 1y-5y that tells u what the market is pricing in for feds rate hikes. The back end is about term premium .5y-10y spread show u the term premium. A collapse in risk premium is all about change in risk appetite. It tells u bond investors don't want to take risk they want they safety of the safe asset which is the 10-year bond.", "created": 1780965775987, "pinned": false, "source": "Financial Notes to print.docx"}
- `18:08:22` --- note 2419/12122  ---

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "nmq5x1e4q93n6", "cat": "philosophy", "text": "The Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) is a regulatory requirement established by the Basel III framework for banking supervision. The LCR is designed to ensure that financial institutions have enough high-quality liquid assets (HQLA) to cover their short-term liquidity needs during a period of financial stress. LCR dictates that Banks should have enough high-quality liquid assets to cover their expected cash outflows over a 30-day stress scenario. High-quality liquid assets typically include cash, central bank reserves, Treasuries and a certain corporate security that are easily convertible to cash without significant loss of value.", "created": 1780965775893, "pinned": false, "source": "Financial Notes to print.docx"}
