- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-0fd1dee5091dcbe2", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:SPX] Best investment advice on risk assets: \r\nHere are some of the most important investment principles and advice when dealing with risk assets (stocks, high-yield bonds, crypto, emerging markets, etc.):\r\n1. Understand Risk\u2013Reward Tradeoff: Higher expected returns always come with higher risk. Don\u2019t chase performance blindly. Ask yourself: \u201cCan I withstand a 30\u201350% drawdown without panicking?\u201d If not, your allocation is too aggressive. Position sizing is the ultimate risk management tool.\r\n2. Diversification is Your First Defense: Spread across asset classes (equities, bonds, real estate, commodities, crypto). Spread within asset classes (different sectors, geography, maturities).\r\nDiversification won\u2019t eliminate risk, but it reduces the chance of catastrophic loss.\r\n3. Liquidity Matters More Than You Think: In crises, it\u2019s not the valuation that kills investors\u2014it\u2019s the lack of liquidity.\r\nKeep a cash buffer (5\u201320%) for unexpected opportunities or emergencies.\r\nAvoid overexposure to illiquid assets if you might need cash within 12\u201324 months.\r\n4. Respect Leverage: Leverage amplifies both gains and losses.\r\nMargin debt or options can wipe you out faster than fundamentals can save you.\r\nUse leverage sparingly, if at all\u2014especially in volatile or opaque markets.\r\n5. Have an Exit Plan: Always know your sell criteria before you buy (stop-loss, valuation trigger, or macro signal).\r\nDon\u2019t fall in love with a position\u2014the market doesn\u2019t care about your cost basis.\r\nTaking small losses early is far cheaper than holding through a collapse.\r\n6. Macro & Market Cycles Matter: \r\nRisk assets perform best when liquidity is abundant (falling rates, expanding credit).\r\nBear markets and crises often follow tightening liquidity (rising rates, shrinking balance sheets).\r\nTrack macro indicators: yield curve, credit spreads, volatility index (VIX), and funding markets (SOFR, repo, RRP balances).\r\n\r\n\r\n7. Position Around Asymmetry: Look for trades where upside far outweighs downside.\r\nExamples: distressed assets at liquidation value, deep out-of-the-money options with limited risk, or equities with cash balances covering most of market cap.\r\nAvoid crowded trades where upside is limited but downside is catastrophic.\r\n8. Behavior is More Important Than Strategy: Even the best strategy fails if you can\u2

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-b6bd480dc73922b8", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:TB4WK] From all the treasury auction which one would show liquidity crunch and financial crisis first?\r\nIf you\u2019re looking for the earliest warning of a liquidity crunch or impending financial crisis from U.S. Treasury auction results, you\u2019d want to watch the shortest-maturity auctions \u2014 particularly 4-week and 8-week T-bill auctions \u2014 before anything else. Here\u2019s why:\r\n  Why short-term bill auctions are the earliest canary Bills = pure liquidity instruments 4-week and 8-week bills are the closest thing to \u201ccash\u201d in the financial system. Large banks, money-market funds, and collateralized lending markets use them heavily for repo and short-term funding. Liquidity stress shows up here first If dealers or money markets start demanding much higher yields to buy these, it\u2019s often because: They need cash urgently and are less willing to tie it up in bills. There\u2019s collateral hoarding in repo markets (similar to 2008 and September 2019 repo spike). Crisis progression often follows: Bill auction stress \u2192 Repo rate spikes \u2192 Broader bond market stress \u2192 Stock sell-off.\r\n  Auction types to monitor in order of earliest signal PriorityMaturity / TypeWhy it\u2019s early warningHistorical examples#14-week T-billPurest liquidity gauge; smallest duration riskSept 2019 repo crisis, March 2020 COVID shock#28-week T-billSame as 4-week but slightly less sensitiveLate 2007 pre-crisis stress#313-week T-billStill liquidity-heavy; can show funding rollover stressAug 2007 BNP freeze#42-year noteFirst coupon auction to show investor rate fearsSummer 2007\u20132008 before Lehman#530-year bondLate-cycle stress indicator; signals deep credit risk aversion2011 U.S. downgrade, debt ceiling episodes\r\n  What to look for in these auctions If any of these appear in short-bill auctions, it\u2019s a big red flag: High Tail \u2014 Actual high yield is way above the expected/when-issued yield. Low Bid-to-Cover \u2014 Drops below ~2.5 for bills or ~2.0 for notes/bonds. Weak Indirect Bidding \u2014 Foreign central banks pulling back. Primary Dealer Take-Down Spike \u2014 Dealers forced to absorb unwanted supply. Huge Spread Between High and Low Yield \u2014 Indicates volatile or nervous bidding.\r\n  Bottom line: 4-week and 8-week bill auctions are the first place a liquidity crunch will show up. Watch for high tails, collapsing bid-to-cover, and surging dealer allotments

YOU WANT TO KNOW THE SECRET? PATIENCE PAYS MORE THAN TALENT\u201d. JESSE Livermore\r\n\u201cWe mostly just sit around reading, thinking and waiting.\u201d \u2013 Stanley Druckenmiller\r\nPATIENCE PAYS MORE THAN TALENT.\r\nTHE BEST INVESTORS IN THE WORLD ARE REALLY GOOD AT DOING NOTHING FOR LONG PERIODS OF TIME.\r\nDEBT TURNS PROBLEMS INTO CATASTROPHES. CASH TURNS PROBLEMS INTO OPPORTUNITIES.\r\nDISCIPLINE TO ENTER IS GOOD. DISCIPLINE TO EXIT IS CRUCIAL, BUT DISCIPLINE TO WAIT, THAT\u2019S WHERE THE FORTUNE IS MADE.\r\nTHE REAL MONEY IS MADE IN THE WAITING, NOT IN THE TRADING! EVERYONE WANTS ACTION. JESSE MOORE BIGGEST PROFITS CAME WHEN HE DID ABSOLUTELY NOTHING. \r\nBUY WHAT\u2019S GOING UP, SELL WHAT\u2019S GOING DOWN! This rule is simple but don\u2019t let its simplicity fool you. IT WILL MAKE OR BREAK YOUR CAREER.\r\nIT\u2019S NOT HOW HIGH IT GOES, IT\u2019S WHAT YOU WALK AWAY WITH. SO REMEMBER THIS YOU MAKE MONEY WHEN YOU EXIT, NOT WHEN YOU ENTER. A GOOD TRADE ISNT COMPLETE UNTIL YOU CLOSE IT ON YOUR TERMS NOT THAT MARKET\u2019S. \r\nDON\u2019T ANTICIPATE THE MARKET, LET IT TELL YOU WHAT TO DO.\r\nEXITS MATTER MORE THAN ENTRIES: HOW YOU EXITS DETERMINES WHETHER YOU WIN OR JUST GET LUCKY ONCE. \r\nIN 1907 JESSY MADE A REAL FORTUNE NOT BCS HE CAUGHT THE TOP. NOT BCS HE PREDICTED THE EXACT MOMENT OF THE CRASH, BUT BCS HE KNEW WHEN TO GET OUT WHILE OTHERS HELD AND HOPED, HE SOLD. HE DIDN\u2019T NEED TO TIME PERFECTION, HE JUST NEEDE TO PROTECT PROFIT AND PRESERVE CAPITAL. \r\nWHEN THE MARKET TELLS YOU IT\u2019S DONE. BELIEVE IT! \r\nPOSITION SIZE MATTERS. NEVER GO ALL IN. ONLY FOOLS DO THAT.\r\n\u201cTHE DESIRE TO ALWAYS BE IN THE GAME IS ONE OF THE SPECTACULOR\u2019S GREATEST ENEMIES IN MANAGING HIS MONEY. IT WILL EVENTUALLY BRING DISASTER, AS IT HAS BROUGHT BANKRUPTCY

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-f01f148c2ebf2b57", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:CSGP] Here are the public aircraft engine manufacturers ranked by their market capitalization (size) as of 2025:\r\n\r\nGeneral Electric (GE Aviation)\r\n\r\nPublic Company: Yes (NYSE: GE)\r\n\r\nMarket Cap: Approximately $110 billion (overall GE market cap, as GE Aviation is a significant part of GE's business).\r\n\r\nNotes: GE Aviation is one of the largest and most prominent aircraft engine manufacturers, with a broad portfolio covering commercial, military, and cargo engines.\r\n\r\nPratt & Whitney (Raytheon Technologies)\r\n\r\nPublic Company: Yes (NYSE: RTX)\r\n\r\nMarket Cap: Approximately $150 billion (Raytheon Technologies' total market cap).\r\n\r\nNotes: Pratt & Whitney, a division of Raytheon Technologies, is one of the largest manufacturers of commercial and military jet engines.\r\n\r\nRolls-Royce\r\n\r\nPublic Company: Yes (LSE: RR)\r\n\r\nMarket Cap: Approximately $20 billion.\r\n\r\nNotes: Rolls-Royce is a major player in the aerospace industry, with engines for both commercial and military aircraft. It is based in the UK and is known for its high-end engineering.\r\n\r\nSafran Aircraft Engines (part of Safran Group)\r\n\r\nPublic Company: Yes (Euronext: SAF)\r\n\r\nMarket Cap: Approximately $60 billion (Safran Group market cap).\r\n\r\nNotes: Safran Aircraft Engines is a major manufacturer, particularly in partnership with GE for the CFM56 and LEAP engines.\r\n\r\nHoneywell Aerospace\r\n\r\nPublic Company: Yes (NASDAQ: HON)\r\n\r\nMarket Cap: Approximately $160 billion.\r\n\r\nNotes: Honeywell Aerospace is a key player in the business jet engine market and also supplies systems for commercial aircraft.\r\n\r\nCFM International (joint venture of GE and Safran)\r\n\r\nPublic Company: No (CFM International itself is not publicly traded; it is a joint venture between General Electric and Safran Aircraft Engines, both of which are public companies).\r\n\r\nNotes: As a joint venture, CFM does not have an independent market cap.\r\n\r\nEngine Alliance (joint venture of GE and Pratt & Whitney)\r\n\r\nPublic Company: No (Engine Alliance itself is not publicly traded; it is a joint venture between GE Aviation and Pratt & Whitney).\r\n\r\nNotes: Similar to CFM, Engine Alliance does not operate as an independent public company.\r\n\r\nSummary:\r\nGE Aviation (via General Electric) and Pratt & Whitney (via Raytheon Technologies) are the largest public companies in the aircraft engine manufac

Free Cash Flow: -$198.25M (\u25bc276.42% YoY)\r\nWhy it\u2019s frightening:\r\nFree cash flow (FCF) is the money left after capital expenditures \u2014 what the company actually has to invest, pay dividends, or reduce debt.\r\n\r\nA negative FCF of nearly $200M means UPS is burning cash, which is unsustainable long-term, especially if it persists.\r\n\r\nThe massive YoY collapse (\u25bc276%) is especially alarming \u2014 this implies a sharp deterioration in operational efficiency or an overextension in capital investment.\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udd34 2. Cash from Operations: $348M (\u25bc82.54% YoY)\r\nWhy it\u2019s frightening:\r\nThis is UPS\u2019s core cash engine, and it has collapsed:\r\n\r\nCash from operations fell from ~$2B to $348M \u2014 this suggests deteriorating core business performance, likely due to falling volumes, cost inflation, or pricing pressure.\r\n\r\nIf this persists, UPS might not have enough cash to sustain dividends (7.76% yield), invest, or survive an extended downturn without borrowing.\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udfe0 3. Earnings per Share: $1.55 (\u25bc13.41%) & Net Income: \u25bc8.94%\r\nWhy it matters:\r\n\r\nEarnings are shrinking across the board, even as expenses grow (see next point). EPS is down over 13%, and net income nearly 9%.\r\n\r\nWhile not as dire as the cash figures, this reflects declining profitability despite UPS cutting headcount and costs in past quarters.\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udfe0 4. Operating Expense: $2.89B (\u25b29.37%)\r\nWhy it matters:\r\n\r\nCosts are rising despite revenue dropping. That means margin compression, a dangerous situation in logistics.\r\n\r\nSuggests UPS is unable to pass costs onto customers (fuel, labor, etc.) \u2014 a competitive pricing war with FedEx or Amazon could be brewing.\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udfe1 5. Revenue: $21.22B (\u25bc2.74%)\r\nA top-line decline might seem small, but for a mature giant like UPS, it signals shrinking demand or market share in a competitive, low-margin business.\r\n\r\nCombined with rising expenses, this contributes directly to the erosion in profitability and cash flow.\r\n\r\n\u26a0\ufe0f Bonus Concern:\r\n\ud83d\udcc9 Stock Price Drop: ~$145 \u2192 ~$84 (\u25bc42% from 52-week high)\r\nThis shows that investors are already pricing in trouble. - `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-c8a07251fe01459b", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:RRPONTSYAWARD] How reverse repos affect liquidity:\r\n\r\nIn a reverse repo, the Fed takes cash from banks (or other counterparties) in exchange for securities and agrees to return the cash (plus a small interest payment) later. This process removes cash from the financial system temporarily, reducing liquidity.\r\nThe Fed uses reverse repos to control excess liquidity. For example, if banks have too much cash (say, from stimulus programs or low borrowing demand), the Fed can use reverse repos to \u201csoak up\u201d some of that cash, preventing it from flooding the market and potentially causing inflation or destabilizing interest rates.\r\nThe \"Wednesday Level\" of reverse repos shows how much cash the Fed has pulled out of the system on that day. A higher face value of securities in reverse repos means more cash has been removed, tightening liquidity. A lower value means less cash is being removed, leaving more liquidity in the system.\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\nReal-World Effects\r\n\r\nFor Collateral: If the Fed increases reverse repo activity, it ties up more high-quality securities, which could make collateral scarcer. This might raise borrowing costs in markets like the repo market, where Treasuries are commonly used as collateral. However, since the Fed\u2019s securities are only temporarily transferred, the impact is usually short-term.\r\nFor Liquidity: By adjusting the volume of reverse repos, the Fed fine-tunes the amount of cash in the system. For example:\r\n\r\nMore reverse repos \u2192 Less cash in the system \u2192 Tighter liquidity, which can push short-term interest rates up.\r\nFewer reverse repos \u2192 More cash in the system \u2192 Looser liquidity, which can keep interest rates low.", "created": 1753966269772, "pinned": false}

For example, if banks have too much cash (say, from stimulus programs or low borrowing demand), the Fed can use reverse repos to \u201csoak up\u201d some of that cash, preventing it from flooding the market and potentially causing inflation or destabilizing interest rates.\r\nThe \"Wednesday Level\" of reverse repos shows how much cash the Fed has pulled out of the system on that day. A higher face value of securities in reverse repos means more cash has been removed, tightening liquidity. A lower value means less cash is being removed, leaving more liquidity in the system.\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\nReal-World Effects\r\n\r\nFor Collateral: If the Fed increases reverse repo activity, it ties up more high-quality securities, which could make collateral scarcer. This might raise borrowing costs in markets like the repo market, where Treasuries are commonly used as collateral. However, since the Fed\u2019s securities are only temporarily transferred, the impact is usually short-term.\r\nFor Liquidity: By adjusting the volume of reverse repos, the Fed fine-tunes the amount of cash in the system. For example:\r\n\r\nMore reverse repos \u2192 Less cash in the system \u2192 Tighter liquidity, which can push short-term interest rates up.\r\nFewer reverse repos \u2192 More cash in the system \u2192 Looser liquidity, which can keep interest rates low.", "created": 1753966233003, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-1edf323d63049a87", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:2330] Risk to Thesis\r\nThere is one risk to the TSMC growth narrative, that even the management seems to be particularly mindful of. This is of course the foreign exchange risk.\r\n\r\nNormally, this would be a manageable background issue for most multinational companies, but given TSMC's operational structure, it stands to deliver material margin contraction for the company. This is because TSMC earns most of its revenue in US dollars, while the bulk of its costs are incurred in the New Taiwanese Dollar (TWD:USD). Unfortunately for TSMC, the Taiwanese dollar has strengthened significantly recently, owing to record equity inflows, trade surpluses, and even high-volume hedging activity by the country's insurance industry.\r\nAs we can see above, the currency has appreciated by over 13% since the beginning of April.\r\n\r\nFor TSMC, this directly hits at its gross margin. To keep it simple, its revenue earning currency is going weaker, and its expense paying currency is growing stronger, so that increases the cost of sales, and thus shrinks its gross profits. In fact, the management has quantified the impact of foreign exchange costs at 4.4%. Based on TTM figures, this accounts for about $2.8 billion. Given the company's massive growth trajectory, this cost is only expected to balloon if the risk isn't managed adequately.\r\n\r\nI see this magnitude of this risk being even further magnified in the case of geopolitical uncertainty, which could infuse further volatility in the currency markets. It is a risk I will be watching closely.", "created": 1753794304785, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-57e94ce5015df004", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:UNTAGGED] why does mexico interest rate minus us interest rate topping and starting to dump always mark the start of crypto bull market\r\n\r\n\r\nChatGPT said:\r\nThe Mexico\u2013U.S. interest rate spread (\ud83c\uddf2\ud83c\uddfd Banxico rate \u2013 \ud83c\uddfa\ud83c\uddf8 Fed rate) topping and then narrowing often aligns with the start of crypto bull markets for several macro-liquidity reasons:\r\n\r\n\ud83e\udde0 1. Carry Trade Unwinding \u2192 Risk-On Reallocation\r\nA high spread (e.g. Mexico rates much higher than U.S.) attracts carry trades: investors borrow in USD (low rate) to earn yields in MXN.\r\n\r\nWhen the spread tops and reverses, these trades unwind, freeing up capital.\r\n\r\nThat capital often rotates into risk assets like equities and crypto as real rates fall globally.\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udccc Conclusion: Falling MXN\u2013USD rate differential = global liquidity is becoming more accommodative \u2192 bullish for crypto.\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udcb5 2. Dollar Weakness Catalyst\r\nWhen Mexico stops hiking or starts cutting before the U.S., it can weaken the dollar.\r\n\r\nA weakening DXY is one of the strongest bull run signals for crypto because:\r\n\r\nCrypto is priced in dollars\r\n\r\nGlobal investors chase higher-beta assets when USD liquidity loosens\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udd01 Crypto bull runs often begin when DXY + U.S. real yields + rate differentials peak and start falling.\r\n\r\n\ud83c\udf0e 3. Emerging Markets as Risk Sentiment Barometers\r\nMexico is a liquidity-sensitive emerging market.\r\n\r\nWhen Banxico begins to ease, it reflects improving global financial conditions.\r\n\r\nRisk appetite tends to return when EMs shift from defensive to accommodative monetary policy.\r\n\r\n\ud83e\udde9 Crypto behaves like an ultra-high-beta EM asset, so it rallies when EMs shift dovish.\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udcca 4. Historical Pattern (Check These Dates)\r\nYear\tMexico-US Rate Spread Peak\tWhat Followed\r\nLate 2018\t+6% \u2192 started falling\tBTC bottomed and rose in 2019\r\nMid 2020\tPeak COVID spread \u2192 crashed\tBTC exploded late 2020\r\nLate 2022\tSpread topped ~7%\tETH, BTC bottomed; 2023 bull began", "created": 1747055694184, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-f7ec690be50c4e98", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:UNTAGGED] why does mexico interest rate minus japan interest rate topping and starting to dump always mark the start of crypto bull market\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\nChatGPT said:\r\nThe Mexico\u2013Japan interest rate differential topping and then narrowing often signals the start of a crypto bull market because it reflects a global macro inflection point in the carry trade and liquidity regime. Global Carry Trade Reversal\r\nWhen Mexico rates (high) minus Japan rates (ultra-low) is rising, it incentivizes carry trades: investors borrow in JPY and buy high-yield MXN assets.\r\n\r\nA top and reversal in this spread = carry trade unwinding.\r\n\r\nCapital flows out of yield plays and into high-beta risk assets, like crypto.\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udd04 Carry trade unwind = liquidity rotation \u2192 bullish for crypto\r\n\r\n2. Peak in \"Real Yield Divergence\" = Peak Tightness\r\nJapan is a perpetual dovish anchor. If Mexico (a high-yield EM) stops hiking or starts cutting, it usually signals:\r\n\r\nGlobal inflation is easing\r\n\r\nFinancial conditions are loosening\r\n\r\nThe peak in global monetary tightening is behind us\r\n\r\n\u26c5 This shift often marks the start of global risk-on \u2192 crypto surges\r\n\r\n3. Crypto Follows Liquidity, Not Just US Rates\r\nCrypto doesn\u2019t only follow the Fed \u2014 it follows global liquidity.\r\n\r\nThe MXN/JPY interest rate spread is a proxy for global monetary divergence.\r\n\r\nWhen it narrows, risk flows out of EM FX and into growth/speculative assets.\r\n\r\nBTC and ETH respond instantly to any signs that global liquidity is rebounding.\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udcc9 Topping rate differential = \ud83d\udfe2 bullish liquidity regime = \ud83e\ude99 crypto inflows\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udd01 Historical Evidence\r\nYear\tMX\u2013JP Rate Spread Topped\tWhat Followed\r\nLate 2018\t+7.5% \u2192 started falling\tBTC bottomed at $3k, bull began\r\nEarly 2020\tSpread crashed w/ COVID\tBTC surged after Fed QE\r\nLate 2022\tTopped >8%\tBTC, ETH bottomed \u2192 2023 bull started\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udcca Additional Context\r\nComponent\tBehavior\tCrypto Impact\r\n\ud83c\uddf2\ud83c\uddfd Banxico cutting\tRisk-on signal\tBullish\r\n\ud83c\uddef\ud83c\uddf5 BoJ staying flat or easing\tWeak JPY\tBullish for global carry\r\nMXN/JPY rate differential falling\tCapital rotates into risk\tCrypto bull start", "created": 1747055

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-df887eaf836617e7", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:UNTAGGED] why does taiwan dollar / us dollar always mark the bottom for markets especially risk assets?\r\n\r\n\r\nChatGPT said:\r\nThe Taiwan Dollar (TWD) / US Dollar (USD) exchange rate is a powerful global liquidity signal, and when TWD strengthens against USD (i.e. USD/TWD goes down), it often marks the bottom or turning point for risk assets \u2014 like tech stocks, semiconductors, and crypto. Here's why:\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udd11 1. Taiwan = Global Tech Supply Chain Epicenter\r\nTaiwan is home to TSMC, the largest semiconductor foundry in the world, and is deeply embedded in the global tech manufacturing ecosystem.\r\n\r\nA strengthening TWD implies capital inflows into Taiwanese assets and production, signaling risk-on behavior and forward demand for tech.\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udd04 2. TWD/USD = Global Export Demand Barometer\r\nA rising TWD (falling USD/TWD) means foreign buyers (especially the U.S.) are demanding more Taiwanese exports\u2014often electronics and chips.\r\n\r\nThat implies reviving global growth, higher consumption, and turnaround in business cycles \u2014 all bullish for risk assets.\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udcb8 3. Liquidity + Capital Flows\r\nWhen global investors rotate into EM Asia equities or semiconductors, TWD strengthens due to capital inflows.\r\n\r\nThese flows often accompany a peak in USD strength and a reversal of global liquidity tightening.\r\n\r\nWhen the USD weakens, risk assets rise. So, a strengthening TWD is a proxy for USD weakness + liquidity return.\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udcc9 4. Historically Predictive\r\nIn early 2020, late 2022, and again in late 2023, TWD strengthening coincided with the start of major bull moves in:\r\n\r\nNasdaq\r\n\r\nSemiconductors (SOXX)\r\n\r\nEthereum/Bitcoin\r\n\r\nMeme coins and tech growth stocks\r\n\r\n\ud83e\udde0 Summary:\r\nWhen TWD strengthens (USD/TWD falls), it signals capital is flowing back into Asia and tech\u2014marking the return of global liquidity and risk-on appetite.", "created": 1746914955100, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-b567992d8e95d63f", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:SOFR] why is sofr so important to track the the global liquidity plumbing?\r\n\r\n\r\nChatGPT said:\r\nSOFR (Secured Overnight Financing Rate) is critically important for tracking global liquidity plumbing because it sits at the core of the U.S. dollar funding system, which is the backbone of global finance. Here's why:\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udd11 Why SOFR Matters for Global Liquidity:\r\n1. SOFR = Cost of Borrowing Cash Overnight Using Treasuries as Collateral\r\nIt reflects the most basic, risk-free secured borrowing rate in the U.S.\r\n\r\nSpikes in SOFR mean banks or funds are scrambling for cash or collateral \u2014 a stress signal.\r\n\r\n2. Core of Repo Market = Dollar Liquidity Engine\r\nSOFR is derived from the overnight Treasury repo market, which moves trillions daily.\r\n\r\nDisruptions here ripple across:\r\n\r\nInterbank lending\r\n\r\nShort-term funding markets\r\n\r\nMargin calls in asset markets\r\n\r\n3. Key Signal of Systemic Strain or Easing\r\nRising SOFR = tightening liquidity (less cash chasing more collateral)\r\n\r\nFalling SOFR = easing conditions, more cash in the system\r\n\r\nHuge spike = potential crisis flashpoint (e.g., Sept 2019 repo blowout)\r\n\r\n4. Replaces LIBOR Globally\r\nSOFR is now the benchmark for pricing $ trillions in loans, swaps, and derivatives.\r\n\r\nIt's the base rate for interest rate swaps, floating rate notes, and Treasury futures.\r\n\r\n5. Correlated with Fed Policy & RRP\r\nFed\u2019s Reverse Repo Facility (RRP) and Treasury issuance affect SOFR directly.\r\n\r\nWatching SOFR vs. RRP usage shows whether:\r\n\r\nBanks prefer parking money at the Fed\r\n\r\nOr lending it out via repo\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udcc9 SOFR Spikes = Flashing Red Light\r\nExample: Sept 2019 \u2192 SOFR spiked to ~10% \u2192 Fed emergency repo ops began\r\n\r\nTight SOFR = dollar shortage, collateral scarcity, or banking stress", "created": 1746888819494, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-36b9e1c011af25c6", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:UNTAGGED] Why does taiwan dollar / usd pumping always flash the start of a bull run in risk assets?\r\nYou sent\r\nA strengthening Taiwan Dollar (TWD) against the U.S. Dollar (USD) \u2014 or \"TWD/USD pumping\" \u2014 often signals the start of a bull run in global risk assets for a few key macroeconomic and liquidity-related reasons:\r\n\r\n1. Global Tech Cycle & Semiconductor Demand\r\n\r\nTaiwan is the epicenter of global semiconductor manufacturing (TSMC, UMC).\r\n\r\nWhen TWD strengthens, it's often because of surging foreign demand for Taiwanese exports, especially chips \u2014 a leading indicator for global tech and manufacturing upcycles.\r\n\r\nTech bull markets usually correlate with early-stage equity rallies, especially in NASDAQ, crypto, and emerging markets.\r\n\r\n2. Capital Inflows & Global Liquidity\r\n\r\nA rising TWD often reflects hot money inflows into Asia, signaling risk-on sentiment.\r\n\r\nInvestors rotate out of USD (a safe-haven currency) into emerging markets, indicating confidence in growth assets.\r\n\r\nThis trend typically begins when the USD index (DXY) stalls or weakens, releasing global dollar pressure \u2014 a green light for risk assets.\r\n\r\n3. USD Liquidity Release\r\n\r\nTWD/USD strength is a proxy for easing USD funding conditions in Asia.\r\n\r\nIt often tracks or even leads:\r\n\r\nFalling cross-currency basis swaps\r\n\r\nRising Asia FX reserves\r\n\r\nLoosening financial conditions.\r\n\r\n4. Correlation With Crypto and Equities\r\n\r\nHistorically, TWD/USD rallies precede or coincide with:\r\n\r\nCrypto breakouts (BTC, ETH, meme coins)\r\n\r\nTech equity rebounds\r\n\r\nCommodities uptrends\r\n\r\nThis is because it reflects reflation trades and manufacturing optimism, both supportive of beta assets.\r\n\r\nSummary:\r\n\r\nTWD/USD pumping = signal of global liquidity returning, USD pressure easing, Asia tech cycle starting, and risk assets (especially tech, crypto, EM) entering a bullish phase.", "created": 1746547025105, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-8d22fc5f493c8ee8", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:RRPONTSYD] WHY REVERSE REPO SPIKING ALWAYS SIGNALS THE END OF CRYPTO BULL RUN?\r\n\r\n\r\nChatGPT said:\r\nA spike in reverse repo (RRP) usage is often a top signal for crypto and other risk assets \u2014 and here\u2019s exactly why:\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udd01 What Is Reverse Repo (RRP)?\r\nRRP = the Fed borrows cash overnight from money markets, giving Treasury collateral in return.\r\n\r\nWhen RRP spikes, it means there\u2019s a surge in demand for ultra-safe, short-term yield (risk-off behavior).\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udcc9 Why RRP Spiking Signals the End of a Crypto Bull Run\r\n\ud83e\uddca 1. It Means Liquidity Is Getting Pulled Out\r\nWhen cash flows into RRP, it\u2019s being sucked out of the financial system.\r\n\r\nLess liquidity \u2192 less fuel for crypto speculation.\r\n\r\nCrypto bull runs need excess liquidity. RRP spikes are like pulling the plug on the pool.\r\n\r\n\ud83c\udfe6 2. Money Market Funds Are Hoarding Cash\r\nHigh RRP = money is fleeing from risk assets (like crypto) to earn safe yield.\r\n\r\nIt reflects investor fear or desire to park cash safely \u2192 bearish for crypto.\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udd10 3. Short-Term Yields Become Too Attractive\r\nWhen RRP pays a decent yield (e.g., 5.3%), institutions prefer parking cash risk-free over speculating on volatile assets like altcoins.\r\n\r\nIt competes with crypto for capital \u2192 drains demand from DeFi, staking, and memecoins.\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udca5 4. - `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-684595519dc41827", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:FRED:RRPONTSYD] WHY REVERSE REPO SPIKING ALWAYS SIGNALS THE END OF CRYPTO BULL RUN?\r\n\r\n\r\nChatGPT said:\r\nA spike in reverse repo (RRP) usage is often a top signal for crypto and other risk assets \u2014 and here\u2019s exactly why:\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udd01 What Is Reverse Repo (RRP)?\r\nRRP = the Fed borrows cash overnight from money markets, giving Treasury collateral in return.\r\n\r\nWhen RRP spikes, it means there\u2019s a surge in demand for ultra-safe, short-term yield (risk-off behavior).\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udcc9 Why RRP Spiking Signals the End of a Crypto Bull Run\r\n\ud83e\uddca 1. It Means Liquidity Is Getting Pulled Out\r\nWhen cash flows into RRP, it\u2019s being sucked out of the financial system.\r\n\r\nLess liquidity \u2192 less fuel for crypto speculation.\r\n\r\nCrypto bull runs need excess liquidity. RRP spikes are like pulling the plug on the pool.\r\n\r\n\ud83c\udfe6 2. Money Market Funds Are Hoarding Cash\r\nHigh RRP = money is fleeing from risk assets (like crypto) to earn safe yield.\r\n\r\nIt reflects investor fear or desire to park cash safely \u2192 bearish for crypto.\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udd10 3. Short-Term Yields Become Too Attractive\r\nWhen RRP pays a decent yield (e.g., 5.3%), institutions prefer parking cash risk-free over speculating on volatile assets like altcoins.\r\n\r\nIt competes with crypto for capital \u2192 drains demand from DeFi, staking, and memecoins.\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udca5 4. RRP Spikes Often Align with Liquidity Stress\r\nHistorically, spikes in RRP have lined up with:\r\n\r\nEnd of stimulus (e.g., March\u2013April 2021)\r\n\r\nQT acceleration\r\n\r\nDebt ceiling risks\r\n\r\nAll of these pressure systemic liquidity, which hits speculative assets hardest.\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udcc9 Bottom Line:\r\nWhen reverse repo spikes:\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udcb8 Liquidity is leaving the market\r\n\r\n\ud83e\udde0 Risk appetite declines\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udcc9 Speculative assets like crypto and meme coins suffer\r\n\r\nSo, watching RRP is watching liquidity gravity. If RRP goes up, gravity strengthens, and crypto loses lift.", "created": 1746051586520, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-a56557313cb042f8", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:RRPONTSYD] WHY DOES REVERSE REPO COLAPPSE NEAR ZERO MARKS THE END OF QT AND THE BEGINNING OF QE?\r\nRRP Balances Collapse to Near Zero QT is partly funded by the reverse repo facility (RRP). As QT nears exhaustion, RRP drains, indicating the Fed has fewer internal sources to absorb balance sheet runoff.\r\nGreat question \u2014 let\u2019s break it down simply.\r\n________________________________________\r\n\ud83d\udd01 Reverse Repo Facility (RRP) Basics\r\n\u2022\tThe RRP facility is where the Fed borrows money overnight from money market funds and others, and gives them Treasuries as collateral.\r\n\u2022\tThink of it like the Fed soaking up excess cash in the system to keep short-term rates in range.\r\n\u2022\tAs of 2021\u20132023, trillions in excess liquidity ended up in the RRP because of past QE + fiscal stimulus.\r\n________________________________________\r\n\ud83e\uddef QT and the Role of RRP\r\n\u2022\tIn Quantitative Tightening (QT), the Fed lets Treasuries and MBS roll off its balance sheet \u2014 i.e., it doesn't reinvest maturing debt.\r\n\u2022\tTo do this without disrupting markets, the Fed first draws liquidity out of the system \u2014 and a big chunk of that came from the RRP.\r\nSo far, QT has been \u201csmooth\u201d because there's been a large RRP balance (~$2T+ at peak) to absorb the tightening.\r\n________________________________________\r\n\u26a0\ufe0f What Happens When RRP Goes to Zero\r\nWhen RRP collapses to near zero, it means:\r\n1.\tThere\u2019s no more excess liquidity for the Fed to drain.\r\n2.\tQT can\u2019t continue at the same pace without:\r\no\tReducing bank reserves (which could spark a 2019-style funding crisis)\r\no\tTriggering spikes in repo/SOFR rates (a sign of stress)\r\n3.\tIt forces the Fed to either pause QT or start injecting liquidity again (via QE, buybacks, or repos).\r\n________________________________________\r\n\ud83e\udde0 The Key Insight:\r\nThe Fed has two pools of liquidity to pull from:\r\n1.\tRRP (non-bank excess cash) \u2014 relatively safe to drain\r\n2.\tBank reserves \u2014 critical plumbing; draining too low causes stress\r\nOnce the RRP is drained, QT hits a wall, and the Fed must choose between:\r\n\u2022\tEnding QT\r\n\u2022\tBreaking something", "created": 1746051453833, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-6fa3fc34537531ff", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:SOFR] Treasury Trades\" Blew Up:\r\n\u2022\tHedge funds had been borrowing massively in repo to finance leveraged bets on U.S. Treasuries (called the \"basis trade\": long cash Treasuries, short futures).\r\n\u2022\tWhen repo rates spiked, their funding costs suddenly exploded, making their trades massively unprofitable overnight.\r\n\u2022\tSome funds had to liquidate positions or beg for emergency cash.\r\n Result: Hidden leverage in the system amplified the stress.", "created": 1745858055240, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-4e1a0d1b39deccd6", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:UNTAGGED] how does china weakening the yuan affect bitcoin and meme crypto?\r\nWhen China weakens the yuan (its currency), it\u2019s usually a deliberate move by the People\u2019s Bank of China to make Chinese exports cheaper and more competitive on the global stage, especially in response to things like U.S. tariffs or economic slowdowns. This has a few ripple effects that can impact Bitcoin. Let\u2019s break it down:\r\n1.\tCapital Flight Pressure: A weaker yuan reduces its purchasing power, which can spook Chinese investors\u2014especially the wealthy or savvy ones. China has strict capital controls, limiting how much money people can move out of the country (about $50,000 per year). When the yuan drops, some turn to Bitcoin as a way to \"park\" their wealth outside the government\u2019s reach. Bitcoin\u2019s decentralized nature makes it hard for authorities to track, despite China\u2019s crypto trading ban since 2021. Historically, yuan devaluations\u2014like in 2015-2016\u2014coincided with Bitcoin price surges (from $200 to $20,000 over time), as people sought alternatives to a weakening currency.\r\n2.\tUnderground Demand: Even with the ban, Chinese investors find workarounds\u2014over-the-counter (OTC) trading, foreign exchanges like Binance, or stablecoins like Tether (USDT). A weaker yuan often boosts this gray-market activity. For example, data from Chainalysis showed China\u2019s crypto transaction volume hit $86.4 billion between mid-2022 and mid-2023, suggesting the ban isn\u2019t fully stopping the flow. If the yuan keeps sliding, this demand could push Bitcoin prices up.\r\n3.\tGlobal Risk Sentiment: A weaker yuan can signal economic trouble in China, the world\u2019s second-largest economy. This rattles global markets, and Bitcoin sometimes benefits as a \u201cdigital gold\u201d hedge against uncertainty\u2014though it can also dip initially if investors dump risky assets like stocks and crypto together. Posts on X and past patterns (e.g., 2013, 2015, 2019) suggest Bitcoin often climbs when the yuan hits key thresholds like 7.2 against the USD.\r\nAnd for meme coins, their fate\u2019s more tied to social media buzz than macro shifts.\r\nIn short: A weaker yuan could juice Bitcoin by driving Chinese money into it as a hedge, with meme coins possibly tagging along for the ride. But it\u2019s not a straight line\u2014more like a chaotic dance between policy, markets, and human psych

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-14a76b6087dc80eb", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:MOVE] HOW DOES MOVE INDEX PREDICT QE AND LIQUIDITY? \r\nThe Fed might step in and start pumping money into the economy again\u2014aka \"going Brrr,\" like a money printer. One signal to watch for this is something called the MOVE Index, which tracks volatility (or wild price swings) in the bond market, specifically U.S. Treasury bonds.\r\nHere\u2019s how it works: When the MOVE Index goes up, it means bond prices are jumping around a lot. This volatility makes life tough for investors or traders who borrow money to buy bonds (like Treasuries or corporate bonds). Why? Because when volatility spikes, the people lending them money (think banks or brokers) get nervous and demand more collateral\u2014aka higher \"margin requirements.\" If these traders don\u2019t have the extra cash or assets to meet those demands, they\u2019re forced to sell their bonds to cover their positions.\r\nThis selling can snowball. A flood of bonds hitting the market pushes bond prices down, which drives yields (interest rates) up. Higher yields can spook the broader financial system, especially since Treasuries and corporate bonds are huge markets the Fed cares deeply about. They\u2019re like the backbone of U.S. finance\u2014Treasuries are the \"safe\" asset everyone relies on, and corporate bonds keep businesses funded.\r\nSo, if the MOVE Index keeps climbing and triggers enough forced selling, it could create chaos in these markets. The Fed, which sees itself as the guardian of financial stability, might decide it has no choice but to step in\u2014cutting rates, buying bonds, or flooding the system with cash (going Brrr) to calm things down and protect those critical markets.\r\nIn short: High MOVE Index \u2192 more volatility \u2192 forced bond sales \u2192 potential market mess \u2192 Fed swoops in to save the day. That\u2019s the theory!", "created": 1744129378336, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-fd37cd32ed447e3b", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:BAMLC0A0CM] WHERE TO SPOT THE LEVERAGE IN THE FINANCIAL SYSTEM? The leverage is ALWAYS in the weaker parts of the corporate sector. That is those firms that are essentially high yields, especially the worst part of the high yield. (which are C Level and lower) and among fallen angels which are a Trillion dollars (fallen angels are bonds that have gone from investment grade to below investment grade) That is THE LEVERAGE IN THE SYSTEM and that leverage is financed a lot by the SHADOW BANKING SYSTEM NOT THE TRADITIONAL BANKS So you cant see it in the balance sheets of the banks. As long as the economy is growing even if the balance sheets of corps are poor but you have revenues and you have some earnings growth, you can manage your debt just fine, you are not going to have a default. But now in addittion to balance sheet problem, you also have an PNL problem that if there was going to be a recession, of course the revenues and the profits of these firms that are already weak are gonna hit and thats where the credit spreads can widen. BUT WHEN THEY WIDEN THEY OFTEN WIDEN EXCESSIVELY NOT ONLY FOR HIGH YIELD BUT ALSO FOR HIGH GRADE. AND IN A RECESSSION, EVEN THE HIGH GRADE ARE GOING TO BE TO SOME EXTENT AT GREATER RISK. SO REALLY, CREDIT MARKETS ARE KEY  BCS WE HAVE A HUGE AMOUNT OF LEVERAGE IN THE CORP SECTOR WITH BALANCE SHEETS THAT WERE EXCESSIVE LEVERAGED BUT AS LONG AS PNL IS DOING WELL YOU DONT HAVE TO WORRY ABOUT IT. BUT WHEN THERE IS A SHOCK TO PNL AND YOU HAVE BAD BALANCE SHEETS THEN YOU HAVE A CREDIT CRISIS AND THE RECESSION BECOMES VERY SEVERE. IT COULD BE AS SEVERE AS 2008.", "created": 1743991855196, "pinned": false}

BUT WHEN THEY WIDEN THEY OFTEN WIDEN EXCESSIVELY NOT ONLY FOR HIGH YIELD BUT ALSO FOR HIGH GRADE. AND IN A RECESSSION, EVEN THE HIGH GRADE ARE GOING TO BE TO SOME EXTENT AT GREATER RISK. SO REALLY, CREDIT MARKETS ARE KEY  BCS WE HAVE A HUGE AMOUNT OF LEVERAGE IN THE CORP SECTOR WITH BALANCE SHEETS THAT WERE EXCESSIVE LEVERAGED BUT AS LONG AS PNL IS DOING WELL YOU DONT HAVE TO WORRY ABOUT IT. BUT WHEN THERE IS A SHOCK TO PNL AND YOU HAVE BAD BALANCE SHEETS THEN YOU HAVE A CREDIT CRISIS AND THE RECESSION BECOMES VERY SEVERE. IT COULD BE AS SEVERE AS 2008.", "created": 1743991844012, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-5d4a6d64eb2e5861", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:MME1!] Why It Mimics Global Liquidity: Emerging markets are highly sensitive to global liquidity because they rely on foreign capital inflows, often in USD. When liquidity is high (e.g., low FRED:RRPONTSYD, high FRED:WALCL), capital flows into emerging markets, boosting EEM. When liquidity tightens, capital exits, and EEM falls.\r\n\r\nCorrelation with Liquidity: In 2021, as global liquidity peaked, EEM hit a multi-year high near $55. By late 2022, as the Fed tightened (RRP spiked to $2.5 trillion via FRED:RRPONTSYD), EEM dropped to $33. It\u2019s also a liquid ETF, trading over 50 million shares daily.", "created": 1742454399247, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-520797a42a550c0e", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:NASDAQ:NQEM] Why It Mimics Global Liquidity: Emerging markets are highly sensitive to global liquidity because they rely on foreign capital inflows, often in USD. When liquidity is high (e.g., low FRED:RRPONTSYD, high FRED:WALCL), capital flows into emerging markets, boosting EEM. When liquidity tightens, capital exits, and EEM falls.\r\n\r\nCorrelation with Liquidity: In 2021, as global liquidity peaked, EEM hit a multi-year high near $55. By late 2022, as the Fed tightened (RRP spiked to $2.5 trillion via FRED:RRPONTSYD), EEM dropped to $33. It\u2019s also a liquid ETF, trading over 50 million shares daily.", "created": 1742454385008, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-a48ac98994a6bd5d", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:RRPONTSYD] When the Federal Reserve's Reverse Repo Facility hits its lowest inventory in 1,392 days, it indicates several key points about the liquidity in the financial system:\r\n\r\n- *Decrease in Excess Liquidity*: The Reverse Repo Facility (RRP) is used by institutions like money market funds to park excess cash overnight with the Federal Reserve in exchange for securities, typically U.S. Treasuries, at a set interest rate. A low inventory suggests there's less cash being placed into this facility, which could mean that there's less excess liquidity within the financial system or that funds are finding other uses for their cash, possibly due to better investment opportunities elsewhere.\r\n\r\n- *Shift in Investment Preferences*: This low level could also reflect a shift in where financial institutions are choosing to invest their cash. With possibly higher returns available in the private market or other investments like Treasury Bills, money might be moving out of the RRP into these alternatives, especially if short-term rates are attractive.\r\n\r\n- *Impact on Monetary Policy*: The RRP helps the Fed control short-term interest rates by setting a floor on them. A decrease in its use might suggest that the Fed's policies aimed at reducing liquidity or managing interest rates are having an effect. However, it could also mean that the financial system is adapting to the Fed's balance sheet reduction efforts, where the central bank is allowing its holdings of securities to mature without reinvestment, thereby draining liquidity from the system.\r\n\r\n- *Potential Market Implications*: Low inventory in the RRP might lead to:\r\n  - *Increased Market Volatility*: Less liquidity can sometimes lead to higher volatility in financial markets as there's less of a buffer for sudden changes in market conditions.\r\n  - *Pressure on Short-Term Rates*: If the facility is used to set a floor under short-term rates, a significant drop in its usage might mean the Fed has less control over these rates, potentially leading to fluctuations.\r\n  - *Shift to Other Liquidity Sources*: Financial institutions might seek other avenues for overnight cash placement, potentially increasing demand for other short-term securities or affecting the repo market.\r\n\r\n- *Economic Signals*: This could also be an indicator of broader economic conditions, like a tightening in credit conditions or banks preparing for potenti

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-0c8a46c057c5b673", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:AVGO] Broadcom Inc. (AVGO) stands out in the tech industry for several key reasons, making it a unique and influential player:\r\n\r\n1. *Strategic Acquisitions*: \r\n   - Broadcom is renowned for aggressive mergers and acquisitions (M&A), skillfully integrating companies like CA Technologies (2018), Symantec\u2019s enterprise security division (2019), and VMware (pending regulatory approval as of 2023). These moves diversify its portfolio beyond semiconductors into enterprise software and cloud infrastructure.\r\n\r\n2. *Diversified Portfolio*:\r\n   - *Semiconductors*: A leader in designing chips for networking, broadband, wireless (e.g., Apple iPhones), storage, and industrial applications.\r\n   - *Software*: Post-acquisitions, it offers mainframe, cybersecurity, and virtualization solutions, creating cross-selling opportunities across hardware and software.\r\n\r\n3. *Financial Strength*:\r\n   - Consistent revenue growth and high profit margins (over 60% gross margins) due to proprietary technology and scale.\r\n   - Strong cash flow supports R&D, dividends, and debt management from acquisitions.\r\n\r\n4. *Leadership & Strategy*:\r\n   - CEO Hock Tan is known for operational efficiency and turning acquisitions into profitable units. The focus on \"mission-critical\" technologies ensures steady demand.\r\n\r\n5. *Innovation & Market Position*:\r\n   - Heavy R&D investment drives advancements in 5G, data centers, and AI. A vast patent portfolio solidifies its edge in connectivity and cloud infrastructure.\r\n\r\n6. *Shareholder Returns*:\r\n   - Reliable dividends and stock buybacks attract income-focused investors, with a history of outperforming the S&P 500.\r\n\r\n7. *Regulatory Navigation*:\r\n   - Despite challenges (e.g., blocked Qualcomm bid in 2018), Broadcom successfully navigates global regulations to expand its ecosystem.\r\n\r\n8. *End-Market Diversity*:\r\n   - Exposure to cloud computing, enterprise software, telecom, and consumer electronics reduces reliance on any single sector.\r\n\r\nIn essence, Broadcom\u2019s blend of strategic M&A, technological leadership, financial discipline, and diversified innovation makes it a cornerstone of modern tech infrastructure", "created": 1738940612968, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-b07d8e412f073ef1", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:CB] Chubb Ltd. operates as a holding company, which engages in the provision of commercial and personal property and casualty insurance, personal accident and accident and health (A&H), reinsurance, and life insurance. It operates through the following segments: North America Commercial Property and Casualty (P&C) Insurance, North America Personal P&C Insurance, North America Agricultural Insurance, Overseas General Insurance, Global Reinsurance, and Life Insurance. The North America Commercial P&C Insurance segment that includes the business written by Chubb divisions that provide P&C insurance and services to large, middle market and small commercial businesses in the U.S., Canada, and Bermuda. The North America Personal P&C Insurance segment offers affluent and high net worth individuals and families with homeowners, high value automobile and collector cars, valuable articles, personal and excess liability, travel insurance, and recreational marine insurance and services. The North America Agricultural Insurance segment is involved in comprehensive multiple peril crop insurance (MPCI) and crop-hail insurance, and Chubb agribusiness. The Overseas General Insurance segment caters for both commercial and consumer P&C insurance and services in countries and territories outside of North America where the company operates. The Global Reinsurance segment covers reinsurance business. The Life Insurance segment focuses on its international life operations. The company was founded in 1882 and is headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland.", "created": 1738617111875, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-e8a3a72baca890b4", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:STT] State Street Corporation stands out in the financial sector due to several distinctive features and contributions:\r\n\r\n1. *Leading Custodian Bank*: \r\n   - As one of the world's largest custodian banks, State Street safeguards over $40 trillion in assets, providing critical services like asset safekeeping, trade settlement, and regulatory compliance for institutional investors, including pension funds and ETFs.\r\n\r\n2. *Pioneer in ETFs*:\r\n   - Through State Street Global Advisors (SSGA), they launched the first U.S. ETF, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), revolutionizing investing. SPY remains one of the largest and most traded ETFs, cementing their leadership in the ETF market.\r\n\r\n3. *Asset Management Powerhouse*:\r\n   - SSGA manages trillions in assets, specializing in passive strategies and smart-beta products, catering to the growing demand for low-cost, index-based investing.\r\n\r\n4. *Technological Innovation*:\r\n   - Invests heavily in fintech, including AI and blockchain, to enhance services like real-time analytics and risk management. Their platforms, such as Charles River Development, support institutional investment workflows.\r\n\r\n5. *Global Reach*:\r\n   - Operates in over 100 markets, offering cross-border custody, foreign exchange, and regulatory expertise, making them a trusted partner for global institutions.\r\n\r\n6. *ESG Leadership*:\r\n   - Integrates ESG factors across offerings, with ESG-focused ETFs and active stewardship, influencing corporate practices through initiatives like the \"Fearless Girl\" campaign.\r\n\r\n7. *Historical Legacy*:\r\n   - Founded in 1792, their long-standing presence underscores reliability and adaptability, evolving from a local bank to a global financial giant.\r\n\r\n8. *Risk and Regulatory Expertise*:\r\n   - Excels in navigating complex regulations, providing clients with robust risk management solutions essential in today\u2019s compliance-heavy environment.\r\n\r\nIn essence, State Street\u2019s blend of custodial excellence, ETF innovation, asset management scale, technological prowess, and global ESG leadership positions it uniquely as a backbone of the financial ecosystem.", "created": 1738339243040, "pinned": false}

This integration provides *permanent capital*, reducing reliance on traditional fund lifecycles and enabling patient, strategic investments.\r\n\r\n3. *Permanent Capital Strategy*:\r\n   - Through structures like Athene, Apollo secures capital that isn't subject to redemption pressures, allowing for investments in illiquid assets (e.g., infrastructure, private credit) without the need for frequent exits. This model enhances returns and stability.\r\n\r\n4. *Diversified yet Credit-Centric Platform*:\r\n   - While Apollo spans private equity, real estate, and real assets, its *credit business* remains a cornerstone. It is a leader in corporate lending, direct origination, and structured credit, offering solutions in markets where traditional banks have retreated.\r\n\r\n5. *Innovative Corporate Structuring*:\r\n   - Apollo's 2021 merger with Athene created a *publicly traded hybrid entity* (NYSE: APO), blending asset management with insurance capabilities. This structure optimizes capital efficiency and aligns interests across stakeholders.\r\n\r\n6. *Leadership and Evolution*:\r\n   - Transitioning from Leon Black to Marc Rowan as CEO, Apollo has emphasized growth in insurance and credit. By managing Athene's assets, Apollo accesses a stable, long-term capital base from insurance premiums (often termed \"float\"), akin to Berkshire Hathaway's model. This integration provides *permanent capital*, reducing reliance on traditional fund lifecycles and enabling patient, strategic investments.\r\n\r\n3. *Permanent Capital Strategy*:\r\n   - Through structures like Athene, Apollo secures capital that isn't subject to redemption pressures, allowing for investments in illiquid assets (e.g., infrastructure, private credit) without the need for frequent exits. This model enhances returns and stability.\r\n\r\n4. *Diversified yet Credit-Centric Platform*:\r\n   - While Apollo spans private equity, real estate, and real assets, its *credit business* remains a cornerstone. It is a leader in corporate lending, direct origination, and structured credit, offering solutions in markets where traditional banks have retreated.\r\n\r\n5. *Innovative Corporate Structuring*:\r\n   - Apollo's 2021 merger with Athene created a *publicly traded hybrid entity* (NYSE: APO), blending asset management with insurance capabilities. This structure optimizes capital efficiency and aligns interests across stakeholders.\r\n\r\n6. *Leadership and Evolution*:\r\n   - Transitioning from Leon Black to Marc Rowan as CEO, Apollo has emphasized growth in insurance and credit. Rowan's vision expanded Apollo into a \"retirement services\" powerhouse, targeting demographic trends like aging populations needing annuity products.\r\n\r\n7. *Scale and Global Reach*:\r\n   - With over *$650 billion in AUM* (as of 2023), Apollo leverages its scale to execute large, complex transactions across North America, Europe

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-c1f1aafb7f218313", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:UNTAGGED] WHY HAS THE S&P500 OUTPERFORMED EVERY OTHER STOCK MARKET IN THE LAST CENTURY?\r\nThe U.S. stock market has significantly outperformed other global markets since the 2008 financial crisis due to a combination of *structural advantages*, *economic resilience*, *monetary policy*, and *sectoral dominance*. Below are the key factors driving this outperformance: \r\n1. **Dominance of Technology and Innovation* - *Tech Sector Leadership*: The U.S. is home to the world\u2019s largest technology companies (e.g., Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, NVIDIA, Meta), which have driven growth through innovation in AI, cloud computing, e-commerce, and digital services. These sectors have grown exponentially since 2008, far outpacing traditional industries. - *Global Reach*: U.S. tech giants operate globally, capturing revenue from emerging markets and developed economies alike. \r\n2. **Aggressive Monetary Policy* - *Quantitative Easing (QE)*: The Federal Reserve\u2019s unprecedented monetary stimulus after 2008 injected liquidity into the economy, lowering borrowing costs and boosting asset prices. The Fed expanded its balance sheet from ~$900 billion in 2008 to nearly $9 trillion by 2022. - *Low Interest Rates*: Near-zero interest rates (2008\u20132022) incentivized risk-taking in equities, particularly in high-growth U.S. stocks. - *COVID-19 Response*: The Fed\u2019s swift actions during the 2020 pandemic (e.g., slashing rates, corporate bond purchases) stabilized markets and fueled a rapid recovery. \r\n3. **Corporate Profitability and Buybacks* - *Strong Earnings Growth*: U.S. companies, especially in tech and healthcare, have consistently delivered robust earnings growth, supported by productivity gains, global demand, and pricing power. - *Stock Buybacks*: U.S. firms have aggressively repurchased shares, boosting earnings per share (EPS) and stock prices. For example, S&P 500 companies spent over $5 trillion on buybacks from 2009\u20132022. \r\n4. **Dollar Hegemony* - *Global Reserve Currency*: The U.S. dollar\u2019s status as the world\u2019s reserve currency attracts foreign capital during crises, creating a \"safe haven\" effect. Foreign investors often flock to U.S. assets during uncertainty, supporting equity valuations. - *Corporate Advantage*: U.S. multinationals benefit from pricing goods and services in dollars, reducing currency risk. \r\n5. **Demographic and Entrepreneurial Advantages* - *Immigr

For example, S&P 500 companies spent over $5 trillion on buybacks from 2009\u20132022. \r\n4. **Dollar Hegemony* - *Global Reserve Currency*: The U.S. dollar\u2019s status as the world\u2019s reserve currency attracts foreign capital during crises, creating a \"safe haven\" effect. Foreign investors often flock to U.S. assets during uncertainty, supporting equity valuations. - *Corporate Advantage*: U.S. multinationals benefit from pricing goods and services in dollars, reducing currency risk. \r\n5. **Demographic and Entrepreneurial Advantages* - *Immig

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-df4c40a878791769", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:UUP] UUP goes long the US dollar and shorts the currencies of major US trading partners using USDX futures. Specifically, the fund is shorting the euro, Japanese yen, British pound, Canadian dollar, Swedish krona and Swiss franc. The USDX's currency weights have been fixed since 1973: It departs from its benchmark by being heavily exposed to the euro, so positive moves in the euro will have strong, negative impacts on the fund. Structured as a commodities pool, UUP distributes K-1s and is marked-to-market at year-end.", "created": 1737586094658, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-12a0997e21d4add1", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:UNTAGGED] EURODOLLAR MECHANISM: A client (an Arab rich oil nation like the Saudia Arabia or UAE would deposit its oil revenues in Billions of dollar) with an overseas bank (Citigroup or Deutsche bank or Mistubishi). So, with that $1 Billion Dollar liability the bank can create a $1 Billion Deposit Asset which is A LOAN (customer deposits are a bank liability). Eurodollar banks take all these Arabs money and other sovereigns\u2019 money and large multinational money and these really big big companies money and they wash it through the Eurodollar system by extending loans and huge credit lines through the system to either sovereigns nations or large multinationals or just to other banks and dealers. So these offshore banking system (the Eurodollar system) has the ability to just print money (new dollars) by just extending new loans in dollars. These new loans extended (the new dollars printed) will then fund global growth and push global assets to new all time highs and may even push up inflation. THE EURODOLLAR SYSTEM JUST SPEWS MONEY AROUND THE GLOBE, IT\u2019S WHAT KEEPS GLOBAL MARKETS LUBRICATED BY INJECTING LIQUIDITY IN THEM. AND THAT\u2019S WHY THE EURODOLLAR SYSTEM FUNDING IS THE KEY FOR GLOBAL LIQUIDITY AND GLOBAL ASSET PRICES. AND THAT\u2019S WHY ITS REALLY REALLY IMPORTANT TO WATCH DXY AND US FED FUNDS RATE AND TREAURY YIELDS, QE AND QT BCS THAT\u2019S WHAT WHAT WOULD MAKE OR BREAK GLOBAL LIQUIDITY. THE NO ONE KNOWS HOW MUCH MONEY IS CIRCULATING AROUND THE EURODOLLAR SYSTEM BUT ITS ESTIMATED AT ABOUT A QUALDRILLION DOLLAR (THAT\u2019S 1000 TRILLION DOLLARS).", "created": 1737044310909, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-f58a44fc2f839aac", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:DXY] EVERYDAY YOU HAVE TO ROLL OVER YOUR POSITION IN THE EURODOLLAR MARKET.\r\nWhy in a crisis the us dollar spike and the Japanese yen or the problem currencies be crashing in the Eurodollar system and globally? SO AS A JAPENESE BANK YOU ARE SHORT $1 BILLION US DOLLAR AND YOU JUST GOT A MARGIN CALL. IT\u2019S JUST NO BUENO!   THIS IS WHAT YOU CALL A MARGIN CALL! SO AS A JAPENESE BANK YOU ARE SHORT $1 BILLION US DOLLAR AND YOU JUST GOT A MARGIN CALL. IT\u2019S JUST NO BUENO! - `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-2a585066467ee6bd", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:FEDFUNDS] LIQUIDITY IS CREATED BY RISING PRICES : PRICES GO UP LIQUIDITY IS NO PROBLEM, PRICES CRUNCH LIQUIDITY DISAPPEARS.\r\nThe Japanese and German banks they go seeking a foreign adventure and they extend a lot of credit.\r\nThe Eurodollar system works like a pawnshop: A Japanese bank take their banking reserves ( their banking reserves would be mostly in kind of very very short term  duration JGBs : Japanese gov bonds) and they approach their international banking counterparties from all over the world and then their international banking counterparties from all over the world and just like in the pawn shop: the Japanese banks would say: \u201c I have got a Billion dollars equivalent of Japanese JGBs cash how many dollars would you give me?\u201d and then their international banking counterparties (the underwriter of the pawnshop owner) say: \u201cyou know what I will give you No haircut so I will give you $1 Billion Dollar in cash\u201d and this NO HAIRCUT SCENARIO THAT CREATES PLENTY OF LIQUIDITY IN THE EURODOLLAR SYSTEM. In times of crisis we start seeing haircuts in the EURODOLLAR system grow larger and larger which dwindles liquidity in the Eurodollar system more and more. BUT KEEP IN MIND AS A JAPENESE BANK IN THIS SCENARIO WHEN YOU PRESENT YOUR JGBS TO BORROW DOLLARS YOU ARE EFFECTIVELY SHORT BOTH US DOLLAR AND US RISK FREE RATE, SO IF THE DOLLAR WAS TO SPIKE OR IF US INTEREST RATES WERE TO SPIKE THAT WOULD BLOW YOUR CARRY TRADE ESPECIALLY IF YOU ARE LEVERAGED WHICH MOST CARRY TRADERS ARE. ONCE THEY BORROW DOLLAR IN THE ABOVE SCENARIO THEY WOULD LEVERAGE TO THE MAX TO MAXIMIZE THEIR PROFITS BUT THAT MAKES THEM SUPER VULNERABLE TO DOLLAR SPIKES AND US INTEREST RATES HIKES AND THAT\u2019S WHY WHEN DOLLAR SPIKE OR US INTEREST RATES HIKE THAT BLOWS UP MANY CARRY TRADE WHICH CAUSE MANY OF THEM TO GET LIQUIDATED AND AS THE EURODOLLAR SEE RISK RISING THEY START INCREASING HAIRCUTS WHICH DWINDLES LIQUIDITY IN THE SYSTEM MORE AND MORE MAKING IT ALL THE SUDDEN POOF JUST DISAPPER.", "created": 1736866039298, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-aecbd4f6dc27ffbf", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:DXY] WHAT THE DOLLAR DOES ON THE GLOBAL STAGE IS THAT IT HIGHLIGHTS FOR YOU THE WEAKEST  SPOTS IN THE WORLD, IT HIGHLIGHTS THE COUNTRIES WITH THE BIGGEST FINANCIAL RISK (EURODOLLAR SYSTEM) NOT ECONOMIC RISK BUT FINANCIAL RISK (NOW FINANCIAL RISK IS GONNA BECOME AN ECONOMICAL RISK DOWN THE LINE BUT WHAT THE DOLLAR DOES FOR U IS THAT IT HIGHLIGHT THE WEAKEST SPOTS WITH THE BIGGEST FINANCIAL RISK IN THE EURODOLLAR SYSTEM). FOR EX: IF THE DOLLAR SURGE AGAINST CHINESE YUAN AND BRAZILIAN RIYALE AND KOREAN WON, OR JUST AGAINST A WHOLE BUNCH OF EMERGING MARKETS; IT\u2019S BASICALLY TELLING YOU THAT CHINA, BRAZIL, KOREA, OR THE EMERGING MARKETS ARE IN TROUBLE.\r\n\r\nTHE DOLLAR BASICALLY POINTS OUT THE WEAKEST FINANCIAL SYSTEMS IN THE EURODOLLAR.\r\n\r\nWHY GLOBAL INVESTORS ALWAYS FLOCK TO THE DOLLAR AND STAY INVESTED IN DOLLAR WHEN US RATES ARE HIGH \u201cMILKSHAKE THEORY\u201d? WELL IF US TREASURIES ARE OFFERING 5% YIELD AND IF THE DOLLAR WAS TO GO UP JUST 5% AGAINST THE FOREIGN INVESTORS CURRENCY THEN HE IS MAKING 10% RETURN RISK FREE, AND IF HE WAS TO INVEST IN THE S&P500 AND THE THE S&P500 GOES UP 25% AND THE DOLLLAR GO UP AGAINST HIS LOCAL CURRENCY JUST 5% WELL NOW HE JUST MADE 30%. MATTER OF FACT EVEN IF THE S&P500 WAS TO GO DOWN 5% IF THE DOLLAR APPRECIATE AGAINST HIS LOCAL CURRENCY 5% THEN HE WILL BE BREAKIGN EVEN AND HE WE WOULDN\u2019T BE DOWN 5%.", "created": 1736181997250, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-ecf8de8ab4ef925e", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:VIX3M] When vix is below 15 approaching its lowest historical points you have to sell some of your position to lighten up your position, or buy puts to hedge your position. Anything below 15 is pretty extreme for vix. And also that would be the perfect time to buy puts bcs if volatility is low the put option premium is gonna be much cheaper. In December 9th 2024 when vix was 13 that was the cheapest price to buy a put option  in the last 20 years. So having a process takes the guessing part out of it so when vix hits below 15 your process should be to automatically buy insurance against ur portfolio by buying put options. It's impossible to know exactly when vix is gonna spike but u know when vix is at or below 15 u know that it's not going much lower", "created": 1734966318274, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-8f5b402dd005b5c5", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:FEDFUNDS] WE SEE THE DOLLAR GOING HIGHER IN THE MIDDLE OF A DOWNTURN, RECESSION, CRISIS, DOLLAR SHORTAGES. THE DOLLAR KEEP SCREAMING HIGHER AS THE RISKS SEEMS TO GET WORSE AND WORSE AND WORSE. WHEN THE DOLLAR IS RIPPING HIGHER THAT SIGNALS THE EURODOLLAR IS CHARGING OTHER CURRENCIES A RISK PREMIUM TO PARTICIPATE IN THE GLOBAL MONETARY SYSTEM AND IT SIGNALS THE EURODOLLAR IS CHARGING A RISK PREMIUM BCS THINGS ARENT GREAT UNDER THE HOOD IN THE GLOBAL ECONOMY. THE DOLLAR BREAKING OUT HIGHER THAT SIGNALS THE RISK PREMIUM IS RISING. \r\nTHE DOLLAR GOES LOWER WHEN THE ECONOMY IS DOING BETTER AND VICE VERSA.\r\nTHE DOLLAR TRADING SIDEWAYS SIGNALS ITS WAITING FOR ONE SIDE OR ANOTHER TO EMERGE: MEANING THINGS ARENT LOOKING NEITHER GREAT NOR HORRIBLE UNDER THE HOOD FOR THE GLOBAL ECONOMY SO ITS TRADING SIDEWAYS WAITING TO TAKE OFF INTO THE POSTION THAT WOULD REFLECT THE POSITION THE GLOBAL ECONOMY WENT TO. \r\nTHE DOLLAR RISE WHEN THINGS ARE NOT DOING WELL. IT\u2019S A SIGN OF RISK OFF, DEFENSIVENESS. \r\nDXY SURGING IS MOST LIKELY DUE TO RISK PREMIUM IN THE EURODOLLAR SYSTEM AND NOT INTEREST RATE DIFFERENTIAL NOR POLICY DIFFERENTIALS.\r\nDXY IS LARGELY DERIVED FROM THE EURO SO ITS VERY IMPORTANT TO MONITOR RISK IN EUROPE AND TO MONITOR EURUSD ALONG DXY. \r\nAS EUROPE SLIDE FURTHER AND FURTHER ACCELERATING INTO A RECESSION THAT SHOWS HIGHER DEGREE OF RISK FOR MORE THAN JUST EUROPE. - `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-389e7710799108bc", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:BAMLEMCBPIOAS] IMPACT OF INTEREST RATES ON EMERGING MARKETS: \r\nInterest rates in advanced economies have increased at the fastest pace in 20 years, and that has made some emerging markets economy especially vulnerable. Let's look at why:\r\nTo start with, high global interest rates increase borrowing costs and many emerging markets survive on external financing for public spending. So when interest rates go up, it becomes more expensive for countries to pay back Their existing debt also becomes harder for countries to access new financing and could even increase the risk of default. Rising interest rates also make emerging markets more vulnerable to capital outflows. Since high interest rates in advanced economists means high returns there investors typically move capital away from emerging markets and that often entails buying advanced economies currencies, which reduces demand for currencies in emerging markets, creating depreciation. And ultimately inflation pressure now in the face of these pressures. How can emerging markets respond? The standard short term policy response is to increase domestic interest rates to incentivize investors to keep their money in emerging markets. But this isn't always optimal because it would lead to unnecessary economic contraction or even create Financial stability risks, especially if the increase is rapid. That's why at the IMF through our integrated policy framework, we advise countries on how to use a set of tools rather than just interest rates depending on each country's economic characteristics and the type of external pressures it is facing. For example, in some emerging markets. Foreign exchange markets relatively shallow So the exchange rate tends to be more sensitive to large transactions. If this country experience sudden large capital outflows due to the loss of investor appetite, they can sell foreign exchange reserve domestically to offset the negative impact on the exchange rate. And when a crisis is imminent, restricting capital outfalls can be an option too.  This policies , however, cannot substitute for a promising and stable growth model and prudent fiscal policy. So given the recent rise in interest rates over the world, what has been the effect on emerging markets? - `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-843fb3fb0bd03360", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:FEDFUNDS] WHAT are the signs of global collateral shortage in the financial markets?\r\nA global collateral shortage can significantly impact financial markets, and there are several key indicators that can signal when a shortage is occurring. These signs often appear as symptoms across lending, repo, and derivatives markets, as well as in risk and liquidity metrics. Here are the main signs of a global collateral shortage:\r\n1. Rising Repo Rates and Repo Market Tensions\r\n\u2022\tWhat to Watch: Repo rates often spike when there is a shortage of high-quality collateral, particularly U.S. Treasuries or high-grade securities.\r\n\u2022\tExplanation: In the repo market, institutions lend securities in exchange for cash, using collateral to back the transaction. A shortage of collateral (e.g., Treasuries) forces repo rates to rise as institutions pay a premium to borrow it. An extreme example was the spike in repo rates in September 2019, attributed to a mismatch in supply and demand for Treasury collateral.\r\n2. Increased Demand for Safe Assets (Flight to Quality)\r\n\u2022\tWhat to Watch: Rising demand and prices for safe assets like U.S. Treasuries, German Bunds, and high-quality mortgage-backed securities (MBS).\r\n\u2022\tExplanation: When high-quality collateral is in short supply, investors flock to safe-haven assets, pushing up prices and lowering yields on these instruments. This causes a shortage because institutions are less willing to lend out these assets, increasing competition for them.\r\n3. Widening Bid-Ask Spreads for High-Quality Assets\r\n\u2022\tWhat to Watch: Increased bid-ask spreads in secondary markets for Treasuries or other high-quality collateral assets.\r\n\u2022\tExplanation: A widening spread suggests that liquidity is tightening and that fewer participants are willing to part with their collateral. It becomes costlier to trade these assets as the demand-supply gap widens.\r\n4. Decreasing Issuance of High-Quality Debt\r\n\u2022\tWhat to Watch: Declines in the issuance of high-quality government or corporate debt, especially during times when market demand for these assets is high.\r\n\u2022\tExplanation: If government debt issuance does not keep pace with global demand for safe collateral, shortages can emerge. For instance, if governments reduce borrowing (such as in times of fiscal austerity), the amount of high-quality debt in circulation diminishes.\r\n5. Increase

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-68d0c7bcd290b718", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:FEDFUNDS] When interest rates go higher, bond prices fall. That includes us treasuries, and it was bond prices falling and the 40 year bond bull market coming to an end that would lead to the Dollar going higher. And what I mean by that is as Treasury prices fall, Interest rates rise as interest rates rise, It makes holding at least short-term US holdings (Treasuries and stocks) in US cash more attractive because you get paid a lot more to do so. As the federal funds rate goes higher, you get paid more to hold on to the dollars and since much of the world already needs dollars anyway to operate in the current monetary system and operate on the global stage, it just makes the dollar that much more attractive. And so as bond prices fall, not only as bond prices falling would make interest rates rise which would make the dollar attractive, but bond prices falling could have ramifications for markets all around the world. So not only would it, the higher interest rates be a catalyst to push the dollar higher, but the potential chaos caused by us Treasury price falling and us interest rates higher would push global investors to seek a safe haven bid into the united states dollar. SO AS YOU SEE BOND PRICES GOING UP THAT MEANS IT\u2019S A BOND SELL OFF THAT MEANS THE DOLLAR IS JUST GETTING MORE ATTRACTIVE BCS THE INTEREST RATE TO HOLD IT IS GOING HIGHER AND THE BOND SELL OFF WOULD CAUSE FEAR WHICH WOULD CAUSE GLOBAL INVESTORS TO RUN INTO THE US DOLLAR SAFETY AND TO BUY US ASSETS (STOCKS, TREASURIES, REAL ESTATE) WHICH WOULD CAUSE US STOCKS TO GO HIGHER.\r\nHIGHER INTEREST RATES ARE LIKE A MAGNET THEY ATTRACT CAPITAL FROM ALL OVER THE WORLD.", "created": 1730124852090, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-321f71ed57e05231", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:US02Y] INVESTORS GENERALLY LIKES BONDS BCS THEY ARE A SAFE INVESTMENT . THE PROBLEM IS THAT THAT RETURN IS GONNA BE OFTEN LOWER, MUCH LOWER THAN STOCKS. \r\nBOND YIELDS ARE A GREAT ECONOMIC BAROMETER: A CLIMBING TREASURY YIELDS SIGNALS INVESTORS ARE SELLING BONDS AND POSSIBLY BUYING STOCKS (BCS IF  INVESTORS ARE BUYING BONDS THEY ARENT BUYING STOCKS AND IF THEY ARE BUYING STOCKS THEY ARENT BUYING BONDS THAT SIMPLE): IF INVESTORS ARE CONFIDENT ABOUT THE ECONOMY, THE MIGHT NOT BE SATISFIED WITH THE SMALL RETURN THEY CAN GET FROM US GOV BONDS, THEY MIGHT CHOOSE TO BUY STOCKS INSTEAD. IF INVESTORS HAVE AN UNDERLYING SENSE OF AN IMPROVED ECONOMIC OUTLOOK THAT WOULD CAUSE RATES TO CLIMB UP (PROBABLY INVESTORS ARE SELLING BONDS TO BUY STOCKS). A DUMPING TREASURY YIELDS SIGNALS INVESTORS ARE BUYING BONDS TO RUN FOR SAFETY (IF THEY ARE BUYING BONDS THAT MEANS THEY ARENT BUYING STOCKS) THAT SIGNAL INVESTORS ARE NERVOUS ABOUT THE ECONOMY. \r\n\r\nBOND YIELDS ARE A KEY PART OF MONETARY POLICY THAT THE FED USES TO HELP INFLUENCE THE ECONOMY. \r\nBOND YIELDS ARE HEAVILY INFLUENCED BY THE OUTLOOK OF SHORT-TERM INTEREST RATES. FED HAVE ABSOLUTELY NO CONTROL OVER LONG TERM INTEREST RATES.\r\nWHEN FED WANTS TO RESTRAIN AN OVERHEATED ECONOMY, IT RAISES SHORT TERM INTEREST RATES. AND WHEN INTEREST RATES RISE, BOND YIELDS GO UP AS WELL. \r\nIF INFLATION IS HIGH, THE FED HAS A MANDATE TO KEEPING PRICES STABLE AND SO IT WILL TRY TO COOL THE ECONOMY BY RAISING BORROWING COSTS. HIGHER INTEREST RATES CAN SEND UP THE PRICES OF MORTGAGES AND OTHER LOANS WHICH WILL LIKELY SLOW DOWN CONSUMER SPENDING. \r\nHIGHER BOND YIELDS CAN HELP COOL DOWN THE ECONOMY WHICH SHOULD BRING DOWN INFLATION IN THE LONGTERM.", "created": 1729731314967, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-0e1cbfaa32d0925c", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:FEDFUNDS] HOW DO FED HIKING SHRINKS GLOBAL CREDIT AND GLOBAL LIQUIDITY IN THE EURODOLLAR MARKET? - `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-67a3d70fd72db3e2", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:FEDFUNDS] FINANCIAL STABITILITY IS A KEY CRITERIA FOR MARKETS .\r\nINTEREST RATES RISING ALWAYS LEAD TO VOLATILITY WHICH WOULD PUSH THE DOLLAR HIGHER.\r\nHIGHER YIELDS IN THE US PULLS CAPITAL INTO THE DOLLAR. \r\nIN A REALLY DEFLATIONARY SCENARIO TREASURIES WILL PUMP BCS INTEREST RATES WILL BE SLASHED TO NEAR 0.\r\nTHE US IS THE LEAST SENSITIVE COUNTRY IN THE WORLD FOR INTEREST RATES BCS THEY CAN PRINT WHATEVER THEY NEED. HIGHER INTEREST RATES CAUSE MORE PROBLEMS FOR THE REST OF THE WORLD THAN THEY DO FOR THE US.\r\nWHY IS IT BEST TO BE IN THE US THAN ANYWHERE ELSE IN THE GOOD AND BAD? THE DOLLAR SMILE THEORY: WHEN THINGS ARE REALLY GOOD, THE ECONOMY IS STRONG, INVESTMENT ASSETS ARE GOING HIGHER. SO PEOPLE FROM AROUND THE WORLD WANT TO PARTICIPATE IN THE US MARKET SO THEY SEND THEIR CAPITAL TO THE US, BUT IF THEY\u2019RE GOING TO SEND THEIR CAPITAL INTO THE US IT GETS PUSHED INTO DOLLARS. YOU NEED US DOLLARS TO BUY US ASSETS. SO A REALLY STRONG US ECONOMY IS TYPICALLY GOOD FOR THE DOLLAR. AND A REALLY BAD ECONOMY THEN THE DOLLAR IS SOUGHT OUT AS A SAFE HAVEN BASICALLY BCS IT\u2019S THE SAFEST IN THE STORM BUT ALSO BCS THERE\u2019S SO MUCH BORROWING IN DOLLARS THAT WHEN THINGS GO DOWN PEOPLE SCRAMBLE FOR THE DOLLARS SO THAT THEY CAN MEET THEIR DEBT OBLIGATIONS. BUT THERE IS A POINT IN THE MIDDLE KIND OF AT THE BOTTOM OF THE SMILE WHERE YOU KNOW IT\u2019S JUST NEUTRAL. THE DOLLAR CAN GO UP, THE DOLLAR CAN GO DOWN, IT\u2019S NOT ANY BIG DEAL. SO IF THINGS ARE GREAT IT\u2019S BEST TO BE IN THE US THAN ANYWHERE ELSE, IF THINGS ARE HORRIBLE IT\u2019S BEST TO BE IN THE US THAN ANYWHERE ELSE. BUT IF THINGS ARE JUST IN THE MIDDLE AND EVERYTHING IS FINE THEN IT DOESN\u2019T REALLY MATTER THAT MUCH.", "created": 1728314818724, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-ed1a2a384de42ac4", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:SPX] WHEN BOTH THE BOND MARKET AND THE STOCK MARKET GET BOTH CRUSHED EQUALLY AS BAD AT THE SAME DAY. THAT\u2019S A VERY VERY BAD SIGN THAT SMTHG IS GOING BAD IN THE PLUMBING SYSTEM. NORMALLY WHEN THE STOCK MARKET FALLS (RISK OFF RALLY: EVERYBODY PILES INTO THE SAFETY OF BONDS WHICH CAUSE BOND YIELDS TO DUMP AND BOND PRICE TO RALLY). SO WHEN EVERYTHING IS DUMPING AND THERE IS JUST NO ASSET TO FLEE TO AND EVERYTHING IS JUST DUMPING LIKE THERE IS NO TOMORROW MOST LIKELY IT\u2019S A FINANCIAL CRISIS. \r\nINFLATION BREATH MORE VOLATILITY.\r\nSO IF YOU ZOOM OUT YOU AREN\u2019T SEEING THE COINCIDENCE OF THREE DIFFERENT BLACK SWANS IN THREE DIFFERENT SPOTS, WHAT YOU ARE SEEING IS ONE META BLACK SWAN EVENT.\r\nWHEN MARKETS GET STRESSED EVERY PROBLEM THEY HAVE ALL APPEAR AT THE SAME TIME, SO YOU WOULD HAVE THE CURRENCY FAILING, YOU WOULD HAVE THE STOCK MARKET FAILING, YOU WOULD HAVE THE BOND MARKET FAILING, YOU WOULD HAVE THE YIELD CURVE INVERTING, THE FED GETS AGGRESSIVE. AND PEOPLE SAY OH BOY ALL THESE BLACK SWANS ARE ALL OCCURING AT THE SAME TIME. NO THIS IS WHAT HAPPENED WHEN MARKETS GET STRESSED. EVERYTHING GOES BAD AT ONCE! \r\nWHEN CRYPTO MARKETS ARE STRESSED THEN ALL THE BAD START TO BUBBLE UP AND POP TO THE SURFACE. FIRST, IT WAS TERRA UST, THEN CELESIUS AND IT ISN\u2019T THAT WE JUST RUN A SERIES OF UNCONNECTED EVENTS THAT SEEM TO HAPPEN RIGHT ALL AT THE SAME TIME. THEY ARE ALL CONNECTED. THEY WERE THE WEAK PARTS OF THE SYSTEM. AMPLE LIQUIDITY IN THE SYSTEM IS LIKE A MAKE UP THAT COVERS ALL THE IMPERFECTION PARTS OF THE SYSTEM.  SO WHEN YOU STRESS THE SYSTEM ALL THE WEAK PARTS BECOME A PROBLEM AT THE SAME EXACT TIME.", "created": 1727890419386, "pinned": false}
