- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-9fa576184567fa8f", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:DXY] WHAT\u2019S THE DOLLAR ROLE IN THE GLOBAL STAGE?  IT\u2019S THE LIQUIDITY PROVIDER FOR THE ENTIRE WORLD. THE DOLLAR IS THE FUNDING CURRENCY FOR THE ENTIRE GLOBE ON EVERYTHING FROM LOANS, SOVEREIGN DEBT, TRADE, INVESTMENT TO INFRASTRUCTURE. JUST EVERYTHING IS FUNDED IN DOLLARS. The demand for dollars Rooted in the relentless demand for dollars to service global debt (Both sovereign debt and Eurodollar market debt), to trade commodities, and build sovereign reserves to secure financial stability in uncertain times. Eurodollar market debt alone is about $14 Trillion as of Q2 2024. This mountain of debt creates a relentless bid for dollars to be able to service this debt especially in times of global stress as borrowers scramble to secure dollars to service their obligations. THAT\u2019S WHY THE DOLLAR STRENGTHENING HURT GLOBAL LIQUIDITY (ESPECIALLY WITH HIGH US INTEREST RATES) BCS EVERYTHING BECOMES MORE EXPENSIVE TO FINANCE.  AND THAT\u2019S WHY DXY  RISING TOO MUCH TOO FAST IS INCREDIBLY DESTABILIZING FOR THE ENTIRE SYSTEM BCS IT UNDERLIES (IT\u2019S THE FOUNDATION) FOR THE ENTIRE SYSTEM. SO ULTIMATELY A WEAKER OR A STRONGER DOLLAR CHANGE MARKET CONDITIONS JUST AS A LOW US INTEREST RATES OR HIGH US INTEREST RATE (ESPECIALLY 10 YEAR GOV BOND YIELD) CHANGE GLOBAL LIQUIDITY MARKET CDONTIONS ( A HIGH US10Y GOV BOND STRENGTHEN THE DOLLAR DUE TO GLOBAL DEMAND). A WEAK DOLLAR AND A LOW US INTEREST RATES ARE AN INCENTIVE FOR THE REST OF THE WORLD TO OBTAIN NEW DEBT. THE DOLLAR AND THE YEN ARE THE TWO BIGGEST LIQUIDITY PROVIDERS  IN THE WORLD. THE YEN IS VERY VERY IMPORTANT AND IT\u2019S THE SECOND MOST IMPORTANT CURRENCY AFTER THE DOLLAR.", "created": 1727625309121, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-78e9c6401f4290bd", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:CHMPMI] Switzerland's economy can be seen as a predictor of global economic trends for several reasons:\r\n\r\n1. Stable Financial Sector: Switzerland has a strong banking system known for its stability and resilience, making it a barometer for global financial health.\r\n\r\n\r\n2. Diverse Economy: The Swiss economy is diverse, encompassing finance, pharmaceuticals, and manufacturing. This diversity allows it to respond to global trends and shifts.\r\n\r\n\r\n3. High Export Levels: Switzerland is heavily reliant on exports, especially in high-value sectors. Changes in global demand can significantly impact its economy, offering early insights into global trends.\r\n\r\n\r\n4. Safe Haven Status: During times of uncertainty, investors flock to Swiss assets. Shifts in investment patterns can indicate broader economic changes.\r\n\r\n\r\n5. Economic Indicators: Swiss economic data, such as GDP growth, inflation rates, and consumer confidence, often reflect or precede trends in larger economies.\r\n\r\n\r\n6. Strong Trade Relationships: Switzerland maintains strong trade ties with both the EU and emerging markets, making it sensitive to shifts in global trade dynamics.\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\nThese factors contribute to Switzerland's role as an early indicator of potential shifts in the global economic landscape.", "created": 1727276029118, "pinned": false}

WELL WHEN YIELDS RISE THAT PULLS CURRENCY HIGHER (BCS INVESTORS ARE GETTING PAID MORE TO PARK THEIR MONEY IN THAT CURRENCY) \u201cWE SAW THAT VERY VERY CLEARLY IN 2022\u201d SO AS THE PRICE OF TREASURY FALL, THE TREASURY YIELD RISE AND AS THE TREASURY YIELD RISE THE DOLLAR RISES AND AS THE DOLLAR RISES THAT PUTS A HUGE AMOUNT OF PRESSURE ON THE REST OF THE WORLD. AND AS THE REST OF THE WORLD ARE UNDER IMMENSE PRESSURE AND THEIR ECONOMY START TO CRUMBLE THEN THEY HAVE TO START QE OR OTHER MONETARY POLICY MEASURES TO LIFT UP THEIR ECONOMY \u201cEXACTLY WHAT WE SAW IN 2022\u201d AND AS THE REST OF THE WORLD ECONOMY CRUMBLES AND THEY DO QE TO LIFT UP THEIR ECONOMY. THE REST OF THE WORLD ECONOMY CRUMBLING WILL CAUSE  A FLIGHT TO SAFETY  ( TO THE DOLLAR ) AND THEIR QE AND OTHER MONETARY MEASURES TO LIFT UP THEIR ECONOMY WOULD DEPRECIATE THEIR LOCAL CURRENCY AGAINST THE DOLLAR. SO THE LATER AND THE FLIGHT TO SAFETY WOULD JUST PUMP THE DOLLAR TREMENDOSLY.  SO WHAT STARTED AS PLOT TO DITCH THE DOLLAR ENDED UP STRENGTHENING THE DOLLAR EVEN MORE.", "created": 1727109131757, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-057e1d9e93601078", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:UNTAGGED] GLOBAL RISK OFF AND LIQUIDITY CRISIS SIGNS: YEN AND DOLLAR STRENGTHENING SIGNIFICANTLY VERSUS ALL THE OTHER CURRENCIES BCS IN A LIQUIDITY CRISIS THE BIG LEVERAGE GETS UNWIND AND THE BIG LEVERAGES ARE IN THE US DOLLAR AND THE JAPENESE YEN, AND YOU CAN SEE THE DOLLAR STRENGTHENNING IN THE DXY AND THE YEN STRENGTHENING IN THE JXY AND IN THE JPY/EUR AND THE JPY/GBP PAIRS. (THIS IS EXACTLY WHAT HAPPENED IN THE DOTCOM BUBBLE AND THE 2008 CRISIS)\r\nTHE YEN OR THE DOLLAR RALLYING IS REALLY BAD FOR GLOBAL LIQUIDITY AND ITS EVEN WORST IF THEY ARE BOTH RALLYING TOGETHER.\r\nBIG SWINGS IN CURRENCIES ARE A NIGHTMARE FOR CAPITAL MARKETS.\r\n\r\nIF THE YEN STRENGTHEN SIGNIFICANTLY THATS A RISK OFF SCENARIO.\r\n\r\nTHE ABSOLUTE WORST SCENARIO FOR GLOBAL ASSETS IF THE YEN AND THE DOLLAR RALLIES SIGNIFICANTLY TOGETHER AT THE SAME EXACT TIME VERSUS ALL THE OTHER CURRENCIES BCS THEY ARE THE TWO GLOBAL FUNDING CURRENCIES.\r\nFIAT CURRENCY LOSES VALUE OVER TIME BUT IT DOESN'T ALWAYS HAPPEN IN A STRAIGHT LINE AND WHEN LEVERAGE IS INVOLVED AND WHEN CARRY TRADE IS INVOLVED YOU CAN GET BIG SWINGS IN CURRENCIES AND BIG SWINGS IN CURRENCIES ARE A NIGHTMARE FOR CAPITAL MARKETS.\r\n\r\nIN ALL THE YEN CARRY TRADE YOU WILL SEE THE YEN STRENGTHEN AS ALL THE LEVERAGE UNWIND.\r\n\r\nPEOPLE GET INTO CARRY TRADE BCS THEY ARE SO LURING, THEY LOOK SO GREAT. BCS YOU BORROW AT 0% AND YOU INVEST IN SMTHG SAFE LIKE US TREASURIES THAT\u2019S YIELD 4%, SO YOU ARE BASICALLY GETTING 4% RISK FREE. AND YOU LEVER IT UP ONCE OR TWICE OR MAYBE THREE TIMES AND NOW ALL THE SUDDEN YOU ARE GETTING 12% FOR INVESTING IN SMTHG VERY SAFE. WELL THE PROBLEM IS IT\u2019S NEVER THAT SIMPLE AND IT\u2019S NEVER THAT EASY .\r\n THERE ARE MANY RISK THAT GOES WITH THE YEN CARRY TRADE: \r\n1-\tINTEREST RATES IS ONE RISK, \r\n2-\tTHE CURRENCY RISK IS ANOTHER RISK,.\r\n3-\tPOLITICAL RISK WHICH INFLUENCES BOTH CURRENCY RISK AND INTEREST RATES RISK SO THAT CAN HAVE A HUGE RAMIFICATION\r\n4-\t LIQUDITY RISK IS ANOTHER RISK BCS WHEN THESE CARRY TRADE BLOW UP USUALLY THEY BLOW UP WHEN THERE IS NOT THAT MUCH LIQUIDITY , SO IF YOU ARE INVESTED IN SMTHG THAT ISNT VERY LIQUID IN THE FIRST PLACE AND ALL THE SUDDEN IT\u2019S DROPPING IN VALUE. SO YOUR COST OF BORROW IS GOING UP AND THE VALUE OF  THE ASSET THAT YOU BOUGHT IS GOING DOWN BUT YOU CAN\u2019T SELL THE ASSET THAT YOU BOUGHT BCS THERE IS NO LIQUIDITY THAT\u2019S A GOOD WAY TO LOSE A LOT OF MONEY.\r\n5-\tLEVER

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-edbba1fb7b9ebccb", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:MME1!] When we say Emerging markets.  what are we referring to? Kenya or Qatar? Korea or Colombia? Commodity exporters or tech titans? Whether in equities or in bonds, the term \u201cemerging markets\u201d no longer does justice to the wide array of constituents within the various EM indices created to attract investor interest in the first place. What is the best definition of an emerging market? It is every country bar 10 \u201clegacy\u201d advanced economies. The EM residual accounts for 87 per cent of all countries, 85 per cent of the world\u2019s population and just under 50 per cent of global GDP. And it accounts for roughly a third of global financial assets. \r\nThe creation of investable emerging market indices starting in the late 1980s marked an important step in mobilizing foreign portfolio investments to developing economies. Deepening trade globalization and rising foreign investor interest in EM were mutually reinforcing. But it is increasingly unhelpful, if not misleading, to make the case for one of the benchmark emerging markets indices because their constituents would fail basic tests of similarity of asset behavior and diversity of returns. At the extreme, the current suite of benchmark indices is downright harmful because a country\u2019s economic and financial performance must go to negative extremes before the country falls out of the index. At various points in the past 25 years, Argentina, Venezuela, Turkey, Nigeria, Egypt and Ukraine have all been examples of countries that continued to receive residual inflows as part of the benchmark indices despite unsustainable economic policies. \r\nFor prospective index-based investors, China is an elephant in the room. It may not carry its economic weight in the various indices but its economic dominance and, more importantly, its distinct financial drivers set it apart from every other country in the index. The key point is not that China is too big or dominant in the investable equity and bond indices (though at nearly 25 per cent of the EM equity index, this is still a problem), but rather that the China investment boom, which fueled such strong growth in commodities demand, ended more than a decade ago. The other big problem for the EM universe is the dollar, given benchmark indices are based on the US currency. This makes those indices highly volatile compared with overall global benchmarks when the returns of underlying EM as

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-01521b5dc255f2da", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:DXY] WHY DXY IS THE MOST IMPORTANT CHART IN THE WORLD TO WATCH? The big problem for EVERY ASSET IN THE UNIVERSE IS THE DOLLAR, given indices are based on the US currency. This makes those indices highly volatile when the returns of underlying assets are effectively \u201cconverted\u201d to the US DOLLAR. The swings happen in both directions, but with a tendency towards extremely negative returns during periods of risk aversion. Please use the sharing tools found via the share button at the top or side of articles. For ex:  Backtests over various time horizons show that EM index returns are consistently higher when funded against a 50/50 basket of dollars and euros rather than fully in the US currency. It proves that indices would do much better even if they just partially insure against the dollar. BASICALLY SINCE THE INDICES ARE IN THE DOLLAR TERM IT\u2019S THE DOLLAR THAT EITHER MAKE OR BREAK THOSE INDICES, A WEAK DOLLAR WOULD MAKE THE INDICES AND A STRONG DOLLAR WOULD KILL THE INDICES.", "created": 1726582836894, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-5b170e91beae8d91", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:TWEXPYY] Why Taiwanese export growth can serve as a useful leading indicator for global business performance?  But why Taiwan? It all boils down to its pivotal role in the global supply chain. Taiwan sits at the upstream end which means it's among the first to see changes in manufacturers' orders signaling shifts in global business conditions ahead of time. During economic downturns, Taiwan's exports decline early on as downstream manufacturers will cut back on orders to prevent inventory buildup. Conversely, when the economy picks up in anticipation of consumer demand making a comeback manufacturers around the world start placing more orders and Taiwan feels the search first through its exports. This is why Taiwanese export growth can serve as a useful leading indicator for global business performance.", "created": 1724870918780, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-c0d530f0ed762fd3", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:SPX] key indicators for for assessing global stock market trends:\r\nGlobal stock markets have seen significant swings recently. Are we looking at short-term corrections or the precursors to a large-scale collapse? Here are the key indicators that drives global stock market trends: \r\n1-market sentiment : are stock markets getting overheated? For that, we can look at the proportion of stock indices above their 200 day moving average. When the ratio hits 80% or 90%, it typically signals overheated market sentiment and potential corrections ahead. However, there's a notable variation among countries, while 80% of the stocks on the NIKKEI and SENSEX are trading above the 200 day market. In Hong Kong, Brazil, Singapore and China: The number is actually around, or below 50%. Also overheating doesn't always translate to risk. When supported by strong fundamentals, pullbacks actually can present buying opportunities. \r\n2- valuation:  Are stocks getting too expensive and is that a problem? We can look at the market cap to GDP ratio to assess if stock market valuations are supported by actual economic growth. That said, a high ratio doesn't necessarily mean the stock market is overvalued. This is because a country's stock market composition does not always mirror its economy. Also, constituents of major indices can change dramatically over time. For example, Hong Kong's market cap to GDP ratio is at a staggering 1000%. This has to do with the fact that some Chinese companies may be listed in Hong Kong. But their production and operations are not in Hong Kong and are thus not reflected in Hong kong's GDP.\r\n3- Liquidity environment is another crucial factor influencing stock market performance. One useful indicator is the net proportion of Central banks cutting rates. A high rating indicates that more Central banks are in the rate cut cycle, which improves liquidity conditions. This means more capital flowing into the stock market and lower borrowing costs for companies. Both factors tend to boost stock market performance, as seen in the rallies in the chart. The proportion has been rising from its lows, and we can see the stock market has started to price in the anticipated rate cuts as well. \r\n4-macro fundamentals: Here we look at 2 more indicators. - `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-b8183c59743cb23d", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:XLP] How to beat the markets and learn the timing to invest in cyclicals and defensive sectors using the World MM Manufacturing cycle index. The stock market is intricate, but we can simplify it in the 2 key players: cyclical and defensive stocks. According to the MM Cyclical and Defensive Stocks Rotation Total Return Index chart: investing in cyclical and defensive stocks over the long-term yields impressive results. But how can we further optimize these returns?  We can use the characteristics of cyclical and defensive stocks to implement a tactical rotation strategy. Cyclical stocks fluctuate with the economic waves with examples: including the technology equipments and automotive sectors. People tend to purchase more cars and tech products when the economy is strong. On the other hand defensive stocks offer stability in uncertain times with examples like utilities and healthcare. Even in poor economic downturns, people still have need for essential goods and services. We can leverage the cyclical and defensive stock ratio and World MM Manufacturing cycle Index  to  Grasp the best investment timing. When the economy is booming and manufacturing is strong invests more in cyclical assets. When the manufacturing sector faces challenges, the defensive stocks take the spotlight. Based on this concept by strategically allocating investments we could have achieved a remarkable ninefold return over the past 30 years, outperforming the long-term performance of solely investing in either cyclical or defensive sectors. MM manufacturing cycle index is an important indicator to watch: if it continues Its ascend expect momentum amid cyclical stocks. But If it falters: brace for potential market risks in that case considers gearing towards defensive stocks for a more resilient portfolio. \r\nFrom 2009 Bottom to 2024: CYCLICAL  (CONSUMER DISCRETIONARY : XLY) have returned 1200% while S&P500 have returned 720% and (CONSUMER STAPLES: XLP) RETURNED 300%.", "created": 1724870677877, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-c2479819d96c9864", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:CL1!] THE MOST CRUCIAL INDICATOR FOR OIL PRICES:\r\nThe oil market is the heart of the global economy. Oil is a lifeblood of manufacturing. It influences everything from transportation to textiles. Oil prices are the pulse of the global economy and this chart holds the key to understanding its fluctuations, now let's look at the upper part of the chart. The YOY US Crude Oil inventory growth rate shows a cycle of approximately 3 to 4 years . A down ward trend signifies rising demand driving oil prices up. An uptrend on the other hand indicates oversupply, leading to a decline in prices. The chart (CRUDE OIL INVENTORIES YOY VS WTI CRUDE OIL FUTURES PRICE) illustrates the inverse relationship between crude oil inventories and prices, An intricate Tango that shapes the global economic conditions. During the summer travel season increases in gasoline demand will boost crude oil demand upstream, and in winter the need for  heating oil will impact crude OIL inventories as well.", "created": 1724787812961, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-5ce048aa2821ff7f", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:DXY] Forex or foreign exchange is the largest financial market in the world, with over $6 trillion traded daily.  But what exactly are we trading? And what makes this market so unique? Let\u2019s explore 4 different types of currencies and their personal characteristics:\r\n1-Policy driven currencies. These include the US dollar British pound, Japanese Yen and Euro, whose values are tied to their respective countries Monetary policies such as policy rate hikes or cuts, quantitative easing and quantitative tightening, for example, after 2008, the implementation of qe and QT policies has led to fluctuations in the US dollars value, it has been observed that following each instance of qe, the value of the US dollar falls while QT Tends to cause it to rise.\r\nThe exchange rate trends of policy-driven currencies are largely dependent on the monetary policies of their respective countries. Major global currencies such as the US dollar, British pound, Japanese yen, and euro usually fall into this category. Significant capital movements often occur when the monetary policies of these countries change, thereby affecting exchange rate trends. An example of which, in this case, is the US dollar.\r\nThe strength of the US dollar is closely correlated with changes in the US benchmark interest rate and global interest rates. When the US benchmark interest rate is lowered or the expectation of rate cuts increases, the interest rate differential between the US and other countries narrows, this causes an outflow of the US dollar to foreign markets, reducing the demand for dollars and leading to a drop in the US dollar index. Conversely, when the benchmark interest rate rises or the expectation of rate hikes increases, capital flows back to the US, driving up the demand for dollars and causing the US dollar index to rise.\r\n 2- Export-oriented currencies: these currencies are those where exports constitute a significant portion of the issuing country's GDP. Let's look at Taiwan, for instance, here we can see that Taiwan heavily relies on its export for its GDP. As more exports are made, we can see the value of its currency rising, whereas the opposite happens when less exports are made. \r\nExport-oriented currencies are those where exports constitute a significant portion of the issuing country\u2019s GDP. Examples include Taiwan (66%), South Korea (47%), and several Southeast Asian countries. An increase in the

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-d6428a7abf20d466", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:BAMLH0A3HYC] CREDIT SPREAD A KEY GAUGE OF CORPORATE DEFAULT RISK:\r\nSince The Fed has hiked interest rates to more than 5% last year, the financial world has been keeping an eye on how interest rates affect companies' abilities to pay back their loans today. We can dive into this topic by looking at 1 indicator:  credit spread, which is a crucial gauge for corporates Default risk that can offer clues to investor confidence and stock market trends. \r\nBut first what exactly is credit spread? Simply put it refers to the difference in the yield between 2 debt securities. What does credit spread tell us about corporate Default risk? When the economy hits a rough patch and businesses start to look shaky, heightened corporate default risk cause investors to pull their money out of high risk assets. Consequently, the prices of higher bond slide, pushing their yields higher and thus widening the credit spread. This had been the case of past economic down turns, such as the Dotcom bubble in 2002, the financial crisis in 2008 and the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. As the credit spread rose indicating more corporate defaults, the S&P 500 fell in tandem. But when the default fear ease higher bond prices recover, yields decline and the credit spread narrows. On the stock market front investors regain confidence, pushing stock prices back towards levels that reflect their assessment on how well companies are doing. In a nutshell, widening credit for us signals, growing concerns about companies not being able to pay back their loans while narrowing spread means Investors are not too worried. Fast forward to the present You can see the credit spread in the US is not on the rise, but remains relatively low at around 9 to 10% Suggesting low default risk a minimal chance of a credit crunch in the near term.", "created": 1724786922764, "pinned": false}
- `18:08:22` --- note 9817/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-217ff2e735621771", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:FRED:BAMLH0A3HYC] CREDIT SPREAD A KEY GAUGE OF CORPORATE DEFAULT RISK:\r\nSince The Fed has hiked interest rates to more than 5% last year, the financial world has been keeping an eye on how interest rates affect companies' abilities to pay back their loans today. We can dive into this topic by looking at 1 indicator:  credit spread, which is a crucial gauge for corporates Default risk that can offer clues to investor confidence and stock market trends. \r\nBut first what exactly is credit spread? Simply put it refers to the difference in the yield between 2 debt securities. What does credit spread tell us about corporate Default risk? When the economy hits a rough patch and businesses start to look shaky, heightened corporate default risk cause investors to pull their money out of high risk assets. Consequently, the prices of higher bond slide, pushing their yields higher and thus widening the credit spread. This had been the case of past economic down turns, such as the Dotcom bubble in 2002, the financial crisis in 2008 and the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. As the credit spread rose indicating more corporate defaults, the S&P 500 fell in tandem. But when the default fear ease higher bond prices recover, yields decline and the credit spread narrows. On the stock market front investors regain confidence, pushing stock prices back towards levels that reflect their assessment on how well companies are doing. In a nutshell, widening credit for us signals, growing concerns about companies not being able to pay back their loans while narrowing spread means Investors are not too worried. - `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-dd3e334adb4c5870", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:BAMLH0A0HYM2SYTW] CREDIT SPREAD A KEY GAUGE OF CORPORATE DEFAULT RISK:\r\nSince The Fed has hiked interest rates to more than 5% last year, the financial world has been keeping an eye on how interest rates affect companies' abilities to pay back their loans today. We can dive into this topic by looking at 1 indicator:  credit spread, which is a crucial gauge for corporates Default risk that can offer clues to investor confidence and stock market trends. \r\nBut first what exactly is credit spread? Simply put it refers to the difference in the yield between 2 debt securities. What does credit spread tell us about corporate Default risk? When the economy hits a rough patch and businesses start to look shaky, heightened corporate default risk cause investors to pull their money out of high risk assets. Consequently, the prices of higher bond slide, pushing their yields higher and thus widening the credit spread. This had been the case of past economic down turns, such as the Dotcom bubble in 2002, the financial crisis in 2008 and the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. As the credit spread rose indicating more corporate defaults, the S&P 500 fell in tandem. But when the default fear ease higher bond prices recover, yields decline and the credit spread narrows. On the stock market front investors regain confidence, pushing stock prices back towards levels that reflect their assessment on how well companies are doing. In a nutshell, widening credit for us signals, growing concerns about companies not being able to pay back their loans while narrowing spread means Investors are not too worried. - `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-4de30e569c5bb2a6", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:DXY] WHAT IS THE YEN CARRY TRADE? The yen carry trade has been going on for at least 20 years. According to the BIS its a $20 Trillion trade. And it's a very simple trade that's made effective bcs of japenese rates are at zero. So a Hedge fund would go to Japan put a little money down as collateral and borrow money at 0%, they then take that money which is in yen and they convert it to another currency for ex US Dollars and THEN ON LEVERAGE they buy another asset: Maybe they are buying Invidia, maybe they are buying the S&P500. Could be gold, oil, futures. They could be short bonds, long bonds. IT CAN BE ANYTHING AND IS EVERYTHING. THAT TRADE WORKS WELL BCS YOU ARE BORROWING AT 0% AND YOU ARE EARNING A RETURN ON YOUR INVESTMENT AND ITS LEVERAGED. THE PROBLEM IS WHEN YOU TAKE THAT MONEY OUT OF JAPAN AND BUY US ASSETS YOU ARE CONVERTING YEN TO DOLLARS SO YOU ARE ESSENTIALLY SHORT THE YEN. WHEN THE YEN IS UP %15 LIKE IN 08/03/2024 OVER 2 TO 3 WEEKS. SO THESE HEDGE FUNDS OR THESE CARRY TRADE INVESTORS ON A LEVERAGED BASIS ARE GOING TO BE DOWN 15% TIMES THE AMOUNT OF LEVERAGE SO THEY COULD BE LOSING 50%, 60%, %80%, 100% ON THEIR INVESTMENT JUST BCS OF THE YEN. AND WHEN THAT HAPPENS THE JAPENESE BANK WOULD  GO TO THE INVESTOR AND SAY WE NEED MORE COLLATERAL AND EITHER THE INVESTOR PUTS UP MORE MONEY OR COLLATERAL OR  THEY HAVE TO SELL THE ASSETS AND THATS WHAT WE SAW IN 08/03/2024 A FORCED LIQUIDATION. WHY IS THAT SO APPARENT? BCS IT'S HAPPENING IN THE MOST POPULAR SPECULATIVE SHORT TERM TRADING POSITIONS: INVIDIA, ETHEREUM ( THESE 2 HAVE BEEN TRADING VERY CLOSELY WITH THE YEN), AND THERE ARE MANY OTHERS LIKE MEGA CAPS , BITCOIN. THE RUSSELL 2000 HAS BEEN A POPULAR LONG TRADE IN THE RECENT WEEKS BCS THAT'S WHERE THE FAST MONEY IS. ANOTHER ONE: THE JAPENESE STOCK MARKET. IF YOU LOOK AT THESE ASSETS THEY ARE TRADING VERY CLOSE TO THE YEN ( THE YEN VS THE DOLLAR). WHAT'S DOING WELL? TREASURIES WHICH ARE TRADITIONALLY A SAFE HAVEN AND THAT'S WHERE MONEY IS FLOWING (THATS WHY US TREASURY AND JAPAN GOV BOND YIELDS DUMPED ON 08/03/2024).", "created": 1722961049292, "pinned": false}
- `18:08:22` --- note 9852/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-754b0ccd12f6eb63", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:UNTAGGED] why the yen strengthen following yen carry trade unwinding? And Why did the yen strengthen in the August 2024 crisis eventhough its usually the dollar that strengthen during crisis? The yen strengthened during the august 2024 crisis bcs bank of japan was hiking rates while every other central bank was cutting rates and we know the capital follows the currency with the highest rates thats gonna pay it the highest yield. Also, the strengthening of the yen has forced many yen carry trade to unwind and carry trade investors had to buy back the yen to pay their yen carry trade loans which strengthened the yen.", "created": 1722950210122, "pinned": false}
- `18:08:22` --- note 9855/12122  ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-64d0fcdd343ec6db", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:DXY] The dollar strengthening or weakening is what controls the flow of capital to the rest of the world and is what makes it capital flow either easy and efficient or hard and inefficient. - `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-5b3286ccc7d70a0b", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:DXY] The rest of the world gets their dollars from the United States. The only way the rest of the world can get dollars other than from the United States is by risking their own balance sheet and increasing loans in the Eurodollar market. So it's not to day that they can't do that BUT THEY NEED A GROWING ECONOMY AND A STRONG GLOBAL ECONOMY IN ORDER FOR THEM TO CONTINUE DOING THAT WITHOUT NEGATIVE CONSEQUENCES TO THEIR BALANCE SHEET. There is basically three places that the rest of the world can get dollars from: 1- Somebody in the united states can put dollars in a suitcase and physically fly them out of the country that's one way. 2- The other way they can get dollars is they can trade with the united states: they can send their goods to the united states and in and in return the united states can send them Dollars. 3- The third way that they can get dollars is they can extend dollar credit in the Eurodollar market but that third way that means they are RISKING THEIR OWN BALANCE SHEET AND IF THE PEOPLE THAT THEY LOAN THOSE DOLLARS TO ARENT ABLE TO GIVE THEM BACK TO THEM THEN THEIR BALANCE SHEET IS IN TROUBLE.", "created": 1722268398370, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-38a961f5dc4f0553", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:DXY] The US Dollar Supremacy: It's not the united states who has a debt problem, the rest of the world has a debt problem as well and they actually have in many ways a bigger debt problem than the united states bcs they owe debt in a currency that they can't print, they owe debt in a currency that they have to go out and buy and they have to buy that currency as it continues to get stronger versus their local currencies and that is why a strong dollar relative to its other currencies peers is such a problem for the world. Also, the rest of the world owes just as much, if not more in dollars as the US owes in dollars. Tbe difference is that the US has a money printing machine for dollars and the rest of the world doesnt and that's why despite all of the bailouts, all of the QE, all of  the money printing, all of the stimulus plans since 2008, the dollar has risen 25% versus peer currencies as far as the DXY goes, and it's up a lot more than that versus several other currencies. So think about all the things that has happened in the last 15 years, all the reasons that should have sent the dollar lower and yet it's up 25%, it has to do with the fact that the rest of the world has a debt problem as well and they owe debt in a currency that they don't have control over.", "created": 1722262616677, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-7b5259286474c06c", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:USHMI] REAL ESTATE PRICE BOOMS ARE CAUSED BY EASY CREDIT AND LOOSE FINANCIAL CONDITIONS: THE SIMPLEST BUBBLE CASE IS A REAL ESTATE BOOM THE TREND THAT PRECIPITATES IT IS THAT CREDIT BECOMES CHEAPER AND MORE EASILY AVAILABLE, THE MISCONCEPTION IS THAT THE VALUE OF THE COLLATERAL IS INDEPENDENT OF THE AVAILABILITY OF CREDIT AS A MATTER OF FACT THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN THE AVAILABILITY OF CREDIT AND THE VALUE OF THE COLLATERAL IS REFLEXIVE WHEN CREDIT BECOMES CHEAPER AND MORE EASILY AVAILABLE ACTIVITY PICK UPS AND REAL ESTATE VALUES RISE, THERE ARE FEWER DEFAULTS, CREDIT PERFORMANCE IMPROVES AND LENDING STANDARDS ARE RELAXED. SO AT THE HEIGHT OF THE BOOM THE AMOUNT OF CREDIT INVOLVED IS AT ITS MAXIMUM AND A REVERSAL PERCIPITATES FORCED LIQUIDATION DEPRESSING REAL ESTATE PRICES. YET THIS MISCONCEPTION CONTINUES TO OCCUR IN VARIOUS GUISES. NOT ALL BUBBLES INVOLVE THE EXTENSION OF CREDIT SOME ARE BASED ON EQUITY LEVERAGING.", "created": 1718406980005, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-def224f70877c7a1", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:UNTAGGED] SOROS BOOM AND BUST THEORY: SOROS BELIEVE THAT STOCK PRICES MOVE IN A BOOM BUST FASHION. FIRST ITS A SELF-REINFORCING TREND BASED ON CHANGES IN FUNDAMENTALS. BECAUSE OF REFLEXIVITY, A POSITIVE FEEDBACK LOOP IS CREATED WHICH SET THINGS IN MOTION. BCS THE MOTION IS SELF REINFORCING, IT DOESNT STOP AT SOME EQUILIBRIUM. THE TREND COULD BE UPWARD OR DOWNWARD, IT DOESNT MATTER (BCS OF REFLEXIVITY HIGH PRICES WILL CAUSE EVEN HIGHER PRICES AND NEW HIGH WILL CAUSE EVEN HIGHER HIGHS IN THE UP TREND AND LOWER PRICES WILL CAUSE EVEN LOWER PRICES AND NEW LOW WILL CAUSE EVEN LOWER LOWER LOWS). SECONDLY, THE INVESTING COMMUNITY WILL REALIZE THAT THE MARKET HAS MOVED TOO FAR AWAY FROM WHAT THE FUNDAMENTALS IN THE ECONOMY SHOULD ALLOW FOR. THIRDLY, THIS CAUSES THE OPINION OF INVESTORS TO CHANGE, AND THE MARKET WILL SELF CORRECT WITH A TREND REVERSAL. GIVEN SOME TIME, REFLEXIVITY WILL CAUSE POSITIVE FEEDBACK LOOPS THAT ARE SELF REINFORCING, BUT THIS TIME IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION. THE FORCE IS TOO STRONG TO STOP AT ANY EQUILIBRIUM THAT FUNDAMENTALS WOULD SUGGEST. THE MARKET HAS NOW GONE THROUGH BOTH A BOOM AND A BUST. SO PRICES IN THE STOCK MARKET DO NO MOVE TOWARDS AN EQUILIBRIUM, BUT RATHER THEY MOVE AWAY FROM IT, UNTIL IT BECOMES OBVIOUS FROM FUNDAMENTAL FACTORS THAT THE BOOM OR BUST HAS GONE TOO FAR. THEN THE PRICE DIRECTION CHANGES.", "created": 1718406506518, "pinned": false}
- `18:08:22` --- note 9919/12122  ---

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-8854910ec5183704", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:SPX] BOOM BUST BUBBLES THEORY GEORGE SOROS: EVERY BUBBLE HAS TWO COMPONENTS: AN UNDERLYING TREND THAT PREVAILS IN REALITY AND A MISCONCEPTION RELATING TO THAT TREND. A BOOM BUST PROCESS IS SET IN MOTION WHEN A TREND AND A MISCONCEPTION POSITIVELY REINFORCE EACH OTHER. THE PROCESS IS LIABLE TO BE TESTED BY NEGATIVE FEEDBACK ALONG THE WAY, IF THE TREND IS STRONG ENOUGH TO SURVIVE THE TEST THEN BOTH THE TREND AND THE MISCONCEPTION WILL BE FURTHER REINFORCED. EVENTUALLY MARKET EXPECTATIONS BECOME SO FAR REMOVED FROM REALITY THAT PEOPLE ARE FORCED TO RECOGNIZE THAT THE MISCONCEPTION IS INVOLVED. A TWILIGHT PERIOD ISSUES DURING WHICH DOUBTS GROW AND MORE PEOPLE LOSE FAITH BUT THE PREVAILING TREND IS SUSTAINED BY INERTIA: \"WE MUST CONTINUE DANCING UNTIL THE MUSIC STOPS\". EVENTUALLY A POINT IS REACHED WHEN THE TREND IS REVERSED IT THEN BECOMES SELF-REINFORCING IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION.", "created": 1718406377018, "pinned": false}
- `18:08:22` --- note 9922/12122  ---

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-f4505841580021db", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:DXY] WHY IS THE DOLLAR SO STRONG? THE DOLLAR IS COMPLETELY DIVORCED FROM THE FUNDAMENTALS THAT GENERALLY BACK UP FIAT CURRENCY.  HIGHER INTERNATIONAL MONETARY SYSTEM IS DRIVEN NOT BY THE FED BUT BY THE EURODOLLAR: BY MONEY THE BANKS LEND TO EACH OTHER SO THAT THEY CAN SUPPORT THE BALANCE SHEET AND LEND TO CUSTOMERS OR OFFER TRANSACTIONS TO CUSTOMERS IF THEY WILL AND THE MAIN TRANSACTIONS THE 800 POUND GORILLA IS APPROXIMATELY $1 QUADRILLION OF DERIVATIVES (OPTIONS, FUTURES, FORWARDS, SWAPS, SWAP OPTIONS)\"$1 QUADRILLION = $1000 TRILLION\". ALL OF THAT $1 QUADRILLION OF DRIVATIVES HAS TO BE BACKED UP BY COLLATERAL: \"IF IM A HEDGE FUND AND YOU ARE MORGAN STANLEY I CALL YOU UP AND SAY I WANT A  $5 BILLION TOTAL RETURN EQUITY SWAP WHICH IS BASICALLY A DERIVATIVE BASKET OF STOCKS AND I CAN BUY AND SELL STOCKS ALL DAY LONG UP TO $5 BILLION IT WILL BE NOTIONAL WHICH MEANS YOU WILL PAY ME THE PROFIT OR LOSS IN DIVIDENDS BUT I DONT ACTUALLY OWN THE STOCKS I JUST HAVE A $ 5 BILLION SWAP WITH YOU AND THEN YOU GO OUT AND MAYBE BUY THE STOCKS AND HEDGE YOUR POSITION YOU'LL DO THAT FOR ME IF IM A BIG ENOUGH HEDGE FUND OR SOVEREIGN WEALTH FUND OR INSTITUTION BUT YOU WOULD WANT COLLATERAL I DONT HAVE TO GIVE YOU $5 BILLION WORTH OF COLLATERAL I JUST HAVE TO GIVE YOU ENOUGH, A LITTLE BIT OF A FOUNDATION. AND THE MARK TO MARKET LOSSES SO IF I LOSE MONEY ON THAT DEAL I WILL GIVE YOU THAT MUCH COLLATERAL (THE COLLATERAL IS TO COVER MY LOSSES) UNTIL SUCH TIME AS WE CLOSE IT OUT, ETC. SO COLLATERAL IS THE KEY TO THE WHOLE QUADRILLION DOLLAR STRUCTURE. WHAT CAN BE COLLATERAL? WELL, BASICALLY SECURITIES BUT WE'RE IN A STAGE NOW WHERE BANKS AND HEDGE FUNDS AND OTHERS ARE BECOMING SUSPICIOUS OR NERVOUS ABOUT EACH OTHER'S CREDIT AND SO THESE ARE THE EARLY SIGNS OF A GLOBAL LIQUIDITY CRISIS WHICH IS DIFFERENT THAN A RECESSION AND DIFFERENT THAN A FINANCIAL CRISIS. THE LIQUIDITY CRISIS IS WHEN YOU GET READY TO TURN OFF THE LIGHTS. SO WHAT'S GOOD COLLATERAL? WELL, IT USED TO BE A LOT OF THINGS. BUT TODAYS BANKS ARE SAYING TO EACH OTHER OR TO THEIR CLIENTS: \" WE DON'T WANT YOUR CORPORATES, WE DON'T WANT YOUR STUPID MORTGAGES, WE ONLY WANT TREASURY NOTES THAT ARE LESS THAN 2 YEARS. WE WANT TREASURY NOTES MAYBE WITH A HAIRCUT OR GIVE US 6 MONTH BILLS, 4 WEEK BILLS, 30 DAY BILLS. WE ONLY WANT THE BEST, THE ABSOLUTE BEST MOST LIQUID FORM OF COLLATERAL. WELL OKAY, FIRST OF ALL, THERE'S A SCARCITY OF THAT, THERE'S A COLLATERAL SHOR

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-eed2397e5f62e5f1", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:SPX] THERE ARE TWO MAIN ECONOMIC POLICIES: ECONOMIC AND FISCAL: \r\n1- MONETARY POLICY IS THE DOMAIN OF A NATION'S CENTRAL BANK, IT INVOLVES MANIPULATING THE MONEY SUPPLY AND INTEREST RATES TO STEER THE ECONOMY.\r\n2-FISCAL POLICY IS THE GOV RESPONSIBILITY ADJUSTING TAX RATES AND GOV SPENDING TO INFLUENCE ECONOMIC ACTIVITY.\r\nTHE MAGIC HAPPENS IN THE INTERPLAY BETWEEN THESE TWO POLICIES FOR INSTANCE WHEN THE US RAISES INTEREST RATES THAT GENERALLY STRENGTHENS THE DOLLAR MAKING US ASSETS MORE ATTRACTIVE. THIS CAN PULL IN FOREIGN CAPITAL POTENTIALLY BOOSTING STOCK PRICES EVEN IN THE FACE OF TIGHTER MONETARY CONDITIONS BUT THE REAL POWER OF THESE POLICIES DOESN'T STOP AT A COUNTRY'S BORDERS.\r\nTHE ECONOMIC DECISIONS OF ONE COUNTRY CAN RIPPLE THROUGH THE GLOBAL MARKET STIRRING UP EVERYTHING FROM COMMODITY PRICES TO FOREIGN EXCHANGE RATES. CONSIDER THE FED TIGHTENING MONETARY POLICY BY RAISING INTEREST RATES, THIS DECISION IMPACTS NOT ONLY US MARKETS BUT IT ALSO REDIRECTS GLOBAL CAPITAL FLOWS. COUNTRIES WITH LOWER INTEREST RATES MAY SEE CAPITAL FLOWING OUT TO THE US WHERE RETURNS COULD POTENTIALLY BE HIGHER. THIS GLOBAL DANCE OF CAPITAL CAN TRIGGER SIGNIFICANT SHIFTS IN MARKET DYNAMICS INFLENCING ASSET PRICES WORLDWIDE. AS CENTRAL BANKS LIKE THE FED AND ECB STEER THEIR ECONOMIES THROUGH MONETARY POLICY THEIR DECISIONS ECHO AROUND THE GLOBE UNDERSTANDING THE INTEREST RATE DIFFERRENTIAL ALONG THE MONETARY AND FISCAL POLICIES DIFFERENTIAL HELPS ANALYSTS PREDICT WHICH REGIONS MIGHT ATTRACT MORE INVESTMENTS AND WHICH MIGHT FACE CAPITAL OUTFLOWS FURTHER MORE GEOPOLITICAL TENSIONS AND TRADE WARS ALSO PLAY INTO THIS FRAMEWORK. SO SOROS IMPERIAL CIRCLE THEORY PROVIDES A LENS TO VIEW THE GLOBAL ECONOMIC DANCE. IT HIGHLIGHTS THE INTERPLAY BETWEEN MONETARY AND FISCAL POLICIES AND THEIR GLOBAL IMPACTS, IT UNDERSCORES THE RIPPLE EFFECTS OF ONE COUNTRY'S ECONOMIC DECISIONS ON THE GLOBAL MARKETS AND IT OFFERS INSIGHTS INTO HOW CURRENT GEOPOLITICAL AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPEMENTS INFLUENCE GLOBAL MARKET DYNAMICS. UNDERSTAND GEORGE SOROS IMPERIAL THEORY EQUIPS INVESTORS TO BETTER NAVIGATE THE EVERCHANGING LANDSCAPE OF OUR INTERCONNECTED GLOBAL ECONOMY. \r\n\r\nGEORGE SOROS IMPERIAL CIRCLE THEORY: IF YOU HAVE A COUNTRY THAT HAS HIGH INTEREST RATES OR RELATIVELY TIGHT MONETARY POLICY RELATIVE TO OTHER COUNTRIES AND YOU HAVE A GOV IN THAT COUNTRY THAT IS SPENDING A LOT AND STIMULATING THE ECONOMY THAT IS A RECIPE FOR ASSET PR
- `18:08:22` --- note 9942/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---

COUNTRIES WITH LOWER INTEREST RATES MAY SEE CAPITAL FLOWING OUT TO THE US WHERE RETURNS COULD POTENTIALLY BE HIGHER. THIS GLOBAL DANCE OF CAPITAL CAN TRIGGER SIGNIFICANT SHIFTS IN MARKET DYNAMICS INFLENCING ASSET PRICES WORLDWIDE. AS CENTRAL BANKS LIKE THE FED AND ECB STEER THEIR ECONOMIES THROUGH MONETARY POLICY THEIR DECISIONS ECHO AROUND THE GLOBE UNDERSTANDING THE INTEREST RATE DIFFERRENTIAL ALONG THE MONETARY AND FISCAL POLICIES DIFFERENTIAL HELPS ANALYSTS PREDICT WHICH REGIONS MIGHT ATTRACT MORE INVESTMENTS AND WHICH MIGHT FACE CAPITAL OUTFLOWS FURTHER MORE GEOPOLITICAL TENSIONS AND TRADE WARS ALSO PLAY INTO THIS FRAMEWORK. SO SOROS IMPERIAL CIRCLE THEORY PROVIDES A LENS TO VIEW THE GLOBAL ECONOMIC DANCE. IT HIGHLIGHTS THE INTERPLAY BETWEEN MONETARY AND FISCAL POLICIES AND THEIR GLOBAL IMPACTS, IT UNDERSCORES THE RIPPLE EFFECTS OF ONE COUNTRY'S ECONOMIC DECISIONS ON THE GLOBAL MARKETS AND IT OFFERS INSIGHTS INTO HOW CURRENT GEOPOLITICAL AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPEMENTS INFLUENCE GLOBAL MARKET DYNAMICS. UNDERSTAND GEORGE SOROS IMPERIAL THEORY EQUIPS INVESTORS TO BETTER NAVIGATE THE EVERCHANGING LANDSCAPE OF OUR INTERCONNECTED GLOBAL ECONOMY. \r\n\r\nGEORGE SOROS IMPERIAL CIRCLE THEORY: IF YOU HAVE A COUNTRY THAT HAS HIGH INTEREST RATES OR RELATIVELY TIGHT MONETARY POLICY RELATIVE TO OTHER COUNTRIES AND YOU HAVE A GOV IN THAT COUNTRY THAT IS SPENDING A LOT AND STIMULATING THE ECONOMY THAT IS A RECIPE FOR AS

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-7df1390b367bc302", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:KRE] Utilities rally is money wants to move into a defensive sector obviously no matter what happens in the world we still need electricity, running water. when utilites dramatically outperform the S&P 500 smthg bad happens we saw that in the covid crash and we continue to see this over and over again : utilities will do very very well for a little window, they would outperform the stock market and then of course they crash with the stock market bcs smthg breaks in the system, smthg breaks in terms of some type of news or bad economic data. People moving into the defensive sector is definitly a bearish sign bcs they are just trying to preserve their capital by moving into the defensive sector. But what people dont realize and that's the same with investors who own high dividend paying stocks and etf who are told by advisors: \" Oh move into dividend stocks bcs you can just always get dividends.\" THE PROBLEM WITH DIVIDEND STOCKS AND UTILITIES IS THEY SELL OFF MORE THAN THE STOCK MARKET INDEX DOES SO IN CRISIS DIVIDEND STOCKS SOLD OFF MORE THAN THE S&P500 THEY DROPPED MORE THAN THE S&P500, UTILITIES STOCKS SOLD OFF MORE THAN THE S&P500 THEY DROPPED MORE THAN THE S&P500. THEY ARE VERY DANGEROUS BUT PEOPLE DONT REALIZE WHEN THE MARKET GOES INTO A BEAR MARKET THESE STOCKS GET HIT AND THE REASON IS THE MAJORITY OF STOCK MARKET INVESTORS ARE 50 PLUS AND THEY ARE ALL DOING THE SAME STRATEGY, THEY'RE BUYING UTILITIES AND DIVIDEND STOCKS AND THEY ALL FREAK OUT AND PANIC AT THE SAME TIME, THEY'RE ALL WATCHING THE SAME NEWS, THEY DON'T UNDERSTAND CHARTS AND THEY ALL DUMP THEIR STOCKS AND THEY ALL OWN THE SAME STOCKS SO THEY GET HIT HARDER THAN EVERYTHING ELSE SO DIVIDEND STOCKS ARE SUPER DANGEROUS IN CRISIS , UTILITY STOCKS ARE REALLY DANGEROUS TO HOLD DURING DOWNTURNS. BY HOLDING DIVIDEND STOCKS AND UTILITIES YOU ARE ACTUALLY HOLDING SMTHG MORE VOLATILE THAN THE STOCK MARKET ITSELF AND PEOPLE DON'T REALIZE IT UNTIL THEY TAKE THE LOSS AND THEN IT'S TOO LATE THEY HAVE ALREADY LOST THEIR MONEY. SAME WITH BANK STOCKS.", "created": 1717628949388, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-f0a74997537ad2f4", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:UNTAGGED] What's the difference between Trend and Momentum? A trend means it's trending in a Direction it's going up or down or sideways. A Momentum is how much power is behind it. Does that Trend have a lot of money moving it, is it moving faster, is it trending up faster, so it's kind of like the power behind smthg. It's like when you're in the ocean surfing you wait for those sets of waves those waves have momentum behind them they got power so when you identify a trend if there isn't a power behind it you don't want to jump on a little ripple even though we know there's a wave coming you should be like let's wait for smthg strong where there's a herd of people piling in driving that wave that , that price action of that asset you want to jump in where there's a swell coming.", "created": 1717613286907, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-c81400817ed3a2f7", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:SPX] NO ONE CAN TIME THE MARKET YOU JUST BUY AFTER A CONFIRMED BOTTOM AND YOU SELL AFTER A CONFIRMED TOP. YOU JUST RIDE THE TREND AND ONCE IT STALLS AND RUN OUT OF SPEED AND START TO GO DOWN YOU JUST GET OUT, YOU JUST LOOK FOR THAT SAFE MIDDLE ZONE BETWEEN THE BOTTOM AND TOP THEN YOU JUST SELL AND GET OUT. YOU HAVE TO GET IN LATER AFTER THE TREND HAS ALREADY HAD A NICE MOVE UP THATS WHEN THE TREND IS CONFIRMED AND THEN YOU RIDE IT UP AND THEN IT LOSES MOMENTUM AND YOU GET OUT. YOU DONT WANNA GUESS AND TRY TO PICK A TOP OR A BOTTOM: UNLESS YOU WANNA GUESS YOU HAVE TO GET IN AFTER A TREND STARTS AND GET OUT WHEN IT'S CONFIRMED THAT IT'S OVER OR ELSE EVERYTHING ELSE REALLY IS JUST GUESSING.", "created": 1717606746458, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-7ad09a1c0dcbee4e", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:FEDFUNDS] Retail Money Market Funds (WRMFNS) is a GREAT INDICATOR FOR Global liquidity trend Reversal: In the Repo Market: money market funds and other asset managers who are looking to make a little money without a lot of risk are the lenders. Thats why its important to focus on Money Market funds if they are just hoarding cash which means they arent lending , or their cash holding is decreasing which means they are doing more lending and flowing cash into the market instead of hoarding it. In the Repo Market: hedge funds, wall street traders, and banks who have a lot of assets but need cash on hand to fund their day to day trading are the borrowers.", "created": 1717599494574, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-77a60d381bfb9c9f", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:FEDFUNDS] How does the fed dries global liquidity by hiking rates? Hot money follow the highest interest rates around the globe. When the fed hike rates exponentially all the hot money from around the globe is gonna flow to the united states bcs they will be getting a higher return on their money and they don't have to take currency risk. When hot money (which is usually in dollar ) flow into a country it makes that country currency appreciate bcs that country have a higher foreign exchange reserves now. So when hot money flees row countries toward the usa. The hot money have to sell that local country currency and buy the dollar which appreciate the dollar and depreciate that local currency and also hot money fleeing those row countries is gonna make their foreign exchange reserves which is gonna weaken that local country's currency even further Bcs it's gonna decrease trust in that country local currency. That's the mechanism that lead to dollar pump and local currencies dump after fed raise rates.\r\n\r\nHot money is the one that cause currencies to pump or dump when central banks either hikes or cut rates. Hot money are in for a short gain they in for a quick buck and they invest in govs bonds and they usually follow the money meaning they usually invest in the countries with the highest rates. And that's the same exact mechanism of how a currency appreciate vs another when it's central bank raise interest rates higher than the others. Hot money sells the currency of the lower interest rate and buy the currency of the country with the higher interest rates. The buying and selling of the currencies doesn't only shift the supply of demand for the underlying currencies but it also change the foreign exchange reserves in both countries boosting foreign exchange reserves in the country with the higher rate boosting confidence in that country currency causing it to pump and diminish exchange reserves in the country with the lower rates which diminish confidence in that currency causing it to dump ( that's bcs most hot money is in us dollar, maybe a Lil bit of euro and yen but a very very small proportion). If hot money makes let's say 30% in the currency fluctuations alone they would immediately exit that country's market (they wouldn't wait for the profit from the gov bonds they would immediately sell that foreign gov bonds get the profit and exit the country). Hot money knows that this is a very r

There is a famous paper by george soros in 1984 called \"THE IMPERIAL CIRCLE\": from 1982 the dollar went on a tear really strong. \r\nIn 1982 US BOND yields tenure had peaked at 16% and inflation was cascading lower. The us had one of the most severe recessions, so treasuries dumped and whats more the Economy went to shit and fiscal policy was actually quiet aggressive, govs was spending like crazyy trying to pull the country out of the severe recession and the dollar appreciated. So you had the deficit spending (gov spending) kind of supercharging the private sector and US Economic growth became faster than the rest of the worldand that attracts speculative money \" I want to enjoy this party\" The carry was still high on rates bcs the US rates have been elevated. So the stock market starting pumping bcs its not just what you get on cash you are like : \" Im making 20% a year in US Stocks and i cant see it ending. And it all became self reinforcing so that bringout even more foreign capital coming in which bringout a stronger dollar. The hawks will tell you that the deificit spending is inflationary but the stronger dollar actually taming down inflation keeping it low which HAD PEOPLE INCLUDING FOREIGN INVESTORS BUYING TREASURIES WHERE THE YIELDS WERE HIGH BUT NOW YIELS ARE COMING DOWN FROM PEOPLE BUYING TREASURIES WHICH MEANS THE PRICE OF TREAURIES ARE GOING UP WHICH MEANS IM OVERSEAS AND I WANT TO BUY MORE BCS AS I BUY MORE THE DOLLAR GOES UP, THE INFLATION IS TAME, THE TREASURY PRICES GO HIGHER AND I WANT TO BUY EVEN MORE. AND THAT WENT ON UNTIL 1987. THE DOLLAR WAS REALLY STRONG AND THE FED WAS LIKE UH UH LIKE YOU KNOW THE US RATES BECAME QUIET HIGH AND THE REST OF THE WORLD REALLY STRUGGLING AND THEY ARE LIKE WE NEED HELP FROM THE WORLD CENTRAL BANKER BUT THE WORLD CENTRAL BANK IS THE FED (A DOMESTIC REGULATOR OF THE US) SO THE FED IS LIKE I REALLY CANT DO ANYTHING SO NOT THE CENTRAL BANKS BUT THE TREASURY MINISTERS AGREED TO A GLOBAL COORDINATED CURRENCY INTERVENTION TO TRY TO SELL DOLLARS AND THAT CAUSED THE BACKLASH FROM THAT FLASH CRASH IN OCTOBER 87 A WHOPPING 50% DUMP, MARKET DUMPED 20% IN ONE DAY. SO AGAIN THE US HAD TO INTERVENE AND COME IN TO RESCUE THE WORLD. A STRONGER DOLLAR SUCK FOREIGN CAPITAL INTO THE USA WHICH IS GONNA CAUSE A PUMP IN US STOCKS AND A PUMP IN US TREASUR

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-287fc2f34a36c8a3", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:DXY] HOW JAPENESE CARRY TRADE ARE MAKING A KILLING ? THEY ARE USING ALMOST THE SAME STRATEGY AS THE CARB LENDING BRITISH INVESTORS WERE USING IN THE 1920S. Carb lending is what fueled 1927 to 1929 us stock Boom and Bust: carb lending was used to lend people money to buy stocks on margin with 20% interest rates. Also while bank of england rate was 4%, Financial speculatives in uk (which was the global hedgemon at the time) saw that they can make a lot more money in carb lending. So they would make 20% off the bat to lend money to people to buy stocks on margin, plus they had their money parked in the US stock market which was just booming AND they also had the Dollar sterling rate in the favor  (sterling was weakening vs the dollar). BTITISH FINANCIERS WERE LIKE:  \"I DONT WANNA INVEST IN GERMANY, IM GONNA LEND PEOPLE TO INVEST INVEST IN THE US STOCK MARKET ON MARGIN I WILL BE GETTING PAID 20% AND MY MONEY IS GONNA BE THE US STOCK MARKET APPRECIATING\" SO THEY WERE TRIPPLE DIPPING. THIS  MASSIVE INFLUX OF MONEY FROM THE UK AND REST OF THE WORLD IS WHAT LIFTED THE US STOCK MARKET IN 1927 TO 1929 TO THE SKY BEFORE IT POPPED IN 1929.", "created": 1716473542341, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-fe7cc99854442d23", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:FEMB] DOLLAR WEAPONIZATION: EM dollar shortage: how fed dry global liquidity and squeeze EM? By Fed raising rates means us treasury yields go higher which means treasury prices go lower. Treasury prices going lower means the savings account that China and other EM has made in dollars purchases less commodities that are now going higher in price (due to dollar strengthening). That's why a strong dollar along a pumping oil and commodities is THE ABSOLUTE WORST NIGHTMARE FOR EM.\r\n\r\nUS TREASURIES ARE FOREIGN COUNTRIES SAVINGS ACCOUNTS.", "created": 1716321593887, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-e2d40de56f4ed8b2", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:EDV] EDV is an ETF of long-duration strips, which has a \"duration\" of roughly 1.5x TLT (24 vs 16 years). - `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-d4670d4e11969632", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:DXY] More Dollars are created every single day outside of America by the Eurodollar system than within the US Domestic Banking system.\r\n\r\nEurodollar system needs collateral you have to present collateral in order to obtain loans in the Eurodollar system think of it as being a pawn shop: You go to the window you present and the pawn broker will evaluate and consider your collateral and will then offer you dollars in exchange and that inject Dollars in the eurodollar system. The collateral the japenese use are Japenese bonds, cash yen and in return they get dollars and with those dollars they fund credit investment and expansion overseas in china and other countries. In china they fund large chinese manufacturning groups building factories there and more importantly they funded the incredible bublle in the chinese real estate. And you can clearly see the blow the japenese banks losses have endured from their Eurodollar loans to the Chinese market in the yen blowing up. You can almost name the day the yen untethering versus the dollar. The yen had sat at 110 versus the dollar for 3 decade today its 156, it became untethered and started blowing up once we started hearing about Evergrand and the other insolvent chinese property companies and so what happens in the pawn shop or the Eurodollar is that the counterparties to japan's banking system are now saying: \" Hey I'm kind of uncomfortable with holding these japanese Gov T-bills and actually i would prefer that you offer me some dollar collateral which will be short term US securities. As you have to respond to that this is a Daily operation you are requested to go back to the collateral window daily and what you are finding is at the margin there is a Huge sale of yen and purchase of dollar and that why you see weakness in the yen and strengthening in the dollar (THATS EXACTLY HOW CURRENCIES FLACTUATIONS UNRATTLES THE GLOBAL MARKETS BCS ITS JUST SHAKES AND UNRATTLES THE EURODOLLAR AT ITS CORE WHICH IS COLLATERAL BY REDUCING THE POOL OF COLLATERAL THEY ACCEPT AND GIVING MAJOR MAJOR HAIRCUTS THAT JUST DECREASE LIQUIDITY IN THE SYSTEM DRAMATICALLY AND IT JUST DECREASE DEMAND FOR JAPENESE AND ITALIAN AND GERMAN BONDS COLLATERAL AND INCREASE AND BOOST DEMAND FOR SHORT TERM US TREASURIES WHICH PUMP THE DOLLAR BCS YOU NEED DOLLARS TO BUY US SECURITIES AND IT DUMP US SECURITIES YIELD BCS THE YIELD DROPS AFTER ALL THIS MEGA PURCHASES OF THE US SECURITIES

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-dba4c7a8794d6522", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:GDXJ] How to play Gold Miners according to Hugh Hendry? People always say buy the miners buy the miners bcs people think that miners are gonna come up to the level of gold and exceed it bcs right now they are so cheap they are on sale that\u2019s the retail narrative but Hugh got a little bit different take based on his experience as a hedge fund manager. THE PRO WAY TO PLAY MINERS IS JUST TO AVOID THEM DON\u2019T BUY THEM AND JUST BUY GOLD INSTEAD. Gold miners don\u2019t offer NOTHING, and they have more price volatility which is to say they are riskier to own than gold itself and yet they had no upside and so you can really replicate the miners just by earning more gold, let\u2019s just consider that with regard to the last 20 years and the gold miners and the gold miners juniors haven\u2019t made no money zero money and it\u2019s been very very risky you\u2019ve had to endure quite savage draw downs yes it has recovered but it has recovered to being zero in terms of your return and yet over the same period gold and just unleveraged gold has gone up 600% . So for the last 20 years if you have just bought gold and short the miners you would be an investment legend, and there is an argument that miners can snap back and go up but  A PRO WILL ALWAYS OWN GOLD VERSUS OWNING THE MINING SHARES AND YOU HAVE THE LAST 20 YEARS CHART TO VALIDATE IT. IF YOUR THEORY HASN\u2019T WORKED FOR THE LAST 20 YEARS WHY IS IT GOING TO WORK FOR THE NEXT 20 YEARS YOU GOT TO KIND LISTEN YOU GOTTA LISTEN TO THE MARKET IT\u2019S YOUR FRIEND YOU CALL A FRIEND (THE MARKET) AND ITS SAYING TO YOU JUST BUY GOLD AND STAY AWAY FROM GOLD MINERS AND GOLD MINER JUINIORS. People say if gold go up 20% the miners always go up five times more than gold so miners would go up 100% if gold was to go up 20% so people always say it\u2019s a great times to move and buy miners when they are cheap and on sale. BUT IN REALITY APART FROM VERY SHORT PERIODS FOR LIKE 3 MONTHS INVESTORS WERE NEVER BETTER OFF HOLDING GOLD MINERS THAN GOLD ITSELF. SO DO YOU REALLY WANNA BE NERVOUS HOLDING THEM CHASING YOUR TAIL? DO YOU REALLY WANNA UBER INVEST? YOU DON\u2019T YOU WANNA INVEST WITH THE CLARITY OF THOUGHT IN MIND AND WITH CLARITY YOU WOULD ALWAYS INVEST IN THE METAL BEFORE YOU WOULD CONSIDER THE MINERS AND LIKE THAT YOU COULD HOLD IT FOR THE NEXT YEAR THE NEXT 2 YEARS ARGUABLY THE NEXT 10 YEARS WORRY FREE. THE MINERS HAVE BEEN TIMED OUT GOLD HAS GONE UP

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-ec33ad55012995f4", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:BAMLEMHBHYCRPIOAS] Why do countries devalue (weaken) their currency? A weaker currency means exporters costs go down RELATIVE TO their sales price and that means exporters can lower prices in their sales currency (dollars) which gonna lead to production increasing. Having lower costs relative to sales price is gonna encourage exports to lower their price. By charging lower prices that would encourage their out of the country clients to increase the order size and volume, which will help local manufacturers to increase sales volume and revenue and grab a higher market share. THE DOLLAR AS A RESERVE CURRENCY IS VERY DIFFERENT: FIRST OF ALL, WE DON\u2019T REALLY HAVE RESERVE CURRENCIES, WHEN YOU GO TO THE PEOPLE\u2019S BANK OF CHINA AND OTHER CENTRAL BANKS AROUND THE WORLD, THEY DON\u2019T HAVE $100 BILLS STACKED UP IN THE BASEMENT WHAT THEY OWN ARE U.S TREASURY SECURITIES WHICH ARE DIGITAL BY THE WAY, THE LAST PAPER TREASURY SECURITY WAS AROUND 1979. SO OF COURSE TREASURY SECURITIES ARE DENOMINATED IN DOLLAR BUT THEY DON\u2019T HAVE PHYSICAL DOLLARS IN A BANK ACCOUNT OR IN PAPER FORM BUT THEY OWN SECURITIES INSTEAD. NOW AS FAR AS THE DOLLAR AS A PAYMENT CURRENCY IS CONCERNED, THAT\u2019S RELATIVELY KIND OF EASY TO DISPLACE BUT THE DOLLAR AS A RESERVE CURRENCY THAT\u2019S ALMOST IMPOSSIBLE TO DISPLACE BCS THERE IS JUST NO OTHER ALTERNATIVE, THE ENTIRE GLOBAL MONETARY SYSTEM RUNS ON DOLLARS (TREASURIES). ITS MUCH HARDER TO DISPLACE THE DOLLAR AS RESERVE CURRENCY BCS IT\u2019S NOT REALLY ABOUT THE CURRENCY BUT IT\u2019S ABOUT THE SECURITIES MARKET. WHO HAS A SECURITIES MARKET THAT\u2019S BIG ENOUGH, LIQUID ENOUGH. YOU NEED ALL MATURITIES OF SECURITIES FROM FOUR WEEKS, 2 YEARS, 5 YEAR TO 30 YEARS. YOU ALSO NEED LARGE PRIMARY DEALERS, YOU NEED UNDERWRITING GROUPS WHICH IS WHAT THE PRIMARY DEALERS ARE, THOSE WHO MAKE MARKETS, YOU NEED SETTLEMENT, CLEARANCE, DISTRIBUTION, CUSTODIANS, HEDGING DEVICES, WHEN ISSUE TRADING, REPOS, FUTURES, OPTIONS, ETC. YOU NEED THE WHOLE NETWORK. THE USA HAS BEEN BUILDING IT FOR 230 YEARS SINCE ALEXANDER HAMILTON AND NO OTHER COUNTRY HAS IT OR ANYTHING ANYWHERE CLOSE TO IT.  THE GERMANS AND ITALIANS HAVE THEIR OWN SYSTEMS BUT THEY ARE NOT REALLY BIG ENOUGH.  AND ABOVE ALL, YOU NEED THE RULE OF LAW.  SO THEY DOLLAR KIND OF WINS THE RESERVER CURRENCY WAR, MEANING THE SECURITIES CROWN BY DEFAULT. THERE IS NOTHING ELSE THAT CAN COMPETE WITH IT, AND THERE WON\u2019T BE SOON. - `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-15d50c0849eb4487", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:QYLD] Covered call ETFs can indeed lose money under certain conditions. Here's why:\r\n\r\nMarket Decline: If the underlying stocks held by the ETF decrease in value, the ETF's net asset value (NAV) will also decline. Even though covered call ETFs generate income through writing call options, if the underlying stocks drop significantly, the losses on the stock holdings might outweigh the premiums earned from selling the call options.\r\nLimited Upside: Covered call strategies involve selling call options against the stocks held in the portfolio. While this generates income in the form of option premiums, it also caps the potential upside of the ETF's performance. If the underlying stocks experience significant price increases, the ETF's returns will be limited by the obligation to sell the stocks at the strike price of the call options, missing out on some of the gains.\r\nVolatility Risk: Covered call strategies are generally suited for sideways or slightly bullish markets. In highly volatile markets, the premiums earned from selling call options might not be enough to offset losses in the underlying stocks or could expose the ETF to significant losses if the underlying securities experience large price swings.\r\nInterest Rate Risk: If interest rates rise, the cost of borrowing to finance the purchase of the underlying securities may increase, potentially reducing the profitability of the covered call strategy.\r\nOverwriting Risk: Overwriting refers to the practice of writing call options on stocks the ETF already holds. If the market rallies sharply, the ETF might miss out on potential gains beyond the strike prices of the call options it has written.\r\nIn summary, while covered call ETFs can generate income through option premiums and provide some downside protection in volatile markets, they are not immune to losses, especially in scenarios where the underlying stocks decline significantly or if the market experiences unexpected volatility.", "created": 1715108825720, "pinned": false}
- `18:08:22` --- note 10256/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---

While this generates income in the form of option premiums, it also caps the potential upside of the ETF's performance. If the underlying stocks experience significant price increases, the ETF's returns will be limited by the obligation to sell the stocks at the strike price of the call options, missing out on some of the gains.\r\nVolatility Risk: Covered call strategies are generally suited for sideways or slightly bullish markets. In highly volatile markets, the premiums earned from selling call options might not be enough to offset losses in the underlying stocks or could expose the ETF to significant losses if the underlying securities experience large price swings.\r\nInterest Rate Risk: If interest rates rise, the cost of borrowing to finance the purchase of the underlying securities may increase, potentially reducing the profitability of the covered call strategy.\r\nOverwriting Risk: Overwriting refers to the practice of writing call options on stocks the ETF already holds. If the market rallies sharply, the ETF might miss out on potential gains beyond the strike prices of the call options it has written.\r\nIn summary, while covered call ETFs can generate income through option premiums and provide some downside protection in volatile markets, they are not immune to losses, especially in scenarios where the underlying stocks decline significantly or if the market experiences unexpected volatility.", "created": 1715108825720, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-f38b2e5dae069418", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:MBB] Mortgage backed securities ETF its the largest holding of jim bianco etf (WTBN) with a weight of 26% it offers a dividend yield of 3.69%\r\n\r\nElevated interest rates can negatively impact mortgage-backed securities (MBS) for several reasons:\r\n\r\nHigher borrowing costs: When interest rates rise, it becomes more expensive for homeowners to borrow money. This reduces the demand for new mortgages, slowing down the pace at which mortgage lenders originate new loans. As a result, the supply of new mortgages that can be bundled into MBS decreases.\r\nDecreased refinancing activity: Rising interest rates often lead to a decline in mortgage refinancing activity. Homeowners are less likely to refinance their existing mortgages when rates are higher than what they currently pay. Since refinancing generates prepayment of existing mortgages (when homeowners pay off their loans early), it can reduce the duration of MBS investments. This means investors may receive their principal back sooner than expected, which can be undesirable, especially if they were counting on a longer stream of interest payments.\r\nDecreased market value: As interest rates rise, the present value of future cash flows from MBS decreases. Investors demand higher yields to compensate for the increased risk of holding these securities, causing prices to fall. This inverse relationship between interest rates and bond prices is known as interest rate risk.\r\nPotential credit risk: Elevated interest rates may also indicate a weakening economy or higher default rates on mortgages. This can raise concerns about the credit quality of the underlying mortgage loans in the MBS pools, leading investors to demand higher returns to compensate for the increased risk of default.\r\nOverall, elevated interest rates can significantly impact the performance of mortgage-backed securities by reducing demand, decreasing refinancing activity, lowering market values, and raising credit risk concerns.", "created": 1715098377894, "pinned": false}
- `18:08:22` --- note 10298/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-dad1ffc757915e95", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:UGA] The United States Gasoline Fund, LP (USO) is an exchange-traded fund (ETF) that aims to track the movements of the price of gasoline, as measured by the movements of the price of futures contracts on unleaded gasoline traded on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX). It's designed to give investors exposure to the price of gasoline without directly trading futures contracts themselves. Investors can buy and sell shares of USO on stock exchanges, much like they would with individual stocks. It's important to note that investing in USO involves risks, including those associated with the volatility of commodity prices and the structure of the fund itself.", "created": 1714660056450, "pinned": false}

If there is any shift in the currency markets or interest rate markets particularly if their local currency get stronger compared to the dollar or their local central bank rate is going up compared to the Fed funds rate. Now they have to pay off an even larger debt than the amount they originally took for the loan So they rush to pay back the loan in the origin country as soon as their local currency strengthen or their interest rate start going up which CHOKE GLOBAL LIQUIDITY AND LOCAL ECONOMIES.", "created": 1711425223069, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-0a03294bbe1f3086", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:UNTAGGED] When we mention global collateral oftentimes, we think that's treasuries and treasury bills and that\u2019s an important part and the biggest part of it but it also consists of Japanese gov bills and italian gov bonds too. All these pieces fit together in a Eurodollar fabric that's often intermediated by US dealers. So it's not necessarily about US treasuries sometimes we see collateral problems begin in the smaller parts of the Eurodollar system that can then spill over across the entire Eurodollar system (Japanese gov bills and italian bonds and they are smaller parts of the Eurodollar when compared to Us treasuries collateral). So we have to pay attention to more than just US treasuries for warnings about where stresses might be building up in the overall global system. So as we all know we have the US treasuries, the Japanese gov bonds (that\u2019s a big one) but we also have the italian gov bonds.\r\n\r\nItalian gov bonds over the last half decade have become an important part of the overall Eurodollar system not just the Euro denominated secured lending system but the entire Eurodollar framework bcs italian gov bonds are the most plentiful source of gov bonds in Euro denominated collateral which means they crucially important for the operation of European banks and as we know the European banks are a huge part of the Eurodollar system, the Germans don\u2019t issue that many gov bonds. \"In Eur/USD fx swaps, US banks tend to borrow Euros from euro area banks, and then channel the euros to Japanese banks. In JPY/USD fx swaps, US banks borrow yen from Japanese banks and channel the yen to Euro area banks\" BIS.  According to European Repo Market survey: \" Italian gov securities expanded from 21.3% of ATS trading in December 2005 to 42.6% in December 2021.\" In other words, Italian instruments were backing nearly half of all Automatic trading systems (ATS) in repo, therefore a decent proxy of what's going on Euro-wide. Over the same timeframe, German bonds had been 44.6% of ATS repo back in 05 but were just 13.8% by june last year. With so much of the secured Euro markets depending upon italian sovereigns, what happens when spreads on italian sovereigns blow out to 250 bps above their German counterparts (BTPbund)?\". So if there's an issue with the biggest form of collateral in Euro denominator terms that\u2019s gonna be an issue for European banks therefore a source of potential pro

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-d51254fae1de57b0", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:FMMI2!] Emerging Market Industrial ETF can serve as a barometer for global liquidity conditions, reflecting investor sentiment, capital flows, economic growth expectations, credit conditions: During periods of ample liquidity, investors may be more willing to invest in riskier assets such as emerging market industrials, driving up the ETF's performance. Conversely, during periods of tight liquidity, investors may shy away from riskier assets, leading to underperformance of the ETF. 1- Capital Flows: Fluctuations in the assets under management (AUM) of the ETF can indicate capital flows into or out of emerging market industrials. Increased AUM may suggest growing investor interest and liquidity in the sector, while decreased AUM may indicate the opposite. 2- Economic Growth Expectations: The performance of industrial companies in emerging markets is closely tied to economic growth expectations. If the ETF performs well, it may suggest optimism about economic growth prospects in emerging markets, possibly driven by expectations of ample liquidity supporting investment and economic activity. 3- Credit Conditions: Liquidity in emerging market industrials can also be influenced by credit conditions. If liquidity is abundant, companies in the industrial sector may find it easier to access credit for expansion and investment, potentially leading to improved performance of the ETF.", "created": 1708880773099, "pinned": false}
- `18:08:22` --- note 10409/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-32b88b6d35ac4113", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:UNTAGGED] In Crypto we MUST FOCUS on tools that predicts future liquidity such as: (US30Y-US05Y, 10 year High Quality Market (HQM) Corp Bond par yield), Japan Nikkei index due to JPY role as a funding currency and japan role as a QE and QT provider for the Eurodollar Market, US PMI, and on Hong Kong small cap index (in USD) : it shows global investor Risk Appetite, if the global economy is Expanding or contracting ( Finland GDP YOY is a great tool to measure that since it the global largest producer of pulp and paper), Emerging Markets Growth (signals High Global liquidity), world manufacturing PMI, Emerging Markets small cap index fund (EEMS), High Yield Bonds, Micro Cap, Pacific small cap, ICE BOFA US HIGH yield index semi-annual yield to worst, Bond Global High Yield EX USA (PGHY), All world ex USA Net Total Return, \r\n\r\nEmerging Markets Growth signals High Global liquidity, Emerging Markets contracting signals low Global Liquidity.\r\n\r\nJapenese Yen is THE MOST IMPORTANT FUNDING CURRENCY IN THE WORLD. Japan is the EuroDollar system QE and QT provider. Japan loan Growth YOY is a great barometer to predict future liqudity in the Eurodollar global system.\r\n\r\nJapenese Stock Market is the MOST important stock Market in the world to watch for Bitcoin and Risk assets due to japan funding currency status for risk assets and for Japan Role as the Eurodollar system QE and QT provider.\r\n\r\nNikkei Along Emerging Markets small cap and Emerging markets liquid index can help us spot global liquidity trend reversal.\r\n\r\nBank of Japan Total Assets (Japan Balance sheet) expanding has ALWAYS triggered a Rally in Bitcoin and Crypto with about a 4 months lag.\r\n\r\nJapan Loan Growth YOY decreasing has ALWAYS drained liquidity from the Eurodollar system. We should consider it as A FLASH WARNING that crypto and bitcoin bull  market is about to end.\r\n\r\nNikkei Bottom in USD ALWAYS MARKED Bitcoin and Crypto Top and Bottom. - `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-3f0d7aeb488eeb17", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:USRI] The Redbook Index is a sales-weighted index of year-over-year (yoy) same-store sales growth in a sample of large US general merchandise retailers representing about 9,000 stores. It is a closely watched indicator of consumer spending, which is a major component of the US economy. The index is calculated by comparing sales in the current week to sales in the same week of the previous year. A positive index indicates that sales are growing, while a negative index indicates that sales are declining.  The Redbook Index is considered to be a leading indicator of retail sales, as it is released before the official retail sales figures from the US Census Bureau. As such, the Redbook Index can be used to gauge the health of the consumer sector and the overall economy.", "created": 1700412182825, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-bdf7490d1839d63f", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:DXY] Why does the Fed printing really doesnt matter? First bcs when the Fed prints it prints for the US and the rest of the world. Second, bcs this actually how the Fed printing actually works: Fed calls primary dealers and say we gonna buy ur 2 year notes or whatever type of bonds, here's a price. Done. Then the banks send the securities to the fed and the fed pays for it with money that comes out of thin air but here is the part that matters: what do the banks actually do with that money? They give it back to the FED in the form of excess reserves, bank deposit at the Fed. So that money never went anywhere, it was created , it is on the balance sheet, but it all went to the assets side which were securities and it never went into the economy. \r\n\r\nSo where does the money come from that runs the economy? it comes from the commercial banks, it comes from the mutliplier effect of lending in the commercial banks which shows in M2. \r\n\r\nCommercial banks has as much printing power as the Fed they just do it differently by lending money or by buying securities and paying for them with money that they create. \r\n\r\nEurodollars DO MATTER, Commercial banks DO MATTER. Thats how we run the system.\r\n\r\nWhy there is a global dollar shortage? How can we have a dollar shortage with the Fed printing trillions of dollars in new money? You have $1 Quadrillion of derivatives in the banking system as a whole , so that slice of $7 Trillion of M0 total money supply or $24 Trillion of M1 that has to support $1 Quadrillion of derivatives. And btw a Quadrillion is 1000 trillion.", "created": 1698776353288, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-cb8daa9d0ca80b4c", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:JP03MY] What's good collateral and why dollar spikes in crisis? in tough times like in 2008 banks tell each other: i dont want your corporates, i dont want your mortgages, i dont even want your 10 year notes. Give me at a stretch, i will give you I'll take a 2 year note with a haircut or what i really want are 30,60,90 day treasury bills. I just want very short term treasury bills, so you gotta go out and get the treasury bills and they are dollar denominated, which means you need dollars. So if you are a credit suisse or barclays or hong kong , shanghai or Deutsche bank, you dont live in the US, the country that prints the dollar, the US does but the European bank doesnt. \r\nSo there is this enormous demand for dollars, not bcs they love the dollar but bcs they need to buy dollar denominated collateral of a very high Quality to pledge as collateral to support the Quadrillion derivatives position and plus any other trading they are doing. What's going on in the Eurodollar in particular is a mad scramble for dollar based, high quality dollar based collateral and that's what's driving the dollar.", "created": 1698776302153, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-d7478347c8307c10", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:RPONTSYD] Repo Market provides the cash the financial firms need to run their daily operations, it provides a lot of the grease that keeps the financial market wheels spinning. When the Repo Market chokes and cash stops flowing trouble can reverberate through the economy Thats what happened in September 16,17 2019. And in response the Fed had to step in to help providing tens of billions of dollars to borrowers to keep the system running.  \r\nHow the Repo market operates? The Repo market operates like an overnight pawn shop. Imagigne 2 people Karen and Mark: Karen has $1000 and she would like to earn some fast interest on her money. Mark has a stack of treasury notes but no cash so he strikes a deal with karen, one treasury note for $100 but there is a catch. Mark has to agree to but that treasury note back tomorrow for $101. The difference between the price of the note on day one and day two thats the repo rate. If everything works properly Mark gets the cash he needs right when he needs it and karen makes some fast money. The Repo market functions in the same way you just have to replace the Karens with money market funds and other asset managers who are looking to make a little money without a lot of risk and replace the Marks with hedge funds, wall street traders, and banks who have a lot of assets but need cash on hand to fund their day to day trading. \r\nIn the repo market, karens and Marks all over the financial system lend back and forth for short periods, often overnight, and they do this at an enormous scale, usually, more than $1 trillion runs through it every day.\r\nOn September 16,17 2019 when rate spiked, the Karens were not willing to trade cash for securities at the usual rate, so the marks who need cash kept offering more and more and more until the FED arrived with help. When the Fed announced its surprise repo operations, people wanted to know why the did Karens stop lending? Experts pointed to two financial deadlines that sapped cash out of the system on the same night causing a crunch: September 16th was the cutoff for banks to submit their quarterly tax payments so a lot of money that they might usually lend in the repo market was being sucked out of their accounts and deposited into the Treasury. Spetember 16th was also the day that $78 Billion of Treasury debt was scheduled to settle which just means another chunk of cash was being turned into securities that day too.",
