- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-adbcb408858aae0c", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:RRPONTSYAWARD] Overnight Reverse Repo Rate (RRP) is the rate the Fed pays on reverse repo operation transactions where both commercial banks and money market funds swap cash for short term treasuries borrowed directly from the Federal Reserve at a certain rate.\r\nIt is typically used as a mechanism to set a floor on short term money market rates as it is the only rate that money market funds can earn directly from the Federal Reserve and therefore has the lowest credit risk out of all their allocation options.\r\nThe secondary use case has also been as a way to absorb liquidity out of markets and tighten financial conditions. This works because the cash deposited at the RRP facility is siloed away from the broad financial market and therefore makes for tighter liquidity conditions.", "created": 1678196724528, "pinned": false}
- `18:08:22` --- note 11574/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-ba2f2823d64d73dc", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:FRED:RRPONTSYAWARD] Overnight Reverse Repo Rate (RRP) is the rate the Fed pays on reverse repo operation transactions where both commercial banks and money market funds swap cash for short term treasuries borrowed directly from the Federal Reserve at a certain rate.\r\nIt is typically used as a mechanism to set a floor on short term money market rates as it is the only rate that money market funds can earn directly from the Federal Reserve and therefore has the lowest credit risk out of all their allocation options.\r\nThe secondary use case has also been as a way to absorb liquidity out of markets and tighten financial conditions. This works because the cash deposited at the RRP facility is siloed away from the broad financial market and therefore makes for tighter liquidity conditions.", "created": 1678196724528, "pinned": false}
- `18:08:22` --- note 11575/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-f56c8bc6806a5490", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:IORB] Interest on Reserve Balances (IORB) represents the overnight rate paid on reserves from depository institutions held at the Federal Reserve. It is the key rate that the Federal Reserve can directly set which allows them to guide the range they want to see for the FFR. They can do this through opportunity cost and arbitrage for banks as they decide what to do with their excess reserves. They can either lend it to other banks at the FFR or deposit it at the Fed and earn the IORB. If the IORB is higher than the EFFR, more flows will go towards the higher rate within which the spread can be closed through arbitrage, and vice versa. In practice, this IORB becomes the floor of the Federal Funds Rate range as it is the lowest rate offered that makes sense. Furthermore, the discount rate/discount window, which represents the rate commercial banks can use to borrow directly from the Fed and is typically only used in times of liquidity stress, acts as the ceiling to the FFR range.", "created": 1678195922825, "pinned": false}
- `18:08:22` --- note 11576/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-6f38b87cfb661acc", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:DTWEXBGS] Bull and Bear Markets are the result of the Central Banks policies, liquidity cycle, and the economy.\r\nThere are several factors that can contribute to a decline in the value of a currency:\r\n\r\nInflation: High inflation rates can lead to a decline in the value of a currency. When inflation is high, the purchasing power of a currency is eroded over time, meaning that people can buy less with the same amount of money. As a result, people may seek to hold other currencies that offer greater purchasing power.\r\n\r\nInterest rates: Central bank policies and changes in interest rates can have a significant impact on a currency's value. Higher interest rates can make a currency more attractive to investors seeking higher yields, which can increase demand for the currency and push up its value. Conversely, lower interest rates can make a currency less attractive to investors and lead to a decline in its value.\r\n\r\nPolitical instability: Political instability, such as political uncertainty, civil unrest, or political corruption, can lead to a decline in a currency's value. Investors may perceive the country as being riskier, and thus demand for the currency may decrease.\r\n\r\nEconomic indicators: Economic indicators such as GDP growth, trade balance, and employment can have an impact on a currency's value. Negative economic indicators can lead to a decrease in demand for the currency and a decline in its value.\r\n\r\nFiscal and monetary policies: Fiscal and monetary policies, such as government spending, taxation, and monetary policy decisions, can impact a currency's value. Expansionary policies such as increased government spending or monetary easing can lead to a decline in a currency's value, while contractionary policies can have the opposite effect.\r\n\r\nMarket sentiment: Market sentiment and investor behavior can also have an impact on a currency's value. If investors perceive a currency as being weak or unstable, they may sell it, leading to a decline in its value.\r\n\r\nOverall, a combination of factors can contribute to a decline in the value of a currency, and the relative importance of each factor can vary depending on the specific currency and economic context.", "created": 1673279253508, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-91757c7f2ccb6e2c", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:SOFR] Difference between SOFR and LIBOR (EURODOLLAR). SOFR is secured lending used overnight in the US, SOFR spot market is HUGE but its future market is TINY but it has been growing tremendously and projected to be as big or maybe overtake LIBOR futures market in 2023 . LIBOR is unsecured lending used OFFSHORE. LIBOR spot market is tiny but its futures market is huge. since SOFR is secured financing and LIBOR is unsecured LIBOR trades at a premium (rates are higher) than sofr bcs its Offshore unsecured lending. SOFR is used a ton in the spot market LIBOR is used a ton in the futures market. LIBOR was replaced by SOFR, LIBOR isn't used anymore.\r\nin Mid April CME is gonna take all EuroDollar position and swipe them to 3 Month SOFR positions. ( 3 Month SOFR is replacing libor mid april 2023)", "created": 1672679006931, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-f1228a69202e5e77", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:UNTAGGED] EFFR - SOFR ( Effective Federal Rate - SOFR) shows the balance between cash and collateral in the system (the presence or absence of collateral). - `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-e3a69255c634936c", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:RRPONTSYD] A reverse repurchase agreement (RRP) is a short-term transaction in which the Federal Reserve Bank of New York (New York Fed) sells securities to an eligible counterparty with an agreement to repurchase those same securities at a specified price at a specific time in the future. The counterparty earns a small interest payment on the transaction, which is currently set at the overnight interest on reserve balances (IORB) rate. RRPs are used by the New York Fed to manage the supply of reserve balances in the banking system and to implement monetary policy. When the New York Fed sells securities in an RRP, it injects reserves into the banking system. When the New York Fed repurchases the securities, it drains reserves from the banking system.\r\nHere is a simplified example of how a reverse repo transaction with the Fed works: 1- A large money market fund (counterparty) wants to invest its excess cash overnight.\r\n2-The counterparty contacts the New York Fed and expresses interest in participating in an RRP. 3-The New York Fed sells the counterparty $1 million in U.S. Treasury securities.\r\n4-The counterparty pays the New York Fed $1 million in reserve balances (The cash transferred by participants to the Fed effectively reduces the amount of reserves in the banking system, impacting the level of liquidity in the financial markets 'draining liquidity') .5-The New York Fed agrees to repurchase the Treasury securities from the counterparty for $1 million plus interest on the overnight reverse repo rate at a specific time in the future, typically the next day.6-At the end of the day, the counterparty has earned a small interest payment on its investment, and the New York Fed has temporarily injected reserves into the banking system.\r\nRRPs are a safe and secure investment for counterparties because the New York Fed is backed by the full faith and credit of the United States government. RRPs are also a very liquid investment, meaning that counterparties can easily sell their securities back to the New York Fed if they need to access their cash.\r\nRRPs are a valuable tool for the New York Fed to manage the supply of reserve balances in the banking system and to implement monetary policy. RRPs also provide counterparties with a safe and secure investment opportunity\r\n\r\nA Reverse Repo Spike means a DXY spike bcs Fed is sucking Dollars out of the market causing Dollar shortage.\r\nFED inje

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-058ceebd41cf87fc", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:KO] The quick ratio communicates how well a company will be able to pay its short-term debts using only the most liquid of assets. - `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-7cf2f8e1f0279150", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:KO] The four main areas of financial health that should be examined are liquidity, solvency, profitability, and operating efficiency. However, of the four, perhaps the best measurement of a company's health is the level of its profitability.\r\n1- EBITDA :This key profitability measure is one of the main measures of a company's financial health and ability to generate cash. EBITDA is short for earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization.\r\n2-Enterprise value/sales is a financial ratio that compares the total value of the company to its sales. The ratio is, strictly speaking, denominated in years; it demonstrates how many dollars of EV are generated by one dollar of yearly sales. Generally, the lower the ratio, the cheaper the company is.\r\n3-The price-earnings ratio, also known as P/E ratio, P/E, or PER, is the ratio of a company's share price to the company's earnings per share. The ratio is used for valuing companies and to find out whether they are overvalued or undervalued.\r\n4-The Price to Tangible Book Value ratio (PTBV) expresses share price as a proportion of the company's tangible book value reported on the company's balance sheet. Tangible book value is calculated by subtracting intangible assets (intellectual property, patents, goodwill etc.) from the company's book value.", "created": 1666799540975, "pinned": false}
- `18:08:22` --- note 11699/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-82dd40229d0f97bb", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:WORAL] Repo Market provides the cash the financial firms need to run their daily operations, it provides a lot of the grease that keeps the financial market wheels spinning. When the Repo Market chokes and cash stops flowing trouble can reverberate through the economy Thats what happened in September 16,17 2019. And in response the Fed had to step in to help providing tens of billions of dollars to borrowers to keep the system running.  \r\nHow the Repo market operates? The Repo market operates like an overnight pawn shop. Imagigne 2 people Karen and Mark: Karen has $1000 and she would like to earn some fast interest on her money. Mark has a stack of treasury notes but no cash so he strikes a deal with karen, one treasury note for $100 but there is a catch. Mark has to agree to but that treasury note back tomorrow for $101. The difference between the price of the note on day one and day two thats the repo rate. If everything works properly Mark gets the cash he needs right when he needs it and karen makes some fast money. The Repo market functions in the same way you just have to replace the Karens with money market funds and other asset managers who are looking to make a little money without a lot of risk and replace the Marks with hedge funds, wall street traders, and banks who have a lot of assets but need cash on hand to fund their day to day trading. \r\nIn the repo market, karens and Marks all over the financial system lend back and forth for short periods, often overnight, and they do this at an enormous scale, usually, more than $1 trillion runs through it every day.\r\nOn September 16,17 2019 when rate spiked, the Karens were not willing to trade cash for securities at the usual rate, so the marks who need cash kept offering more and more and more until the FED arrived with help. When the Fed announced its surprise repo operations, people wanted to know why the did Karens stop lending? Experts pointed to two financial deadlines that sapped cash out of the system on the same night causing a crunch: September 16th was the cutoff for banks to submit their quarterly tax payments so a lot of money that they might usually lend in the repo market was being sucked out of their accounts and deposited into the Treasury. September 16th was also the day that $78 Billion of Treasury debt was scheduled to settle which just means another chunk of cash was being turned into securities that day too. \r\n\
- `18:08:22` --- note 11703/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---

Experts pointed to two financial deadlines that sapped cash out of the system on the same night causing a crunch: September 16th was the cutoff for banks to submit their quarterly tax payments so a lot of money that they might usually lend in the repo market was being sucked out of their accounts and deposited into the Treasury. September 16th was also the day that $78 Billion of Treasury debt was scheduled to settle which just means another chunk of cash was being turned into securities that day too.

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-b46c90dad725fed6", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:GBGDG] Countries with the Highest Debt to GDP are the ones who gonna suffer the most in a rising Interest Rate and Stronger Dollar environment bcs most of the Gov Revenue will go just to service their Debt.\r\nAny given country\u2019s debt-to-GDP ratio can tell you a lot about its financial health as a whole.\r\nWhat Is the Debt-to-GDP Ratio?\r\nA country\u2019s debt-to-GDP ratio compares a nation\u2019s total public debt against its gross domestic product, or national income. A government\u2019s debt consists of how much it owes to external creditors like private lenders, international aid organizations, or central banks. Countries pay these debts via tax revenue, cost-cutting measures, or issuance of new currency (if the country has a sovereign central bank of its own). Gross domestic product consists of investment spending, exports, government spending, and consumption.\r\n\r\nYou shouldn\u2019t confuse debt-to-GDP with net-debt-per-capita (how much debt each citizen would owe if you were to divide it up equally) or budget-deficit-to-GDP (the yearly public deficit\u2014as opposed to public debt as a whole\u2014compared to that same year\u2019s GDP).\r\n\r\nMeet One of Your New Instructors\r\nSign Up\r\n\r\n4 Examples of Debt-to-GDP Ratios in Action\r\nDebt-to-GDP ratios have real-world benefits and consequences for countries. Consider these four nations\u2019 sovereign debts in relation to their GDP levels:\r\n\r\n1. Greece: During the Eurozone debt crisis in the 2010s, Greece was at particular risk of default. Ironically, several European countries with higher debt levels could issue enough Euros to help bail out Greece. They could do so because they had far lower debt-to-GDP ratios than Greece.\r\n2. Indonesia: This Southeast Asian country had a debt-to-GDP ratio of around 36.6 percent as of 2020. For an emerging market like Indonesia, this relatively low proportion of debt-to-GDP makes for an enticing investment to international investors and organizations.\r\n3. Japan: The national debt ratio for this country is significant. Japan clocked in at 254.13 percent debt-to-GDP as of the last quarter of 2020. The country can achieve debt sustainability because it has its own central bank and possesses most of its own assets. As such, it keeps interest rates low by lending to itself through the Bank of Japan.\r\n4. United States: Should the United States ever need assistance paying its external deb

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-da6c576551ccab9b", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:USM2] But what, exactly, is the money supply? Economists have used four main measures, known as M0, M1, M2, and M3. The four measures are nested: M3 includes M1 and M2; M2 includes M0 and M1.\r\n\r\nThe main feature distinguishing the four measures is the liquidity of their components (how easily one can exchange the asset for cash). The smallest and most liquid measure, M0, is strictly currency in circulation and money being kept by banks in reserves; hence, M0 is often referred to as the \"monetary base.\" M1 is defined as all of M0 plus the remaining demand deposits not in reserves as well as traveler\u2019s checks; it is often referred to as \"narrow money.\" M2 is everything included in M1 plus savings accounts, time deposits (under $100,000), and retail money market funds. M3 is everything in M2 plus larger time deposits and institutional money market funds. (Because the cost of estimating M3 was thought to outweigh its value, the Fed stopped reporting it in 2006.)", "created": 1666453856203, "pinned": false}
- `18:08:22` --- note 11719/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---
- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-0ea53726ec4eb02e", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:ECONOMICS:USM2] But what, exactly, is the money supply? Economists have used four main measures, known as M0, M1, M2, and M3. The four measures are nested: M3 includes M1 and M2; M2 includes M0 and M1.\r\n\r\nThe main feature distinguishing the four measures is the liquidity of their components (how easily one can exchange the asset for cash). The smallest and most liquid measure, M0, is strictly currency in circulation and money being kept by banks in reserves; hence, M0 is often referred to as the \"monetary base.\" M1 is defined as all of M0 plus the remaining demand deposits not in reserves as well as traveler\u2019s checks; it is often referred to as \"narrow money.\" M2 is everything included in M1 plus savings accounts, time deposits (under $100,000), and retail money market funds. M3 is everything in M2 plus larger time deposits and institutional money market funds. (Because the cost of estimating M3 was thought to outweigh its value, the Fed stopped reporting it in 2006.)", "created": 1666453856203, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-126d3a369041ba39", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:USM1] But what, exactly, is the money supply? Economists have used four main measures, known as M0, M1, M2, and M3. The four measures are nested: M3 includes M1 and M2; M2 includes M0 and M1.\r\n\r\nThe main feature distinguishing the four measures is the liquidity of their components (how easily one can exchange the asset for cash). - `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-6e848cb6f0ce5802", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:VIX] The Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) is a real-time index that represents the market\u2019s expectations for the relative strength of near-term price changes of the S&P 500 Index (SPX). Because it is derived from the prices of SPX index options with near-term expiration dates, it generates a 30-day forward projection of volatility. Volatility, or how fast prices change, is often seen as a way to gauge market sentiment, and in particular the degree of fear among market participants.", "created": 1665408477995, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-9b9a60d9a86ee929", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:SKEW] The SKEW index is a measure of potential risk in financial markets. Much like the VIX index, the SKEW index can be a proxy for investor sentiment and volatility. The Skew Index measures perceived tail-risk in the S&P 500. Tail-risk is a change in the price of the S&P 500 or a stock that would place it on either of the tail ends, or the far edges of the normal distribution curve. These price changes typically have a low probability.\r\nSKEW index is a leading indicator for VIX. After SKEW index spikes, vix index would follow with a Lag.", "created": 1665408200004, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-00172d5a925a01f6", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:WLRRAL] Reverse repurchase agreements are transactions in which securities are sold to a set of counterparties under an agreement to buy them back from the same party on a specified date at the same price plus interest. Reverse repurchase agreements may be conducted with foreign official and international accounts as a service to the holders of these accounts. All other reverse repurchase agreements, including transactions with primary dealers and a set of eligible money market funds, are open market operations intended to manage the supply of reserve balances; reverse repurchase agreements absorb reserve balances from the banking system for the length of the agreement. As with repurchase agreements, the naming convention used here reflects the transaction from the counterparties' perspective; the Federal Reserve receives cash in a reverse repurchase agreement and provides collateral to the counterparties.\r\n\r\nIn Reverse Repo Banks and Money Market Funds lend money to Fed Overnight and earn a yield for doing so. For example: if Banks and Money funds are earning 3% Risk Free from FED why would they want to invest in Risky Assets just to earn the same 3%.\r\nFed uses Reverse Repo as a mechanism to drain Liquidity. Reverse Repo can be looked at as Fed paying Banks not to lend.", "created": 1661982413421, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-13a008baec9a753b", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:CPFF] The difference between the 3-month commercial paper rate and the federal funds rate can provide insights into the liquidity and credit conditions in the financial markets.\r\n\r\nThe federal funds rate is the interest rate at which depository institutions (banks) lend funds to each other overnight to meet reserve requirements. It is set by the Federal Reserve and serves as a benchmark for short-term interest rates in the economy.\r\n\r\nThe 3-month commercial paper rate represents the interest rate at which corporations and financial institutions can borrow funds by issuing commercial papers with a 3-month maturity.\r\n\r\nWhen the 3-month commercial paper rate is higher than the federal funds rate, it suggests that corporations and financial institutions are paying a premium to access short-term funding compared to the interbank lending market. This could indicate tighter credit conditions, increased perceived risk in the corporate sector, or a higher demand for short-term funding.\r\n\r\nConversely, when the 3-month commercial paper rate is lower than the federal funds rate, it implies that corporations and financial institutions can access short-term funding at a lower cost compared to interbank lending. This could indicate more favorable credit conditions, lower perceived risk in the corporate sector, or a lower demand for short-term funding.\r\n\r\nThe spread between the 3-month commercial paper rate and the federal funds rate is closely monitored by investors, analysts, and policymakers as an indicator of credit market conditions and liquidity in the economy. It can provide insights into the availability and cost of short-term funding for corporations and financial institutions, which can have implications for economic activity and financial stability.\r\n\r\nShort-term liquidity spread: 3-month AA financial commercial paper or repurchase agreement (repo) rates minus 3-month Treasury bills (T-bills). If this spread is positive, then illiquid assets are paying higher rates to compensate for the lack of liquidity and thus there is a liquidity premium. This metric spiking is a sign for Low Liquidity in short term. This metric spiking is a sign for Low Liquidity in short term.\r\nSpike in SOFR signals low short term liquidity", "created": 1661639156113, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-f452edc700d3a8da", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:WRESBAL] Bank reserves are a great barometer of liquidity in the system.\r\n\r\nReserve balances are the amount of money that depository institutions, such as banks, maintain in their accounts at their regional Federal Reserve Banks. Reserve balances are made up of two components: 1-Required reserves: The amount of reserves that banks are required to hold by the Federal Reserve. Required reserves are a percentage of banks' deposit liabilities.\r\n2-Excess reserves: Any reserves that banks hold in excess of their required reserves.\r\nBanks use reserve balances to settle payments with each other and with the Federal Reserve. Banks also use reserve balances to meet their reserve requirements.\r\nThe Federal Reserve uses reserve balances to implement monetary policy. For example, the Fed can buy and sell government securities to banks, which affects the amount of reserve balances in the banking system. When the Fed buys government securities from banks, it injects more reserve balances into the banking system. When the Fed sells government securities to banks, it drains reserve balances from the banking system. Here are some of the factors that can affect reserve balances: 1-Federal Reserve monetary policy actions: The Fed's monetary policy actions, such as open market operations and reserve requirement changes, can affect the amount of reserve balances in the banking system. 2-Bank lending: When banks lend money, they typically create new deposits. These new deposits require banks to hold more reserves. 3-Currency withdrawals: When customers withdraw cash from their bank accounts, the banks lose reserve balances. 4-Government spending: When the government spends money, it typically deposits the money into banks' accounts. These new deposits require banks to hold more reserves.\r\nReserve balances are an important part of the US monetary system. They help to ensure that banks have enough money on hand to meet their obligations to customers and to the Federal Reserve.\r\nSecurities held by the FED YOY, Securities held by commercial banks YOY  and \r\nreserve Balances with FED YOY signals liquidity in the system. it predicts bitcoin and crypto TOPS and BOTTOM.\r\nThe reserves of a commercial bank consist of. deposits at the Federal Reserve Bank and vault cash.", "created": 1661608640821, "pinned": false}

They help to ensure that banks have enough money on hand to meet their obligations to customers and to the Federal Reserve.\r\nSecurities held by the FED YOY, Securities held by commercial banks YOY  and \r\nreserve Balances with FED YOY signals liquidity in the system. it predicts bitcoin and crypto TOPS and BOTTOM.\r\nThe reserves of a commercial bank consist of. deposits at the Federal Reserve Bank and vault cash.", "created": 1661608640821, "pinned": false}

This rate is equal to the Eurodollar base rate, adjusted for the maximum reserve requirements lenders are required to maintain on their Eurodollar deposits.\r\nEurodollar practically function as a reserve currency for the rest of the world.\r\nEurodollar = dollar deposits outside of the United states. Eurodollar system is a fractional system which means money gets loaned into existence: its a system where banks borrow money and issue credit based on their Dollar reserves.\r\nEurodollar works as long as it's in expansion of credit ( creation of more money) but when the system stagnate or contracts you get a risk of contagion where one big loan risks to wreck the whole system.\r\nBcs it's an unregulated market and  there is no central bank that can intervene to collaterize the system. 2008 was about Dollar shortage contagion in the EuroDollar that caused loans defaults and wrecked the whole system.\r\nEuroDollar is a Fractional reserve banking  system: meaning its a system where banks. hold only a fraction of their deposits in their reserves and loan the Rest: meaning for every $1 in bank reserve shadow banks overseas would issue $100 dollars in new credit. ($100 is used just an example for explanation).\r\n\"Move\" : Ice BOAMl US Bond Market Volatility Estimate Index: Indicator shows Liquidity in EuroDollar. Ice BOFA Emerging Markets High Yield Option Adjusted Spread. Also ICE BOFA Emerging Markets Corp Bonds yields also shows Liquidity in EuroDollar System: High yield signals very low Liquidity. Low yield signals High Liquidity in the system.\r\nForeign Govs and entities selling US treasuries and US Assets can be a sign of them starving for Dollar Liquidity. They sell Treasuries and Dollar Assets to get Liquid Dollars. Therefore, the global copper price can provide insight into the level of demand for industrial commodities, which can be an indicator of economic activity.\r\n\r\nGlobal economic growth: Copper is sometimes referred to as \"Dr. Copper\" because it is thought to have a close relationship with the global economy. As copper is used in many industrial processes, changes in its price can be a reflection of changes in global economic growth. For example, a rising copper price may indicate increased demand for copper in construction and manufacturing, which can be a sign of stronger economic growth.\r\n\r\nChinese economic activity: China is the world's largest consumer of copper, accounting for over half of global demand. Therefore, the global copper price can be a useful indicator of economic activity in China, particularly in the manufacturing and construction sectors.\r\n\r\nInflation: Copper is a key input in many industries, and changes in the copper price can have an impact on inflation. Higher copper prices can lead to higher costs for businesses, which can then be passed on to consumers in the form of higher prices for goods and services.\r\n\r\nOverall, the global copper price can provide important insights into the state of the global economy and industrial activity, as well as inflation trends. However, as with any commodity price, it is important to consider the specific factors driving changes in the copper price and to interpret it in the context of other economic indicators.\r\n\r\nA Sharp Drop in Global price of Copper  along Global price index of all commodities and Oil : signals a Black Swan event is about to happen.\r\nIt signals beginning and End of Global Bull and Bear Markets. - `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-3d8de3b37abbc058", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:PEZ] The best economic forecaster is the inside of the stock market. The performance of cyclicals versus defensive stocks that always leads the real economy it doesnt lag it. It shows you when you are getting an upturn so if you see cyclical stocks beginning to pick up thats a really good sign. Also yield curve steepening thats a good sign, also looking at monetary hedges: precious metals , bitcoin when they pump thats a good sign. Also Tech stocks should lead bcs they are long duration investments.\r\n\r\nA cyclical stock is a stock that's price is affected by macroeconomic or systematic changes in the overall economy. Cyclical stocks are known for following the cycles of an economy through expansion, peak, recession, and recovery. Most cyclical stocks involve companies that sell consumer discretionary items that consumers buy more during a booming economy but spend less on during a recession.\r\nCyclical stocks are generally the opposite of defensive stocks. Cyclical stocks include discretionary companies, such as Airlines and Hospitality companies, while defensive stocks are staples, such as Campbell Soup.\r\nCyclical stocks usually have higher volatility and are expected to produce higher returns during periods of economic strength.\r\nCompanies that have cyclical stocks include car manufacturers, airlines, furniture retailers, clothing stores, hotels, and restaurants. When the economy is doing well, people can afford to buy new cars, upgrade their homes, shop, and travel.\r\n\r\nWhen the economy does poorly, these discretionary expenses are some of the first things consumers cut. If a recession is severe enough, cyclical stocks can become completely worthless, and companies may go out of business. Cyclical stocks rise and fall with the economic cycle. This seeming predictability in the movement of these stocks\u2019 prices leads some investors to attempt to time the market. They buy the shares at a low point in the business cycle and sell them at a high point.", "created": 1661290608881, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-ea27c1355ab4b33a", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:RRPONTSYAWARD] The Reverse Repo facility is the tool the Fed uses to put a floor underneath interest rates.\r\n\r\nThe reverse repurchase agreement (reverse repo) rate is the interest rate at which the central bank borrows money from commercial banks and other financial institutions by selling securities, typically government bonds, with an agreement to buy them back at a later date. In other words, it is the interest rate paid by the central bank to absorb excess liquidity from the banking system.\r\n\r\nReverse repo transactions are used by central banks as a monetary policy tool to manage liquidity in the financial system. When the central bank raises the reverse repo rate, it incentivizes banks to lend money to the central bank instead of lending it to other institutions or individuals. This helps to reduce the amount of money available in the banking system, which can help control inflationary pressures.\r\n\r\nThe reverse repo rate serves as a floor for short-term interest rates in the economy because it represents the rate at which financial institutions can invest excess funds in low-risk assets, typically government securities. By adjusting the reverse repo rate, central banks can influence short-term interest rates and the overall level of liquidity in the financial system.\r\n\r\nIt's worth noting that the specific details and mechanics of reverse repo operations can vary across central banks and countries. The reverse repo rate set by a central bank is typically a tool to manage short-term interest rates and liquidity conditions in the economy, and it is separate from the policy interest rate (such as the federal funds rate in the United States) that is used to guide monetary policy.\r\n\r\nWhat would make the fed pivot is a problem in the funding market: treasury auctions, collateral agreements, reverse repo.", "created": 1661273472405, "pinned": false}

Treasury general account, DXY and Reverse REPO to drain liquidity.\r\n\r\nThe current interest rate system of the Federal Reserve consists of the following tools:\r\n\r\n1. Target range for the federal funds rate: The Federal Reserve sets an upper and lower limit for interest rates and commits to keeping the effective federal funds rate (EFFR) within this range. The Fed aims to steer steer interbank borrowing rates by adjusting the target range for the federal funds rate, thereby injecting or withdrawing liquidity from the market. Set by the FOMC, the overnight reverse repurchase agreement (ON RRP) offering rate represents the lower bound of the target range.\r\n\r\n2. SOFR and EFFR: The Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) and the effective federal funds rate (EFFR) are both overnight lending rates, where SOFR represents lending rates with Treasuries as collateral while EFFR is based on overnight loans without collaterals. Both rates are indicative of the tightness of the cash flow in the market.\r\n\r\n3. IORB: Interest Rate on Reserve Balances (IORB) is the interest rate the Federal Reserve pays to banks on reserve balances held at the Federal Reserve by depository institutions. IORB can incentivize banks to hold reserves or inject credit into the market. Both the IORB and ON RRP offering rate are tools the Fed uses to regulate short-term interest rates. The interest rate on excess reserves (IOER) and the interest rate on required reserves (IORR) have been replaced by IORB starting from July 29, 2021.\r\n\r\nWhen the SOFR and EFFR reach/surpass the upper limit of the target range, it means the cash flow is tight, and the Fed might ease monetary policy by lowering the IORB or the target range of the federal funds rate.\r\n\r\nThe Effective Federal Funds Rate (EFFR) is the rate of which unsecured lending occurs overnight between 1 bank and another. - `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-9750aa223a7bf569", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:US30Y] US30Y tells us about future US Growth and Inflation expectations. \r\nThe difference between the yield on a 30 year treasury and a 6 months treasury is almost an extra 30 years of risk. what is the risk? lets take default off the table, the real risk is inflation. If you loaning the money to the gov for 6 months how much less could it be worth even if you have 10% inflation over 6 months that only 5% that you lose but if you have 10% inflation iver 30 years by the time you get your money back there is nothing left. so when you have a higher inflation you need even a higher premium to loan the gov money for 30 years bcs u are taking 30 years of risk. Now what are the factors that determine the inflation risk? Its the size of gov deficits bcs the bigger the gov deficits are the more inflation that the gov is likely to create. so when you have large fiscal deficits you would expect to have a higher premium on longer term bonds. If the yield on a 6 months treasury is 5.5% and 30 year treasury yield is 4.7% thats not how a yield curve works its positively slopped. so just by looking at the average premium in 80s,90s and 2000s If the yield on a 6 months treasury is 5.5%, the 30 year treasury yield should be at least 7.5%.\r\n\r\nA spike in US10y and US30y yields are signs of stress in the US Bond Markets and a sign investors are selling those Bonds massively which cause the yield to spike.\r\n\r\nyou only gonna on the long term bonds if you think the FED is about to cut rates over the next couple of quarters.", "created": 1661087647632, "pinned": false}
- `18:08:22` --- note 11948/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-0a62b6d97db85c1a", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:UNEMPLOY] Big rise in the unemployment rate has been a warning signal for violent market declines.\r\nBuy the market aggressively when unemployment start to pick up strongly. - `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-ba419d7b64a1e75d", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:BAMLC0A4CBBB] Global Liquidity Crisis can be seen in Credit Spreads. \r\nThis indicator shows liquidity in the US Corporate Bond Market. Check \"Move\" indicator for a better picture of whats going to happen in the bond market. \"Bond\" precedes this indicator and shows the bigger picture of the bond market.\r\nMost corporate Bonds in the US market are BBB bonds. A downgrade of a BBB bond will turn it from an investment grade status bond to a junk bond status. BBB bonds reflects the US market. In a recession : when a Corp income falls then their ability to service their debt also falls causing its Corp bond to be downgraded by the bond ratings company (Moodys, s&p Fitch) The fundamental problem is that most of US Corp bonds half of them which are investment grade bonds are just one notch above the junk bond threshold so if they get downgraded all the investment grade funds ETF will be forced to sell them (bcs their ratings got lowered to a junk bond status while the investment grade bond funds are only for investment grade bonds \"highest quality of Corp bonds\") causing the company's credit spread to widens costing the Corp more to refinance its debt or pay off its debt later on . Bcs when it refinance a new debt it will be financed at the higher yield so its debt servicing costs will be higher. so unless it's revenue increases, to offset the higher debt servicing costs , the probability of the Corp default on its debt increases. This event would cause contagion. the market will panic, worrying about other companies getting downgraded so even companies which are sounds will see their credit spread increase so they could in turn be downgraded.\r\n\r\nSo the fact that there is soo much debt at the BBB bonds level can cause this avalanche effect of cascadation. This cascadation will cause major problems for equities.\r\nAs long as corporate health is good then the state of the debt market is good. When corporate health goes south, the bond market goes south. The bond market is bigger than the stock market by multiples.\r\nSo when the bond market is struggling the damage is felt throughout the entire economy.", "created": 1660663860745, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-555621dba5ee0723", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:UNTAGGED] Treasury yield curve is a short term bet on a long term rate.\r\n\r\nThe Eurodollar futures curve is a long term bet on a short term rate bcs EuroDollar future is like we're betting on what an overnight rate is going to be two years from now.\r\n\r\nYield Curve should NEVER be inverted. Yield Curves should be upward sloping just bcs of time value of money and uncertainty. If banks lend for a longer period of time or make further forward bet they should get a higher rate.\r\n\r\nIf yield Curves are inverted (downward sloping) thats bcs investors are betting that overnight rates are gonna be lower a year or two years from now.( and the only way for rates to be lower in the future if the economy gets into a recession and things get a lot worse).\r\n\r\nyield curves inversion implies that market is betting strenuously that something or a lot of things are gonna happen that will force FED to cut the rates. (Whether the FED wants to or not)\r\n\r\nUS10Y-US02Y inverts right before FED hike rate , and  when US10Y-US02Y un-inverts the Fed cuts rates.\r\n\r\nEvery Time The German Yield Curve inverted and went Below 0 a Global Financial Crisis followed.\r\n(known as the yield curve) predicts the future of markets and the Economy. It shows the future moves of the credit market and the economy with a 6 months lag. \r\nTreasury yield curve : a short term bet on a long term rate.\r\nEuro dollar curves should be upward slopping bcs of time value of money, uncertainty, if people lend u for longer period of time they should get a higher rate  The only explanation for eurodollar yield curving is that the world is going to a recession.  Things are about to get a lot worst.\r\nWe say the Yield is inverted once it crosses and goes below 0.", "created": 1660663077878, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-8340532421bd8362", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:MCRO] This ETF looks to offer investors a way to replicate the risk-adjusted return characteristics of two hedge fund strategies. These methods include; a macro strategy and an emerging markets strategy, both using ETFs to accomplish their objectives. As stated, the fund will not invest in hedge funds but rather in exchange-traded products in order to replicate the exposure of a hedge fund strategy. Although this actively managed fund costs more than a comparable index fund, it does offer investors a much less volatile play on global markets while producing a comparable return as a world benchmark. The fund could make for a solid choice for those looking for a highly uncorrelated product that offers exposure to a wide variety of asset classes in a single ticker. Just be aware that the expenses are pretty hefty but this is one case where the active management appears to actually add value as opposed to subtract.", "created": 1660595516160, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-b22189754954145c", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:SOFR] SOFR: is a broad measure of the cost of borrowing cash overnight (Limited to overnight transactions only) collateralized by U.S. Treasury securities in the repurchase agreement (repo) market. The global price of money is now being priced based upon the quantity of available collateral in the global markets which just so happens to be US Treasuries. Coincidentally, the biggest driver of supply of treasuries is the Fed through QE/QT.\r\nA sudden Sharp increase signals low liquidity (like 17 September 2019): it implies banks don't have cash to lend to each other requiring ongoing Fed Liquidity injections to bring the rate down.\r\n(SOFR previously known as LIBOR; SOFR was chosen to be the successor to LIBOR for the global rate of lending for short term cash \"Overnight\" )", "created": 1660390896277, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-bbbac5d919756955", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:DRTSCILM] Liquidity expands in a global growth environment: \" A customer Alpha deposit $10,000 into the Bank. The Bank would then set aside 10% : $1,000 in vault and then loans out the rest of his money $9,000. Then another person B comes in asking for a car loan of $9,000, the Bank loans out $9,000 from Customer Alpha original Deposit to borrower B. Borrower B would pay the car seller C the money. Then car seller C would deposit the money into the Bank (its treated as a new deposit) and the whole process would be repeated all over just like customer Alpha Deposit. So the Money keeps getting redeposited and reloaned until the initial Deposit of $10,000 becomes $100,000 So the Euro Dollar Bank just created $90,000 out of thin air just by loaning out the money. And then the reverse process cause Liquidity to Contrats in Global growth environment: When Cutomer B defaults on the $9,000 then Bank only have $900 in the vault and the rest was loaned out. So Every Default is 10 times more than the amount the bank has kept in the vault to cover it ( because they just keep 10% in vault and loan out the other 90% ). This force banks to tighten and not issue new credit because they new the money to cover for the Default.\r\nSo in Expansion: $10,000 becomes $100,000 in new loans ( expanding money supply). And in contraction: $10,000 default cause a $100,000 contraction in money supply. \r\n\r\n\r\nThe 2 biggest components of Credit Market are: 1- Gov credit Market (controlled through interest rate policies, treasuries issuance, QE and QT and swaps). 2- private Equity credit market (can be seen through % of banks tightening, ice BOFA ccc interest rate spread)\r\n\r\nMoney and Liquidity comes either from the Fed or Commercial Banks. When When this metric goes up Commercial banks are tightening they draining liquidity from the system. when it comes down Commercial banks are easing they injecting liquidity into the markets.", "created": 1660348579742, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-96329243bff03d45", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:DPCREDIT] The Fed uses the discount rate as a ceiling for the federal funds rate. The discount rate is the interest rate that the Fed charges banks for loans through the discount window. Banks are unlikely to borrow from the banks at a rate higher than they can borrow from the FED. As a result, the discount rate acts as a ceiling on the federal funds rate.\r\nFor example, if the Fed sets the discount rate at 3%, banks are unlikely to borrow from the other banks at a rate higher than 3%. This means that the federal funds rate is unlikely to rise above 3%.\r\n\r\nThe discount rate/discount window, which represents the rate commercial banks can use to borrow directly from the Fed and is typically only used in times of liquidity stress, acts as the ceiling to the FFR range.\r\nWhen banks have liquidity problems they go to the feds as a last resort and obtain loans against collateral at a rate slightly above feds funds rate.", "created": 1660345923130, "pinned": false}
- `18:08:22` --- note 12080/12122 >>> MACRO/RISK-RELEVANT <<< ---

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-31b003d254a81bb1", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:US10Y] US10Y reflects current economic conditions and market future inflations expectations and market future growth expectation.\r\n\r\nwhat does us10y tell us about economic conditions\r\n\r\nThe US10Y, or the 10-year US Treasury yield, can provide important information about economic conditions. Generally, the yield on the 10-year Treasury note is a reflection of market expectations for future inflation, economic growth, and monetary policy.\r\n\r\nWhen the US10Y is rising, it often indicates that investors are becoming more optimistic about the economy's prospects. This can happen when investors expect inflation to rise, or when they believe that the Federal Reserve may need to raise interest rates in response to stronger economic growth or inflationary pressures.\r\n\r\nConversely, when the US10Y is falling, it often indicates that investors are becoming more pessimistic about the economy's prospects. This can happen when investors expect inflation to remain low or when they believe that economic growth may slow down.\r\n\r\nHowever, it's important to remember that the US10Y is just one indicator of economic conditions, and it should be considered along with other indicators such as GDP growth, unemployment rates, and consumer spending. Additionally, the yield on the 10-year Treasury note can be influenced by a variety of factors beyond just economic conditions, such as global market trends and geopolitical risks.\r\n\r\nIn the U.S., you would focus on the 10-year Treasury note: A rising yield is dollar bullish. A falling yield is dollar bearish. A decline in the 10-year yield indicates caution in the markets and the future of the global economy. \r\nConversely, gains in the 10 year yield signal confidence. A consistant decline in US10Y can signal risk of a financial crisis like in 2007 and 2020 Tnx kept dropping and the financial crisis happened in 08 and 2020.\r\n10 year yields shows Risk on/Risk Off and shows Top in Crypto Other than the times where the Feds are directly involved in the market by either easing or tightening. \r\nInterest rates are a significant factor in yields. Since they are the benchmark from which all other rates are derived, they have a direct impact on yields.", "created": 1660343295039, "pinned": false}

Shelter is Sticky bcs it changes infrequently since most prices are locked in place throughout a lease term thats why Data for shelter is gather EVERY 6 months (Panels report Data either in January and July or February and August which means the Data wont show up in BLS Data until Months Down the line) while Data for food and transportation is gathered every month or two which can cause Shelter inflation to show up in CPI as  rising still even when inflation start to come down in other sectors. According to the Dallas Fed changes in the Rental markets can precede changes in the shelter index by about a year bcs u have to wait for enough people to sign new leases or renew their leases for those price increases to actually show up and then u have to wait for the lag for it to be processed and show up on BLS Data.", "created": 1660342796301, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-fb4609e5b1e95cc4", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:USRR] Repo Rate: The cost of borrowing money overnight, it tracks how much banks and others pay for overnight loans using repurchase agreements.\r\n\r\nRepo Rate is funding source for treasuries, Repo Rate spiking signals liquidity plumbing issues. A sudden Sharp increase signals low liquidity (like 17 September 2019): it implies banks dont have cash to lend to each other requiring ongoing Fed Liquidity injections to bring the rate down.\r\nThe Repo rate spikes September 16,17 2019 have caused a big chaos in the financial world. That's bcs the repo market is a critical part of the financial system, it provides a lot of the grease that keeps the wheels spinning meaning it provides the cash the financial firms need to run their daily operations.", "created": 1660341902313, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-6492540b8be1a75f", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:AGG] ALWAYS FOLLOW THE MONEY: IF INVESTORS ARE INVESTING IN THE BOND MARKET THEY ARENT INVESTING IN THE STOCK MARKET.AND IF THE INVESTORS ARE INVESTING IN THE STOCK MARKET THEY ARENT INVESTING IN THE BOND MARKET.\r\n\r\nFixed income tends to lean itself toward macro more than equities thats more micro.\r\nBonds dumping especially sovereign bonds dumping is a major Warning signal that macro is deteriorating.\r\n\r\nAGG Bond Market strength is THE BEST tool to gauge stock Market health\r\n\r\nHow do Fed hiking interest rates shrinks global credit and global liquidity? when fed hike rates, treasury bond value drops. Since trasuries are used as a collateral for derivatives and global credit when their value drop that means the amount of derivatives and credit that can be obtained through them will also drops which shrinks global credit and liquidity. Same concept works in reverse, FED cutting rates will increase treasury bond value which will increase the amount of credit and liquidity that can be obtained by using them as collateral.", "created": 1660266070270, "pinned": false}

- `18:08:22`   {"id": "tv-004199d01e26ef16", "cat": "thesis", "text": "[TV:WTI] The WTI (West Texas Intermediate) oil price is an important indicator of global oil market dynamics and can provide insight into several different areas:\r\n\r\nSupply and demand: The price of oil is influenced by the balance of supply and demand. When demand for oil is high and supply is low, prices tend to rise, and vice versa. The WTI oil price, therefore, can tell us about the current state of supply and demand in the oil market.\r\n\r\nGlobal economic activity: The price of oil is also closely tied to global economic activity. When economic growth is strong, demand for oil tends to increase, driving up prices. Conversely, when economic growth slows down, demand for oil can decrease, leading to lower prices. Therefore, fluctuations in the WTI oil price can tell us about the overall health of the global economy.\r\n\r\nGeopolitical risks: Geopolitical risks such as conflicts, wars, and sanctions can also impact the WTI oil price. For example, tensions between major oil-producing nations or disruptions in key supply routes can lead to price spikes or drops. Therefore, the WTI oil price can provide an indication of the geopolitical risks affecting the oil market.\r\n\r\nEnergy policy: Government policies related to energy can also influence the WTI oil price. For example, changes in regulations or taxes on oil production or consumption can affect the price of oil. Additionally, shifts towards renewable energy sources can reduce demand for oil, leading to lower prices.\r\n\r\nOverall, the WTI oil price is a useful indicator of the global oil market and can provide insight into various economic, geopolitical, and environmental factors that affect the price of oil.\r\n\r\nThe drop in WTI (West Texas Intermediate) oil prices could be a warning sign about a number of different things:\r\n\r\nGlobal Economic slowdown: If the drop in oil prices is part of a broader economic slowdown, it could be a warning sign that demand for oil is decreasing, which in turn could signal a weakening economy.\r\n\r\nOversupply: A sudden drop in oil prices could also be a warning sign that there is too much supply in the market relative to demand. This could happen if there is a sudden increase in oil production or if geopolitical events disrupt the supply chain.\r\nThe WTI (West Texas Intermediate) oil price can provide some predictive value for a range of factors. STOCK PUMPS AND SPX HITS NEW HIGHS DURING THE LAST PHASE OF THE INVERSION BEFORE A MEGA CRASH AND DUMP OCCUR. \r\n\r\nTreasury yield curve is a short term bet on a long term rate.\r\nThe Eurodollar futures curve is a long term bet on a short term rate bcs EuroDollar future is like we're betting on what an overnight rate is going to be two years from now.\r\nYield Curve should NEVER be inverted. Yield Curves should be upward sloping just bcs of time value of money and uncertainty. If banks lend for a longer period of time or make further forward bet they should get a higher rate.\r\nIf yield Curves are inverted (downward sloping) thats bcs investors are betting that overnight rates are gonna be lower a year or two years from now.( and the only way for rates to be lower in the future if the economy gets into a recession and things get a lot worse).\r\nUS02y-US10y (know as the yield curve) predicts the future of markets and the Economy.
